observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned figure number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Figure 1 – Tourism receipts and GDP, Caribbean countries.”
observations.fit_rationale: The heading provides both the primary identifying title and the document-assigned identifier supported by existing fields.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays vertical bars by country with a numeric y-axis.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a bar chart.

observations.evidence: The chart title states “Tourism receipts / GDP (2001).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the represented indicator or measured concept.

observations.evidence: The represented measure is explicitly written as “Tourism receipts / GDP.”
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure and measure_type fields can represent that values are expressed as a ratio.

observations.evidence: The chart title includes “(2001).”
observations.fit_rationale: The year is directly represented by time_period, with annual temporal granularity supported by the year-only expression.

observations.evidence: The title says “Caribbean countries,” and the x-axis lists places such as Haiti, Barbados, Aruba, and Turks (*).
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields capture the Caribbean scope, named represented entities, and country-level reporting.

observations.evidence: The bars are organized along the x-axis by country or territory names such as Haiti, Jamaica, St Lucia, and Anguilla.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields capture the country-based grouping and its explicit labels.

observations.evidence: The source line states “Source: Authors’ calculations using Caribbean Tourism Organization data.”
observations.fit_rationale: The named Caribbean Tourism Organization data can be represented as the cited source from which the data originate.

observations.evidence: The source line states “Authors’ calculations using Caribbean Tourism Organization data.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can capture the named source or a specific method, but not the provenance fact that the displayed values are author-calculated from source data.

observations.metadata_concept: Interpretive footnote for exceptional plotted value
observations.evidence: The snapshot includes the note “(*) Actual ratio 2.27” next to the Turks label.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field captures explicit notes or caveats needed to interpret the figure.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Foreign informational lobbying can enhance tourism : evidence from the Caribbean.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language “english” with code “en.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier “10240515” and World Bank ID “090224b0828ca1d5.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields refer to the snapshot within the document or to projects, while source_document_title does not capture formal parent-document identifiers.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata contains the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/919351468011128387/pdf/WPS4834.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can record the parent document title but has no field for an access URL or retrieval locator for the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicit statement describing that represented values were derived, calculated, transformed, or otherwise produced from cited source data, including the responsible party when stated.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source captures the underlying cited data, analysis_method captures named analytical methods, and interpretive_note captures explanatory caveats, but none cleanly represents calculation provenance such as “Authors’ calculations using … data.”
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users distinguish directly reported source data from values computed or transformed by document authors, supporting interpretation, verification, and reuse.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional repository ID, publication number, or other persistent document identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for identifiers such as Figure 1 within the document, project_identifier is limited to projects or operations, and source_document_title does not preserve external document identifiers needed for retrieval or citation.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports reliable linking, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of snapshots through their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web access locator for the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document textually but does not provide a retrievable access location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, and cite the original document context for the extracted snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and internal figure identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Figure 1: Restrictiveness of Services Trade Policies by GDP per capita, 2005."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title and internal_identifier fields directly capture the figure caption and document-assigned figure number.

observations.evidence: The figure concerns "Restrictiveness of Services Trade Policies by GDP per capita" and the source document is titled "Services in Doha : what's on the table ?"
observations.fit_rationale: The broad trade-in-services domain and the concise analytical purpose of relating services trade policy restrictiveness to GDP per capita are covered by existing subject fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Axis-specific variable roles in a bivariate scatter plot
observations.evidence: The y-axis is labeled "Restrictiveness of services trade policy" and the x-axis is labeled "GDP per capita PPP, 2006."
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can record the measured concepts, but the schema has no field for preserving which variable is assigned to which axis without misusing category_dimension for a continuous x-axis variable.

observations.evidence: The figure shows country-labeled points plotted against two quantitative axes.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a scatter plot.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical overlay or fitted trend line
observations.evidence: A red downward-sloping line is drawn across the scatter plot in addition to the country points.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type can note the scatter plot and analysis_method applies only when a method is stated, but neither cleanly captures the explicit presence of an analytical trend-line overlay.

observations.evidence: The title includes "2005," the x-axis includes "2006," and the note states "GDP per capita, PPP is in constant 2005 international USD."
observations.fit_rationale: The represented years, monetary unit, and constant-price qualification can be captured using existing temporal, measurement, and interpretive-note fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Country geographic scope, entities, and granularity
observations.evidence: The plotted labels are country abbreviations and the note states "There are in total 56 countries."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields can represent a multi-country scope, named country entities, and country-level reporting granularity.

observations.evidence: The note states that the 56 countries include "32 developing and 24 are OECD countries."
observations.fit_rationale: Because the developing and OECD breakdown is presented as an explanatory sample note rather than an encoded category or comparator, interpretive_note can preserve it without material semantic loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Sectoral coverage of the represented services data
observations.evidence: The note states that the covered sectors are "financial, telecommunications, retailing, maritime, air passenger transport, and professional services."
observations.fit_rationale: subject fields can indicate a services-trade topic, but the schema lacks a structured field for the specific sectors covered when they are not visible categories in the chart.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data source and collection context
observations.evidence: The source-document abstract says the paper presents "the results of the first survey of applied trade policies in the major services sectors of 56 industrial and developing countries."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_source and data_collection_method fields can capture the explicitly stated survey basis for the represented services trade policy data.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document title and snapshot language
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Services in Doha : what's on the table ?" and the language is listed as "english."
observations.fit_rationale: The parent document title and language are directly covered by existing provenance and language fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides identifiers such as World Bank D&R "10455617" and a URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/707781468337263912/pdf/WPS4903.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within a document, but no existing field captures a parent-document identifier or URL for retrieval and verification.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit assignment of a represented variable or indicator to a visualization axis or equivalent positional role, such as x-axis or y-axis.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name records represented concepts but loses axis role, while category_dimension is intended for grouping or classification and would distort a continuous numeric axis variable.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Preserves the semantic structure of bivariate charts for search, interpretation, and analytical reuse without requiring chart reconstruction.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly visible analytical layer added to a visualization, such as a fitted trend line, reference line, confidence band, or smoothing curve.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type captures the primary chart form and analysis_method requires a stated method, but neither records the presence of an interpretive overlay when the method is not specified.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports discovery and interpretation of charts that present modeled or summarized relationships in addition to raw plotted values.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The specific economic, policy, service, industry, or thematic sectors explicitly covered by the represented data when they define the scope of the snapshot rather than categorical encodings.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: subject_domain and subject_summary are broad or prose-oriented, and category_labels apply to explicit category dimensions rather than sectors listed only as coverage scope.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables structured retrieval and comparison of snapshots by covered sectors, especially when the sectors are not chart axes, rows, columns, or legend categories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A document-level identifier, persistent identifier, or URL that enables retrieval or verification of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name only, while internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot's within-document reference and cannot represent parent-document retrieval metadata.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance verification, citation, and retrieval of the original document from which a snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and internal figure identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Figure 1: Restrictiveness of Services Trade Policies by GDP per capita, 2005."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title and internal_identifier fields directly capture the figure caption and document-assigned figure number.

observations.evidence: The figure concerns "Restrictiveness of Services Trade Policies by GDP per capita" and the source document is titled "Services in Doha : what's on the table ?"
observations.fit_rationale: The broad trade-in-services domain and the concise analytical purpose of relating services trade policy restrictiveness to GDP per capita are covered by existing subject fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Axis-specific variable roles in a bivariate scatter plot
observations.evidence: The y-axis is labeled "Restrictiveness of services trade policy" and the x-axis is labeled "GDP per capita PPP, 2006."
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can record the measured concepts, but the schema has no field for preserving which variable is assigned to which axis without misusing category_dimension for a continuous x-axis variable.

observations.evidence: The figure shows country-labeled points plotted against two quantitative axes.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a scatter plot.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical overlay or fitted trend line
observations.evidence: A red downward-sloping line is drawn across the scatter plot in addition to the country points.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type can note the scatter plot and analysis_method applies only when a method is stated, but neither cleanly captures the explicit presence of an analytical trend-line overlay.

observations.evidence: The title includes "2005," the x-axis includes "2006," and the note states "GDP per capita, PPP is in constant 2005 international USD."
observations.fit_rationale: The represented years, monetary unit, and constant-price qualification can be captured using existing temporal, measurement, and interpretive-note fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Country geographic scope, entities, and granularity
observations.evidence: The plotted labels are country abbreviations and the note states "There are in total 56 countries."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields can represent a multi-country scope, named country entities, and country-level reporting granularity.

observations.evidence: The note states that the 56 countries include "32 developing and 24 are OECD countries."
observations.fit_rationale: Because the developing and OECD breakdown is presented as an explanatory sample note rather than an encoded category or comparator, interpretive_note can preserve it without material semantic loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Sectoral coverage of the represented services data
observations.evidence: The note states that the covered sectors are "financial, telecommunications, retailing, maritime, air passenger transport, and professional services."
observations.fit_rationale: subject fields can indicate a services-trade topic, but the schema lacks a structured field for the specific sectors covered when they are not visible categories in the chart.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data source and collection context
observations.evidence: The source-document abstract says the paper presents "the results of the first survey of applied trade policies in the major services sectors of 56 industrial and developing countries."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_source and data_collection_method fields can capture the explicitly stated survey basis for the represented services trade policy data.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document title and snapshot language
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Services in Doha : what's on the table ?" and the language is listed as "english."
observations.fit_rationale: The parent document title and language are directly covered by existing provenance and language fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides identifiers such as World Bank D&R "10455617" and a URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/707781468337263912/pdf/WPS4903.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within a document, but no existing field captures a parent-document identifier or URL for retrieval and verification.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit assignment of a represented variable or indicator to a visualization axis or equivalent positional role, such as x-axis or y-axis.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name records represented concepts but loses axis role, while category_dimension is intended for grouping or classification and would distort a continuous numeric axis variable.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Preserves the semantic structure of bivariate charts for search, interpretation, and analytical reuse without requiring chart reconstruction.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly visible analytical layer added to a visualization, such as a fitted trend line, reference line, confidence band, or smoothing curve.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type captures the primary chart form and analysis_method requires a stated method, but neither records the presence of an interpretive overlay when the method is not specified.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports discovery and interpretation of charts that present modeled or summarized relationships in addition to raw plotted values.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The specific economic, policy, service, industry, or thematic sectors explicitly covered by the represented data when they define the scope of the snapshot rather than categorical encodings.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: subject_domain and subject_summary are broad or prose-oriented, and category_labels apply to explicit category dimensions rather than sectors listed only as coverage scope.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables structured retrieval and comparison of snapshots by covered sectors, especially when the sectors are not chart axes, rows, columns, or legend categories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A document-level identifier, persistent identifier, or URL that enables retrieval or verification of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name only, while internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot's within-document reference and cannot represent parent-document retrieval metadata.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance verification, citation, and retrieval of the original document from which a snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot caption begins with “Figure 3:” before the descriptive title.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing internal_identifier field directly captures a document-assigned figure number used to reference the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The caption reads “Figure 3: Top ten Ethiopian products in terms of lost tariff revenue.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the primary caption, while subject_summary can summarize the analytical subject if needed.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays vertical bars with an axis and value labels.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a bar chart.

observations.evidence: The title refers to “lost tariff revenue” and the y-axis is labeled “percentage change.”
observations.fit_rationale: The represented measure, percentage unit, percentage-change form, and financial-revenue concept are expressible with existing measurement fields.

observations.evidence: The x-axis is labeled “hscodes,” and the table below lists “hscode” and “Product” entries such as 72142000 and “IRON/STEEL BARS & RODS.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields can capture the product-code dimension and explicit code or product labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Classification or coding system for categories
observations.evidence: The category axis and table explicitly use “hscodes” with eight-digit product codes.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing category fields can store the codes as labels but do not separately represent that the categories belong to a named classification system.

observations.evidence: The title describes “Ethiopian products.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent Ethiopia as the geographic context explicitly named in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The caption states “Top ten Ethiopian products in terms of lost tariff revenue.”
observations.fit_rationale: The title and summary can preserve the phrase, but no existing field structurally captures that the displayed categories are selected and ranked by a stated criterion.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Assessing the adjustment implications of trade policy changes using TRIST (tariff reform impact simulation tool).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language “english.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document retrieval identifier or locator
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides idno “11225119,” World Bank identifiers, and the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/804891468339572958/pdf/WPS5045.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can name the parent document but has no field for a source-document identifier or URL needed for retrieval and verification.

observations.evidence: The source-document title says the paper assesses trade policy changes “using TRIST (tariff reform impact simulation tool).”
observations.fit_rationale: The evidence identifies the document’s analytical tool, but it does not explicitly state that this specific figure was produced by TRIST.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The named taxonomy, coding scheme, or classification system used to define categorical labels represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels can store the dimension and labels, but they do not separately encode that labels come from a reusable code system such as HS codes.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, harmonization, and interpretation of snapshots that use standardized classifications such as product, industry, occupation, disease, or geographic codes.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated basis by which represented entities are ranked, filtered, or selected for display in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: title and subject_summary can include the wording, but they do not provide a structured way to identify that the snapshot shows a top-N subset selected by lost tariff revenue.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to distinguish ranked or filtered snapshots from complete distributions and to search for top-N, bottom-N, or criterion-selected displays.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An identifier, accession number, persistent link, or URL that locates the parent document from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support storing a retrieval or verification locator such as a document ID or URL.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, verification, deduplication, and retrieval of the parent document associated with a snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: Unit_of_measure captures percent and measure_type captures the values as shares or percentages.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays two side-by-side vertical stacked bar charts by year.
observations.fit_rationale: Visualization_type adequately captures the primary encoding as stacked bar charts.

observations.evidence: The source note states "Source: COMTRADE and author's computations based on UNCTAD (1985) methodology, SITC1 4 digit."
observations.fit_rationale: Data_source directly captures COMTRADE as the cited source from which the represented data originate.

observations.evidence: The source note says the results are "author's computations based on UNCTAD (1985) methodology, SITC1 4 digit."
observations.fit_rationale: Analysis_method captures the stated UNCTAD methodology and interpretive_note can preserve the SITC1 four-digit methodological detail.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Argentina : trade patterns and challenges ahead."
observations.fit_rationale: Source_document_title directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R "11867889" and World Bank ID "090224b0828b51c2."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields capture the parent document title, snapshot identifier, or project identifier but not a formal identifier for the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/277971468199128775/pdf/WPS5221.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields identify the parent document title or underlying data source but do not represent a retrieval link for the parent document used to verify or access the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the data snapshot, such as an institutional repository identifier, report number, or persistent document ID.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document title, internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot’s in-document figure or table reference, and project_identifier is limited to associated projects or operations.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports reliable retrieval, citation, deduplication, and verification of snapshots extracted from institutional document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web location where the parent document containing the data snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not provide an access location, and data_source refers to the origin of the represented data rather than the location of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the source document, verify snapshot provenance, and link extracted snapshots back to their institutional publication context.

observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A repository-assigned, persistent, or formal identifier for the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title is not unique, internal_identifier is defined for a snapshot's within-document label, and project_identifier applies only to associated projects or operations.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports precise retrieval, citation, deduplication, and verification of snapshots against their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or URI where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The existing schema records the source document title but lacks a retrieval locator for the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the original document, verify extraction context, and audit snapshot provenance.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly stated cutoff date or period through which source events, announcements, records, or inputs were included in the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the period represented by the data, and interpretive_note is an unstructured catchall that does not distinguish a source-inclusion cutoff from ordinary caveats.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps compare data vintage, interpret coverage limits, and retrieve snapshots based on the recency or cutoff of included evidence.

observations.evidence: The snapshot has a top-level heading reading "Wheat."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Panel-level headings in a composite figure
observations.evidence: The figure contains separate headings "Monthly Price" and "Monthly Returns (% change) and KL (2000) test detected breaks."
observations.fit_rationale: The panel_title field is designed for explicitly present headings of individual panels within a multi-panel snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Measured concepts shown in the panels
observations.evidence: The panel headings identify "Monthly Price" and "Monthly Returns (% change)" as represented quantities.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields can capture the indicators, percentage-change unit, and statistical form without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal range and monthly reporting resolution
observations.evidence: The x-axes show date labels from Jan-1784 through Jan-2008, and both panel headings use the term "Monthly."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has dedicated fields for both the represented date range and the monthly temporal resolution.

observations.evidence: The snapshot consists of two time-series plots with line-based marks across dates.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the snapshot as a line chart or multi-panel time-series chart.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical test used to detect breaks
observations.evidence: The lower panel title explicitly states "KL (2000) test detected breaks."
observations.fit_rationale: The analysis_method field explicitly covers analytical or statistical methods used to produce reported results.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Are commodity prices more volatile now ? a long-run perspective."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot and source context
observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language name "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language evidenced in the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic subject of commodity price volatility
observations.evidence: The source-document abstract states that the paper examines commodity price volatility using a monthly panel dataset on individual commodity prices.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can capture the broad macroeconomic commodity-prices domain and the snapshot's analytical subject.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying dataset represented by the snapshot
observations.evidence: The source-document abstract describes "a newly compiled monthly panel dataset on 45 individual commodity prices from the end of the 18th century until today."
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field can represent the cited dataset from which the snapshot's data originate.

observations.evidence: The top-level snapshot heading identifies the represented commodity as "Wheat."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can store the word or describe it in prose, but they conflate the commodity entity with a title, category label, or measured variable.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "12916918" and World Bank ID "090224b0828aef59."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field identifies the parent document by name but cannot preserve formal document identifiers needed for verification and retrieval.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/538551468313809476/pdf/WPS5460.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field contextualizes the parent document but cannot represent a retrieval locator for the source file.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Named non-geographic, non-human entity, item, product, commodity, asset, institution, or other object that the snapshot's represented data are primarily about, distinct from the measured variable and from geographic or population entities.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: title preserves the visible heading but not its semantic role, subject_summary is unstructured prose, category_labels require a category dimension, and variable_name is better reserved for measured concepts such as price or returns.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables structured retrieval and grouping of snapshots by commodities, products, assets, institutions, or other represented entities even when only one such entity is shown.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, including repository, institutional, DOI, or other document-level identifiers when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document by name but does not capture stable repository or institutional identifiers, while internal_identifier is defined for document-assigned snapshot references rather than parent-document identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, verification, citation, and retrieval of snapshots by linking them to stable parent-document records.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided in source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title provides descriptive context but cannot function as a direct retrieval link or locator for the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, and audit the source document associated with an extracted data snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.

observations.metadata_concept: Figure title and document-assigned figure number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Figure 14 The expenditure poverty incidence and the income poverty incidence of provinces.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture both the caption text as the snapshot title and “Figure 14” as the document-assigned identifier.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Poverty and inequality maps for rural Vietnam: an application of small area estimation.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot contains two side-by-side scatter plots under one shared figure title.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type can record scatter plot and panel_title can capture explicit panel headings, but neither captures the number or presence of untitled panels in a composite figure.

observations.metadata_concept: Axis-specific variable roles in a scatter plot
observations.evidence: Both panels label the x-axis “The income poverty incidence” and the y-axis “The expenditure poverty incidence.”
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can list the measured concepts but does not preserve their x-axis and y-axis roles, while category_dimension is not appropriate for measured axis variables.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title refers to expenditure and income poverty incidence, and the document title refers to poverty and inequality maps for rural Vietnam.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent poverty and inequality as the domain, summarize the comparison of poverty incidence measures, and name the poverty incidence variables.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and administrative reporting level
observations.evidence: The snapshot title says the incidence measures are “of provinces,” and the document metadata lists Vietnam as the reference country.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Vietnam as the scope and provinces as the reporting granularity without requiring named province labels.

observations.evidence: The document title specifies “rural Vietnam,” and the abstract discusses province and district level poverty estimates for rural Vietnam.
observations.fit_rationale: population_group can capture the rural population context while geographic_scope captures Vietnam as the represented area.

observations.metadata_concept: Data sources and represented data year
observations.evidence: The snapshot source note states “Authors’ estimation from VHLSS 2006 and ARFC 2006,” and the abstract states estimates are for the year 2006.
observations.fit_rationale: data_source can capture VHLSS 2006 and ARFC 2006, and time_period can capture the represented year 2006.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical method used to produce estimates
observations.evidence: The document title describes the paper as “an application of small area estimation.”
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method directly captures small area estimation as the stated analytical method.

observations.evidence: Each scatter plot includes a diagonal red line running from the lower-left toward the upper-right of the plotting area.
observations.fit_rationale: comparison_group can represent benchmarks in general, but it conflates a visual reference line with a comparator group, entity, cohort, or scenario.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document URL for retrieval
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/451271468316151758/pdf/WPS5443.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but no existing field captures a locator needed to retrieve or verify the source document.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier “13148967” and World Bank ID “090224b0828b4f62.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and internal_identifier refers to the snapshot, but no field captures formal identifiers assigned to the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The number of distinct panels or subplots that compose a multi-panel data snapshot, when explicitly visible or labeled.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type records the primary chart form and panel_title records explicit panel headings, but neither represents that a snapshot is composed of multiple untitled panels.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports indexing, extraction planning, and interpretation of composite figures where each panel may require separate analysis.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A measured concept or variable explicitly assigned to a named chart axis, including the axis role where available.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name loses the semantic distinction between x-axis and y-axis variables, and category_dimension is designed for grouping dimensions rather than measured variables plotted on axes.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves retrieval and reuse of charts by preserving how variables are encoded and compared within scatter plots and other axis-based visualizations.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly shown or labeled line or curve used as a benchmark or interpretive reference within a chart.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: comparison_group covers comparator groups, entities, cohorts, scenarios, or benchmarks but does not cleanly represent a visual reference line embedded in a chart.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users identify charts that include visual benchmarks or interpretive guides that affect how plotted values should be read.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent locator for the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrievable locator for verification or access.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval, provenance verification, and linking from the snapshot metadata record back to the original source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document by a repository, publisher, DOI registry, or other document authority.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for identifiers assigned to the snapshot within a document, while source_document_title does not capture formal parent-document identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports document-level disambiguation, provenance tracking, deduplication, and reliable linkage between snapshots and source documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Figure title and document-assigned figure number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Figure 14 The expenditure poverty incidence and the income poverty incidence of provinces.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture both the caption text as the snapshot title and “Figure 14” as the document-assigned identifier.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Poverty and inequality maps for rural Vietnam: an application of small area estimation.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot contains two side-by-side scatter plots under one shared figure title.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type can record scatter plot and panel_title can capture explicit panel headings, but neither captures the number or presence of untitled panels in a composite figure.

observations.metadata_concept: Axis-specific variable roles in a scatter plot
observations.evidence: Both panels label the x-axis “The income poverty incidence” and the y-axis “The expenditure poverty incidence.”
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can list the measured concepts but does not preserve their x-axis and y-axis roles, while category_dimension is not appropriate for measured axis variables.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title refers to expenditure and income poverty incidence, and the document title refers to poverty and inequality maps for rural Vietnam.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent poverty and inequality as the domain, summarize the comparison of poverty incidence measures, and name the poverty incidence variables.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and administrative reporting level
observations.evidence: The snapshot title says the incidence measures are “of provinces,” and the document metadata lists Vietnam as the reference country.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Vietnam as the scope and provinces as the reporting granularity without requiring named province labels.

observations.evidence: The document title specifies “rural Vietnam,” and the abstract discusses province and district level poverty estimates for rural Vietnam.
observations.fit_rationale: population_group can capture the rural population context while geographic_scope captures Vietnam as the represented area.

observations.metadata_concept: Data sources and represented data year
observations.evidence: The snapshot source note states “Authors’ estimation from VHLSS 2006 and ARFC 2006,” and the abstract states estimates are for the year 2006.
observations.fit_rationale: data_source can capture VHLSS 2006 and ARFC 2006, and time_period can capture the represented year 2006.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical method used to produce estimates
observations.evidence: The document title describes the paper as “an application of small area estimation.”
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method directly captures small area estimation as the stated analytical method.

observations.evidence: Each scatter plot includes a diagonal red line running from the lower-left toward the upper-right of the plotting area.
observations.fit_rationale: comparison_group can represent benchmarks in general, but it conflates a visual reference line with a comparator group, entity, cohort, or scenario.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document URL for retrieval
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/451271468316151758/pdf/WPS5443.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but no existing field captures a locator needed to retrieve or verify the source document.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier “13148967” and World Bank ID “090224b0828b4f62.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and internal_identifier refers to the snapshot, but no field captures formal identifiers assigned to the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The number of distinct panels or subplots that compose a multi-panel data snapshot, when explicitly visible or labeled.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type records the primary chart form and panel_title records explicit panel headings, but neither represents that a snapshot is composed of multiple untitled panels.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports indexing, extraction planning, and interpretation of composite figures where each panel may require separate analysis.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A measured concept or variable explicitly assigned to a named chart axis, including the axis role where available.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name loses the semantic distinction between x-axis and y-axis variables, and category_dimension is designed for grouping dimensions rather than measured variables plotted on axes.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves retrieval and reuse of charts by preserving how variables are encoded and compared within scatter plots and other axis-based visualizations.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly shown or labeled line or curve used as a benchmark or interpretive reference within a chart.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: comparison_group covers comparator groups, entities, cohorts, scenarios, or benchmarks but does not cleanly represent a visual reference line embedded in a chart.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users identify charts that include visual benchmarks or interpretive guides that affect how plotted values should be read.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent locator for the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrievable locator for verification or access.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval, provenance verification, and linking from the snapshot metadata record back to the original source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document by a repository, publisher, DOI registry, or other document authority.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for identifiers assigned to the snapshot within a document, while source_document_title does not capture formal parent-document identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports document-level disambiguation, provenance tracking, deduplication, and reliable linkage between snapshots and source documents.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to verify the snapshot against the original document and retrieve contextual source material.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The legend lists “Licences,” “Prohibitions-Quotas,” and “Technical Barriers.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields capture both the classification dimension and its explicit labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal coverage and annual comparison points
observations.evidence: The x-axis repeats the years “2001” and “2010” for each country group.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields capture the represented years and annual granularity, while category_dimension can represent year as an organizing dimension.

observations.evidence: The title names the “MENA region,” and the x-axis groups are Egypt, Lebanon, Tunisia, and Morocco.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields capture the regional scope, named countries, and country-level granularity.

observations.evidence: The chart pairs 2001 and 2010 within each country under a title about the “Shifting nature” of measures.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing comparison_group field can represent the intended comparison between the two years.

observations.metadata_concept: Cited data or publication source for represented data
observations.evidence: The bottom note reads “Source: Gourdon 2011.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_source field explicitly covers cited publications or sources from which the represented data originate.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document title and language
observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Trade integration as a way forward for the Arab world : a regional agenda,” and the language is listed as “english.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title and language fields cover the parent document title and language context for the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes idno “13840629” and identifiers such as World Bank D&R “13840629” and World Bank ID “090224b0828b6191.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document only by name, while internal_identifier is reserved for the snapshot’s identifier within the document rather than a parent-document identifier.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/377151468299191607/pdf/WPS5581.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title helps identify the parent document but does not capture a retrievable location for verification or reuse.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published as “2010-07-01.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period is defined for the period represented by the data, so using it for the parent document publication date would conflate provenance timing with data coverage.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from the snapshot’s internal figure or table identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document name, and internal_identifier is defined for identifiers used to reference the snapshot within the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports reliable citation, deduplication, retrieval, and verification of snapshots by linking them to formally identified parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or URI where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or retrieved.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: No existing field captures a retrievable location for the parent document, while source_document_title only names the document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to verify the snapshot against the original document and retrieve contextual source material.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or release date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the represented data period and would distort provenance semantics if used for a document publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, provenance tracking, version assessment, and temporal organization of snapshots by parent-document publication context.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned chart identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Chart 19. Annual change of nonperforming loans (NPLs) and provisions in the pre-crisis, crisis, and post-crisis periods.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the descriptive heading and internal_identifier captures “Chart 19” without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The title and legend identify nonperforming loans, provisions, and the Provisions/NPLs ratio as the represented measures.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent the specific variables, summarize the analytical subject, and classify the domain as finance or banking.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal coverage and annual reporting granularity
observations.evidence: The x-axis lists years from 2003 through 2010 and the title refers to annual change.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields capture both the represented date range and the annual resolution.

observations.evidence: The title states that the annual changes are shown “in the pre-crisis, crisis, and post-crisis periods.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category and comparison fields can represent the period-based grouping or comparative framing without requiring a new field.

observations.metadata_concept: Multiple measurement units and axis-specific interpretation by series
observations.evidence: The chart has a left axis labeled “In millions of denars,” a right axis labeled in percentages, and legend entries indicating NPLs, Provisions, and Provisions/NPLs with lhs/rhs notation.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can list variables, units, currency, and measure types, but they do not preserve which unit or axis applies to each series in a multi-measure chart.

observations.metadata_concept: Visualization form as a combined bar-and-line chart
observations.evidence: The snapshot displays blue and red vertical bars for two series and a green line for the Provisions/NPLs series.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can describe the mixed bar-and-line chart sufficiently for discovery and interpretation.

observations.evidence: The snapshot includes the note “Source: NBRM.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field directly captures the cited source from which the represented data originate.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document title contextualizing the snapshot
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Macroprudential regulation of credit booms and busts : the experience of the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context of the snapshot from the parent document
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists ref_country as “North Macedonia” and the document title refers to the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture the explicitly evidenced country context relevant to interpreting the banking-system chart.

observations.evidence: The chart title, labels, legend, and source note are written in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Association between each explicitly labeled data series or variable and the unit of measure, currency, measure type, or axis needed to interpret that series when a snapshot contains multiple measurement contexts.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure, currency, measure_type, and variable_name can record values independently but cannot express that one series is interpreted in millions of denars while another is interpreted as a percentage or tied to a different axis.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Preserves interpretive context for multi-measure charts and supports accurate search, extraction review, and downstream reuse without conflating units across series.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult
