CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot caption begins with the explicit label "Figure 1:".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing internal_identifier field directly represents a document-assigned figure label.

observations.evidence: The caption states "Duration Between Liberalization and a Crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary caption identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The subtitle limits the figure to "countries which had banking crisis following liberalization".
observations.fit_rationale: Subject_summary can mention this restriction, geographic_granularity can capture country level, and population_group is human-focused, but none structurally captures the non-human analysis universe and inclusion criterion.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title refers to liberalization and crisis, and the source document title is "Transparency, liberalization, and banking crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields can represent the broad financial-sector topic and analytical focus without material loss.

observations.evidence: The x-axis is labeled "Years after Liberalization".
observations.fit_rationale: The intervention_type field explicitly includes policies and can represent liberalization as the policy event shown in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The x-axis reports "Years after Liberalization" with categories 1 through 5.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can store the axis label, labels, unit, and policy event separately, but they do not capture that time is measured relative to a specific anchor event rather than as a calendar period.

observations.evidence: The y-axis is labeled "Number of Crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent the measured concept as crises, the statistical form as a count, and the unit as crises.

observations.evidence: The figure displays vertical bars for the year-after-liberalization categories.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a bar chart.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives the title "Transparency, liberalization, and banking crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language as "english" with code "en".
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/429731468739157817/pdf/multi-page.pdf".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for an explicit retrieval URL needed to verify or retrieve the exact source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The set of entities, observations, or cases included in the snapshot, including explicitly stated inclusion criteria or sample restrictions.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: subject_summary can only describe the restriction narratively, population_group is limited to human groups, and geographic_granularity captures only the spatial level rather than the inclusion criterion.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables filtering, comparison, and reuse of snapshots by the population or case universe actually represented, especially for non-human units such as countries, firms, schools, or events.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The event or condition used as the anchor point for a relative temporal measure represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is for calendar periods, temporal_granularity is for reporting resolution, category_dimension stores the axis concept, and intervention_type stores the event itself but not its role as the temporal anchor.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and interpretation of event-study, duration, and before-or-after snapshots where time is measured relative to a policy, crisis, intervention, or other event.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or URI for retrieving the parent document that contains the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a machine-actionable locator for retrieval or verification of the exact source.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, auditability, and retrieval of the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

observations.evidence: The snapshot caption begins with the explicit label "Figure 1:".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing internal_identifier field directly represents a document-assigned figure label.

observations.evidence: The caption states "Duration Between Liberalization and a Crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary caption identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The subtitle limits the figure to "countries which had banking crisis following liberalization".
observations.fit_rationale: Subject_summary can mention this restriction, geographic_granularity can capture country level, and population_group is human-focused, but none structurally captures the non-human analysis universe and inclusion criterion.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title refers to liberalization and crisis, and the source document title is "Transparency, liberalization, and banking crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields can represent the broad financial-sector topic and analytical focus without material loss.

observations.evidence: The x-axis is labeled "Years after Liberalization".
observations.fit_rationale: The intervention_type field explicitly includes policies and can represent liberalization as the policy event shown in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The x-axis reports "Years after Liberalization" with categories 1 through 5.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can store the axis label, labels, unit, and policy event separately, but they do not capture that time is measured relative to a specific anchor event rather than as a calendar period.

observations.evidence: The y-axis is labeled "Number of Crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent the measured concept as crises, the statistical form as a count, and the unit as crises.

observations.evidence: The figure displays vertical bars for the year-after-liberalization categories.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a bar chart.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives the title "Transparency, liberalization, and banking crisis".
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language as "english" with code "en".
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/429731468739157817/pdf/multi-page.pdf".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for an explicit retrieval URL needed to verify or retrieve the exact source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The URL or persistent web location where the parent source document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support direct retrieval or verification of the document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables snapshot users to locate, cite, audit, and retrieve the source document associated with a data snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional record number, catalog identifier, or external document identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot's in-document label, while project_identifier is limited to associated projects or operations and does not capture parent document identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, provenance tracking, document lookup, and reliable linkage between snapshots and their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, group, or organization credited as author or creator of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source captures the origin of the represented data and source_document_title captures only the document title, so using either for document authorship would conflate distinct provenance roles.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, attribution, provenance review, and interpretation of snapshots in relation to the parent document's credited creators.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data, and no existing field records when the parent document was published.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, version context, retrieval filtering, and avoiding confusion between represented data dates and document publication dates.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/117251468743744606/pdf/multi-page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification URL for the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "437802" and World Bank ID "090224b082b05769."
observations.fit_rationale: The internal_identifier field refers to the snapshot's document-assigned label, while no existing field captures identifiers assigned to the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the author full name as "Jadresic,Alejandro."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title and data source but has no field for the creator or author of the parent document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists "date_published": "2010-07-01" and "date_created": "2000-04-30."
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the represented data period, not publication or creation dates of the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The URL or persistent web location where the parent source document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support direct retrieval or verification of the document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables snapshot users to locate, cite, audit, and retrieve the source document associated with a data snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional record number, catalog identifier, or external document identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot's in-document label, while project_identifier is limited to associated projects or operations and does not capture parent document identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, provenance tracking, document lookup, and reliable linkage between snapshots and their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, group, or organization credited as author or creator of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source captures the origin of the represented data and source_document_title captures only the document title, so using either for document authorship would conflate distinct provenance roles.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, attribution, provenance review, and interpretation of snapshots in relation to the parent document's credited creators.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data, and no existing field records when the parent document was published.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, version context, retrieval filtering, and avoiding confusion between represented data dates and document publication dates.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

ValidationObservation.description:

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot caption and document-assigned figure number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Figure 3: Geographical spread of conflict over time."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the caption text and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned label "Figure 3."

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject and measured conflict concept
observations.evidence: The snapshot states "Geographical spread of conflict over time" and "Districts reporting more than 100 deaths since 1996."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent the conflict-related analytical subject through subject_summary, variable_name, and subject_domain without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Explicit threshold rule defining highlighted map areas
observations.evidence: The subtitle specifies the displayed areas as "Districts reporting more than 100 deaths since 1996."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can mention the threshold only by embedding it in a variable, label, or note, but none directly captures a classification or inclusion rule used to define displayed entities.

observations.evidence: The map panels are labeled 2001, 2002, 2003, and 2004, and the subtitle includes "since 1996."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema covers the represented years, the annual temporal resolution, and the individual year labels used as panel titles.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and district-level spatial granularity
observations.evidence: The subtitle refers to "Districts," and the source-document metadata lists ref_country as "Nepal."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can capture Nepal as the geographic scope and districts as the geographic reporting level.

observations.evidence: The snapshot shows four separate map panels labeled by year.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema represents the primary visualization as a map and the year labels as panel titles.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Poverty, social divisions, and conflict in Nepal."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot and source document
observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language name "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language evidenced by the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Source-document locator or formal identifier for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R "7581269" and URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/871141468323682873/pdf/wps4228.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a source-document identifier or locator needed to retrieve or verify the snapshot source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicit rule, threshold, or condition used to classify, filter, or determine which entities or observations are displayed or highlighted in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name, category_labels, and interpretive_note can only store the threshold as embedded text and do not distinguish the rule that defines the displayed class from the measured concept or labels.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation and reuse of maps, charts, and tables where displayed entities are selected or highlighted based on an explicit criterion.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier, accession number, persistent identifier, or URL used to locate or verify the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable or verifiable locator such as a repository identifier or URL.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves retrieval, provenance verification, citation, and deduplication of snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Figure 10. Estimated country-specific brand effects in coffee and cocoa production.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the caption or heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The caption begins with the identifier “Figure 10.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing internal_identifier field is defined for document-assigned references such as figure numbers.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays vertical bars for countries against a coefficient axis.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field covers identifying the artifact as a bar chart.

observations.evidence: The title states “Estimated country-specific brand effects” and the y-axis is labeled “Coefficient.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the estimated brand effects and measure_type can represent that values are expressed as coefficients.

observations.evidence: The x-axis lists country names including Côte d’Ivoire, Tanzania, Togo, Kenya, South Africa, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields cover country as the grouping dimension and its explicit labels, while geographic_entities covers the named places.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic coverage represented in the snapshot
observations.evidence: The chart includes multiple African countries and also Brazil, Colombia, and Peru as country labels.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent the named countries and the country-level granularity without needing a new field.

observations.evidence: The title refers to “coffee and cocoa production,” and the source-document title refers to “agricultural growth and infrastructure development.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields cover the agricultural production topic and its analytical purpose.

observations.evidence: The chart text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language as “english.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “what is missing between agricultural growth and infrastructure development ? cases of coffee and dairy in Africa.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier “8772744,” World Bank ID “090224b0828abd3d,” and number “WPS4411.”
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures a stable identifier for the parent document, and internal_identifier and project_identifier refer to different entities.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/450141468003606079/pdf/wps4411.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures the retrievable location of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives the document type as “Policy Research Working Paper.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not capture its publication or document class, which contextualizes retrieval and interpretation.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent source document that contains the data snapshot, such as an institutional record number, report number, DOI, or catalog identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title is not a stable identifier, internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within the document, and project_identifier refers to projects or operations rather than parent documents.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports verification, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of the exact source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web location for accessing the parent source document that contains the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable access location or link to the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, audit, and verify the source document associated with a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or document class of the parent source document containing the data snapshot, such as working paper, annual report, evaluation report, or policy brief.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document by name but omits the document class, and no existing field represents the parent document’s publication type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, organization, interpretation, and citation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document they come from.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports verification, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of the exact source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web location for accessing the parent source document that contains the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable access location or link to the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, audit, and verify the source document associated with a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or document class of the parent source document containing the data snapshot, such as working paper, annual report, evaluation report, or policy brief.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document by name but omits the document class, and no existing field represents the parent document’s publication type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, organization, interpretation, and citation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document they come from.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and internal table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table A - 3: Traders' Perceptions of Import Documentations Associated with Customs Valuation, Rules of Origins and Standards compliance."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the full heading and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned table number without semantic loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic subject domain of trade facilitation and regional integration
observations.evidence: The source document themes are "regional integration" and "trade facilitation and market access," and the table concerns import documentation, customs valuation, rules of origin, and standards compliance.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields adequately represent the broad policy area and analytical purpose of the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary measured concepts are traders' perceptions of import documentation problems and compliance costs
observations.evidence: The table presents questions on customs valuation, rules of origin documentation, product standards compliance, and costs of compliance with technical requirements.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field covers the indicators or measured concepts represented in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Population or respondent group represented by the data
observations.evidence: The title states "Traders' Perceptions" and the source abstract says the paper summarizes results of a firm-level survey in nine countries.
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field can represent traders or respondent companies as the group the survey data are about.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic country columns and regional scope
observations.evidence: The table columns list Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Tunisia, UAE, and Yemen, while the source metadata gives spatial coverage as Middle East and North Africa.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the overall regional scope, named country entities, and country-level geographic granularity.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic role as surveyed or reporting country
observations.evidence: The country columns report responses for Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Tunisia, UAE, and Yemen in a firm-level survey.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_role field can express that the listed countries are respondent or reporting locations.

observations.metadata_concept: Table organization by country columns and issue or response rows
observations.evidence: Column headers are countries and Total, while rows are grouped under Customs Valuation, Rules of Origin, Product Standards Compliance, Yes/No counts, Range, and Average.
observations.fit_rationale: The structural and category fields cover the conceptual row and column organization and the explicit labels used for grouping.

observations.evidence: The artifact is visually presented as a bordered table with rows and country columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents the snapshot as a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Measurement forms include counts, percentages, ranges, and averages
observations.evidence: Rows are labeled "Yes (Count)," "No (Count)," "Range," and "Average," and totals include values such as "69 (29.6%)."
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type field captures the statistical forms in which the table values are expressed.

observations.metadata_concept: Unit of measure for compliance-cost values
observations.evidence: The table labels costs of compliance as "percent of CIF import value."
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure field covers the percent-of-CIF-import-value unit used to interpret those values.

observations.evidence: The table footnotes state "Numbers in parentheses are percents of total respondents" and "See Footnote in Table A-1."
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field is designed for explanatory footnotes and caveats that aid interpretation.

observations.evidence: The source abstract states that the paper summarizes "the results of a firm-level survey in nine countries."
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field explicitly covers survey instruments when stated in the document context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Changes in cross-border trade costs in the Pan-Arab free trade area, 2001-2008."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the source metadata lists language as "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The language field covers the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/311581468275088490/pdf/WPS5031.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable source-document locator.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists idno "11017288" and a World Bank D&R identifier "11017288."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields refer to the snapshot within a document or to projects, not to the parent source document itself.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for the parent document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a machine-actionable locator for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, citation linking, and reinspection of the source document for extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An institutional, repository, catalog, or other formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined as a document-assigned identifier for the snapshot, and project_identifier is limited to associated projects or operations, leaving parent-document identifiers unrepresented.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves deduplication, source-document matching, provenance tracking, and reliable lookup of snapshots across document repositories.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The mathematical transformation or scaling applied to a represented variable before reporting or analysis, such as logarithm, differencing, indexing, normalization, or standardization.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name can retain a transformed label but conflates the underlying concept with the transformation, while measure_type and unit_of_measure describe statistical form or units rather than transformations applied to variables.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Capturing transformations improves interpretation, search, and analytical reuse of snapshots where the same underlying variable appears in transformed and untransformed forms.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A document-internal reference to another table, figure, panel, or snapshot whose values, estimates, or results are cited, reused, or compared within the current snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier identifies the current snapshot, comparison_group captures benchmark groups or entities, and interpretive_note captures explanatory text, but none represent a structured reference from the current snapshot to another document artifact.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Capturing related snapshot references supports navigation, provenance verification, and reconstruction of analytical dependencies among tables and figures within a document.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: snapshot title and document-assigned table identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Table 5: Rural farm profits per capita, IFLS.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the heading and internal_identifier captures “Table 5” without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The artifact is a tabular display with rows, columns, coefficients, and standard errors.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Distributional impact analysis of past climate variability in rural Indonesia.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/421651468260134997/pdf/WPS5070.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title but has no field for a retrieval URL that supports verification and access to the parent document.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language “english.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: geographic scope of the represented analysis
observations.evidence: The source-document title refers to “rural Indonesia” and the metadata ref_country lists “Indonesia.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Indonesia as the geographic context evidenced by the source document.

observations.evidence: The table title ends with “IFLS.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field can capture the explicitly cited source acronym without requiring expansion.

observations.metadata_concept: dependent or outcome variable in a model-results table
observations.evidence: The table header states “Dependent variable: Farm profits per capita.”
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field can store the variable label but loses the explicit dependent-variable role needed to interpret the model-results table.

observations.evidence: Rows under coefficients list “Monsoon Onset,” “Onset squared,” “Onset cubic,” and “Onset quartic.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can identify row labels or a primary variable but do not distinguish covariates from the dependent variable in a statistical model table.

observations.evidence: Column group headings and row sections include “One lag,” “Two lags,” “Prior Year,” and “Two years ago.”
observations.fit_rationale: Column_dimension can describe table organization, but time_period or comparison_group would conflate model lag specification with the represented data period or a benchmark comparison.

observations.metadata_concept: early versus late onset estimated-effect categories
observations.evidence: The lower section is headed “Estimated Effects” with subsections “Early onset” and “Late onset.”
observations.fit_rationale: The category and comparison fields can represent early and late onset as explicit analytical categories compared within the table.

observations.metadata_concept: statistical estimates and model diagnostics as table contents
observations.evidence: The table displays “Coef,” “SE,” “Observations,” “Households,” and “R² (within)” with associated numeric values.
observations.fit_rationale: The displayed estimates, standard errors, counts, and diagnostics are statistical outputs or table contents explicitly outside the metadata schema scope.

observations.evidence: The bottom note states “See notes to table 1.”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field can store the explicitly provided note text even though the referenced note content is not present in this snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The URL or persistent web location for the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable location for verification, citation, or access.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval of the source document, provenance verification, and linking indexed snapshots back to their institutional source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The variable explicitly identified as the dependent, outcome, response, or target variable in an analytical or model-results snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name captures the variable label but not its analytical role as the dependent variable, which is important in regression and model-results tables.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves search and reuse of model-result snapshots by enabling users to distinguish outcomes from predictors or grouping dimensions.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A variable explicitly presented as an independent variable, predictor, regressor, covariate, or explanatory factor in an analytical or model-results snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name is oriented to the primary represented variable and row_dimension describes table structure, but neither captures the predictor role of variables in a model specification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval and comparison of analytical snapshots by modeled predictors, covariates, or explanatory factors.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated lag horizon or lag specification used in a model or analytical estimate presented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the period represented by data, column_dimension describes layout, and comparison_group describes benchmarks, but none adequately represents lagged model specification semantics.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret and retrieve analytical snapshots that compare effects across prior-period or multi-lag specifications without confusing those lags with data coverage dates.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 4: Estimated Impact of P4P on Maternal and Child Health Care Services."
observations.fit_rationale: The heading provides both the primary title and the internal identifier explicitly covered by existing fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of the table
observations.evidence: The table is titled "Estimated Impact of P4P on Maternal and Child Health Care Services" and contains sections for maternal care utilization, quality of prenatal care, and child preventive visits.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent the analytical purpose as a subject summary and the broad health theme as subject domain.

observations.evidence: The title refers to "P4P" and the source abstract states that paying for performance provides financial incentives for providers.
observations.fit_rationale: The represented intervention or policy activity is directly captured by intervention_type.

observations.metadata_concept: Outcome indicators represented in table rows
observations.evidence: Rows include "Any prenatal care (=1)," "Institutional delivery (=1)," "Standardized Quality Score," and "Child 12-23 months is fully immunized (=1)."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can capture the measured concepts as variable_name values and the table-row organization as row_dimension with explicit category labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Grouped health-service categories used to organize outcomes
observations.evidence: Bold row group headings include "Maternal Care Utilization," "Quality of Prenatal Care," and "Child Preventive Visit in last 4 weeks."
observations.fit_rationale: These group headings are explicit classification labels for the row-organized outcome measures and fit existing category fields.

observations.evidence: Column headers include "N," "β," "(95% C.I.)," "P-Value," and "% Δ+."
observations.fit_rationale: The column structure can be described using column_dimension and category_labels without storing the statistical output values themselves.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical method used to estimate results
observations.evidence: Footnotes repeatedly state that "The β is the estimated treatment effect" with controls, fixed effects, and clustered standard errors.
observations.fit_rationale: The estimation approach and methodological qualifications are representable through analysis_method and interpretive_note.

observations.evidence: Footnotes describe covariate controls, facility fixed effects, clustering levels, eligibility limits for tetanus, and the calculation of "% Δ."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing interpretive_note is defined to capture explanatory notes, caveats, assumptions, and methodological remarks.

observations.evidence: The table includes maternal care rows and child rows such as "Visit by child age 0-23 months" and "Child 12-23 months is fully immunized."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly covers human groups that are the subjects of represented data.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context from the source document
observations.evidence: The source-document title is "Paying primary health care centers for performance in Rwanda" and ref_country lists Rwanda.
observations.fit_rationale: The document metadata materially contextualizes the snapshot’s Rwanda setting and maps to existing geographic fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data collection design and sources
observations.evidence: The source abstract states that the evaluation used data from 166 facilities and a random sample of 2158 households.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema includes fields for the collection method and cited data source when explicitly stated.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Paying primary health care centers for performance in Rwanda."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field exactly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The language used in the snapshot is directly represented by the existing language field.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document identifier for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "11696987" and World Bank ID "090224b0828b65ee."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields identify the snapshot within the document or name the parent document but do not capture a parent-document identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/285131468308376024/pdf/WPS5190.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a parent-document title field but no field for a retrieval URL or access location for the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the data snapshot, such as a repository identifier, institutional document ID, DOI, or catalog record ID.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier refers to the snapshot’s document-assigned label, while source_document_title names the parent document but cannot record stable document identifiers needed for verification or retrieval.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, citation, source verification, and reliable retrieval of snapshots across document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or access link for the parent document containing the data snapshot when explicitly provided in source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide an actionable access location, and no existing field captures document-level retrieval links.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to locate, verify, and retrieve the source document for the snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 4: Estimated Impact of P4P on Maternal and Child Health Care Services."
observations.fit_rationale: The heading provides both the primary title and the internal identifier explicitly covered by existing fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of the table
observations.evidence: The table is titled "Estimated Impact of P4P on Maternal and Child Health Care Services" and contains sections for maternal care utilization, quality of prenatal care, and child preventive visits.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent the analytical purpose as a subject summary and the broad health theme as subject domain.

observations.evidence: The title refers to "P4P" and the source abstract states that paying for performance provides financial incentives for providers.
observations.fit_rationale: The represented intervention or policy activity is directly captured by intervention_type.

observations.metadata_concept: Outcome indicators represented in table rows
observations.evidence: Rows include "Any prenatal care (=1)," "Institutional delivery (=1)," "Standardized Quality Score," and "Child 12-23 months is fully immunized (=1)."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can capture the measured concepts as variable_name values and the table-row organization as row_dimension with explicit category labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Grouped health-service categories used to organize outcomes
observations.evidence: Bold row group headings include "Maternal Care Utilization," "Quality of Prenatal Care," and "Child Preventive Visit in last 4 weeks."
observations.fit_rationale: These group headings are explicit classification labels for the row-organized outcome measures and fit existing category fields.

observations.evidence: Column headers include "N," "β," "(95% C.I.)," "P-Value," and "% Δ+."
observations.fit_rationale: The column structure can be described using column_dimension and category_labels without storing the statistical output values themselves.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical method used to estimate results
observations.evidence: Footnotes repeatedly state that "The β is the estimated treatment effect" with controls, fixed effects, and clustered standard errors.
observations.fit_rationale: The estimation approach and methodological qualifications are representable through analysis_method and interpretive_note.

observations.evidence: Footnotes describe covariate controls, facility fixed effects, clustering levels, eligibility limits for tetanus, and the calculation of "% Δ."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing interpretive_note is defined to capture explanatory notes, caveats, assumptions, and methodological remarks.

observations.evidence: The table includes maternal care rows and child rows such as "Visit by child age 0-23 months" and "Child 12-23 months is fully immunized."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly covers human groups that are the subjects of represented data.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context from the source document
observations.evidence: The source-document title is "Paying primary health care centers for performance in Rwanda" and ref_country lists Rwanda.
observations.fit_rationale: The document metadata materially contextualizes the snapshot’s Rwanda setting and maps to existing geographic fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data collection design and sources
observations.evidence: The source abstract states that the evaluation used data from 166 facilities and a random sample of 2158 households.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema includes fields for the collection method and cited data source when explicitly stated.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Paying primary health care centers for performance in Rwanda."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field exactly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The language used in the snapshot is directly represented by the existing language field.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document identifier for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "11696987" and World Bank ID "090224b0828b65ee."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields identify the snapshot within the document or name the parent document but do not capture a parent-document identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/285131468308376024/pdf/WPS5190.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a parent-document title field but no field for a retrieval URL or access location for the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier refers to the snapshot’s document-assigned label, while source_document_title names the parent document but cannot record stable document identifiers needed for verification or retrieval.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, citation, source verification, and reliable retrieval of snapshots across document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or access link for the parent document containing the data snapshot when explicitly provided in source-document metadata.
