observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Table 5: Gabon Log Output Channeled into a Single Chain (at Gabon Wood Utilization Rates), Assuming Input of 3,400,000m3 logs.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the caption and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned label “Table 5” without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The artifact presents rows, columns, grid lines, and column headings such as “Logs,” “Sawn wood,” “Veneer sheets,” and “Plywood.”
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of Gabon timber/log processing value chain outputs
observations.evidence: The title describes “Gabon Log Output Channeled into a Single Chain” and the rows list output, foreign exchange, employment, capital cost, and producer margins.
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain and subject_summary can represent the timber/forestry value-chain domain and the table’s analytical purpose.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary measures reported by table rows
observations.evidence: The row labels include “Output real,” “Foreign exchange,” “Employment,” “Capital cost,” and “Producer margins.”
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name captures the reported measures and row_dimension captures that measures are organized by table rows.

observations.metadata_concept: Product or processing-stage categories used as table columns
observations.evidence: The column labels are “Logs,” “Sawn wood,” “Veneer sheets,” and “Plywood.”
observations.fit_rationale: category_dimension, category_labels, and column_dimension adequately encode the column grouping by timber product or processing stage.

observations.evidence: The title refers to “Gabon Log Output” and “Gabon Wood Utilization Rates.”
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities can represent Gabon as the explicitly stated geographic focus.

observations.metadata_concept: Multiple temporal references with distinct semantic roles
observations.evidence: Notes state a 2003–2007 production-volume average, 2006 prices, fieldwork data collected November 2008–March 2009, and 2003 capital depreciation costs and exchange rate.
observations.fit_rationale: time_period can store dates and interpretive_note can preserve explanations, but the schema does not structure whether each date is a data period, base-price year, collection period, or cost/exchange-rate reference year.

observations.evidence: The table includes “’000m3,” “$1,000,” “indexed to ex-forest cost of log,” and measures such as employment and foreign exchange.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields can represent physical units, monetary denomination, index/count forms, and financial quantities.

observations.metadata_concept: Cited data sources for represented values
observations.evidence: The source line cites “Terheggen’s fieldwork data” and “Odyssée Développement,” and notes cite UNCTAD, ITTO 2009, FAOSTAT, and data.un.org.
observations.fit_rationale: data_source directly captures cited datasets, fieldwork data, publications, and organizations from which the represented data originate.

observations.metadata_concept: Methodological and interpretive notes attached to table values
observations.evidence: Notes describe conversion using wood utilization rates, species weighted averages, own calculations, and exclusions of environmental costs such as consultancy and certification fees.
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method, data_collection_method, and interpretive_note can capture the stated calculations, fieldwork basis, assumptions, and exclusions.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document title and snapshot language
observations.evidence: Document metadata gives the title “What happens when the market shifts to China ? the Gabon timber and Thai cassava value chains,” and the snapshot text is in English.
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title and language directly represent the parent document title and language evidenced for the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator for the parent source document
observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/859011468011755367/pdf/WPS5206.pdf” and identifiers including World Bank D&R “11777361.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a parent document title but no field for a source-document URL or persistent document identifier, while internal_identifier is snapshot-level and project_identifier is project-level.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The semantic role of an explicitly stated temporal reference associated with the snapshot, such as data averaging period, price base year, data collection period, cost base year, or exchange-rate reference year.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period records temporal values but does not distinguish the roles of multiple dates, and interpretive_note preserves prose without enabling structured temporal filtering or interpretation.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: It would help users correctly interpret and search snapshots where dates qualify different aspects of measurement, calculation, collection, or valuation.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable locator, and existing identifier fields are scoped to snapshots or projects rather than source documents.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: It would support provenance verification, citation, deduplication, and retrieval of the source document for the extracted snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can describe the education, employment, and earnings focus without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Vocational secondary schooling, occupational choice, and earnings in Brazil.”

observations.evidence: The footnote states “* Significant at the .001 level. Differences between means were tested employing t-tests.”

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists identifiers including “World Bank D&R” identifier “437268” and URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/564481468769185938/pdf/multi-page.pdf.”

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot caption title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 4: Probit Estimates : Financial Liberalization and Transparency (1)".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has title for the caption text and internal_identifier for the document-assigned label "Table 4."

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a tabular display with rows of explanatory variables and columns of estimates.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of financial liberalization, transparency, and bank crisis
observations.evidence: The title states "Financial Liberalization and Transparency" and the table states "Dependent Variable: Bank Crisis."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject fields can capture the broad financial-sector domain and summarize the table's analytical focus.

observations.metadata_concept: Dependent or outcome variable in a statistical model
observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly states "Dependent Variable: Bank Crisis."
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can store "Bank Crisis" but does not preserve the explicitly stated dependent-variable role needed to interpret a model-results table.

observations.evidence: The table title states "Probit Estimates."
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method directly captures the explicitly stated Probit estimation method.

observations.evidence: The left row header says "Explanatory Variables" and row labels include "GDP growth," "Inflation Rate," and "Transparency."
observations.fit_rationale: row_dimension can capture that rows represent explanatory variables and category_labels can capture their explicit names.

observations.metadata_concept: Alternative statistical model specifications represented by columns
observations.evidence: Column headings distinguish specifications such as "Measure 1 Corruption index," "Measure 2 Public sector involvement," and "1 period Lagged Macro and Financial Var."
observations.fit_rationale: The column and category fields can record the labels but do not clearly capture their role as alternative estimation specifications rather than ordinary categories or comparison groups.

observations.metadata_concept: Reported statistical forms for table entries
observations.evidence: The column headers state "dF/dX" and "(z-statistics)."
observations.fit_rationale: measure_type can represent that the table reports marginal effects and z-statistics without storing the numerical outputs themselves.

observations.evidence: The note states "*** Significant at 1%", "**Significant at 5 %", and "* Significant at 10%."
observations.fit_rationale: interpretive_note is intended for explanatory notes and caveats that aid interpretation of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Cited sources for represented variables or indexes
observations.evidence: Footnotes state "Data source Political risk services of ICRG" and "Index constructed using International Financial Statistics."
observations.fit_rationale: data_source directly captures cited datasets or publications from which represented data originate.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal coverage of the empirical data
observations.evidence: The document abstract says the empirical evidence is "based on data for 56 countries in 1977-97."
observations.fit_rationale: Because the abstract explicitly describes the empirical evidence underlying the paper, time_period can capture the stated 1977-97 data period for this model table.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic coverage and granularity of the empirical data
observations.evidence: The document abstract says the empirical evidence is "based on data for 56 countries in 1977-97."
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope can record the explicit multi-country coverage and geographic_granularity can record that data are at the country level.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Transparency, liberalization, and banking crisis."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: language directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Persistent identifier for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "437731" and World Bank ID "090224b082b057b3."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a parent document identifier that enables unambiguous verification or retrieval.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/429731468739157817/pdf/multi-page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but lacks a field for a source-document access URL needed for retrieval and verification.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The outcome, response, or dependent variable explicitly identified for a statistical model or analytical result represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name can name the measured concept but does not preserve the model-specific role that the snapshot explicitly assigns to it as the dependent variable.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports accurate indexing, retrieval, and interpretation of regression or model-results tables by distinguishing outcomes from predictors and other variables.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly labeled statistical model variant, estimation specification, or regression column represented in a model-results snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: column_dimension and category_labels can store column labels, but they conflate model specifications with ordinary table categories and comparison_group implies a benchmark relationship that may not be present.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to identify and compare alternative estimation specifications without reconstructing the table contents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent identifier assigned to the parent document that contains the snapshot, such as an institutional repository ID, DOI, or catalog identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but cannot disambiguate documents or support reliable lookup when titles are duplicated or changed.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, deduplication, citation, verification, and retrieval of snapshots back to their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or URI where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title provides descriptive provenance but not an actionable retrieval location for the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports auditability and retrieval by allowing users or systems to locate the source document associated with a snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot caption title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 4: Probit Estimates : Financial Liberalization and Transparency (1)".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has title for the caption text and internal_identifier for the document-assigned label "Table 4."

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a tabular display with rows of explanatory variables and columns of estimates.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of financial liberalization, transparency, and bank crisis
observations.evidence: The title states "Financial Liberalization and Transparency" and the table states "Dependent Variable: Bank Crisis."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject fields can capture the broad financial-sector domain and summarize the table's analytical focus.

observations.metadata_concept: Dependent or outcome variable in a statistical model
observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly states "Dependent Variable: Bank Crisis."
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can store "Bank Crisis" but does not preserve the explicitly stated dependent-variable role needed to interpret a model-results table.

observations.evidence: The table title states "Probit Estimates."
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method directly captures the explicitly stated Probit estimation method.

observations.evidence: The left row header says "Explanatory Variables" and row labels include "GDP growth," "Inflation Rate," and "Transparency."
observations.fit_rationale: row_dimension can capture that rows represent explanatory variables and category_labels can capture their explicit names.

observations.metadata_concept: Alternative statistical model specifications represented by columns
observations.evidence: Column headings distinguish specifications such as "Measure 1 Corruption index," "Measure 2 Public sector involvement," and "1 period Lagged Macro and Financial Var."
observations.fit_rationale: The column and category fields can record the labels but do not clearly capture their role as alternative estimation specifications rather than ordinary categories or comparison groups.

observations.metadata_concept: Reported statistical forms for table entries
observations.evidence: The column headers state "dF/dX" and "(z-statistics)."
observations.fit_rationale: measure_type can represent that the table reports marginal effects and z-statistics without storing the numerical outputs themselves.

observations.evidence: The note states "*** Significant at 1%", "**Significant at 5 %", and "* Significant at 10%."
observations.fit_rationale: interpretive_note is intended for explanatory notes and caveats that aid interpretation of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Cited sources for represented variables or indexes
observations.evidence: Footnotes state "Data source Political risk services of ICRG" and "Index constructed using International Financial Statistics."
observations.fit_rationale: data_source directly captures cited datasets or publications from which represented data originate.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal coverage of the empirical data
observations.evidence: The document abstract says the empirical evidence is "based on data for 56 countries in 1977-97."

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic coverage and granularity of the empirical data

observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope can record the explicit multi-country coverage and geographic_granularity can record that data are at the country level.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Transparency, liberalization, and banking crisis."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language "english" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: language directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a parent document identifier that enables unambiguous verification or retrieval.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The outcome, response, or dependent variable explicitly identified for a statistical model or analytical result represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: variable_name can name the measured concept but does not preserve the model-specific role that the snapshot explicitly assigns to it as the dependent variable.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports accurate indexing, retrieval, and interpretation of regression or model-results tables by distinguishing outcomes from predictors and other variables.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly labeled statistical model variant, estimation specification, or regression column represented in a model-results snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: column_dimension and category_labels can store column labels, but they conflate model specifications with ordinary table categories and comparison_group implies a benchmark relationship that may not be present.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to identify and compare alternative estimation specifications without reconstructing the table contents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent identifier assigned to the parent document that contains the snapshot, such as an institutional repository ID, DOI, or catalog identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but cannot disambiguate documents or support reliable lookup when titles are duplicated or changed.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, deduplication, citation, verification, and retrieval of snapshots back to their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or URI where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title provides descriptive provenance but not an actionable retrieval location for the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports auditability and retrieval by allowing users or systems to locate the source document associated with a snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The parent document title ends with "in Mexico" and the document metadata lists ref_country as Mexico.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other resolvable link used to access the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not provide a retrieval location, and no existing provenance field stores a source-document access link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, auditability, and verification by linking a snapshot metadata record back to the document from which it was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The author, authors, or credited creators of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the title of the parent document, while data_source would incorrectly conflate document authorship with the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves citation, attribution, provenance review, and disambiguation of snapshots from similarly titled institutional documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a stable unique identifier, and internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within the document rather than the document itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables unambiguous source-document identification, deduplication, retrieval, and verification of snapshots extracted from institutional document collections.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other resolvable link used to access the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not provide a retrieval location, and no existing provenance field stores a source-document access link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, auditability, and verification by linking a snapshot metadata record back to the document from which it was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The author, authors, or credited creators of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the title of the parent document, while data_source would incorrectly conflate document authorship with the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves citation, attribution, provenance review, and disambiguation of snapshots from similarly titled institutional documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the caption text and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned label “Table 6.”

observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.fit_rationale: variable_name can capture “use of fertilizer” and subject_summary can summarize the table’s analytical purpose.

observations.evidence: The rows are labeled “Female,” “Male,” and “All,” and the title refers to “Gender Differences.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent gender as the row/category dimension, the explicit labels as category_labels, and the gender comparison as comparison_group.

observations.evidence: The column headers are “Gauss,” “Epanechnikov,” “Quartic,” “Uniform,” and “Cosinus.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing structural fields can record the column dimension and its explicit labels without needing to reconstruct the table values.

observations.evidence: The table footer states “Source: Authors’ calculations,” and the document abstract states that the paper uses data from the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source covers the cited survey and calculation source from which the represented results originate.

observations.evidence: The document abstract says the paper uses “the logic of causal inference” and “a normalized comparison of productivity outcomes.”
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method is defined to capture explicitly stated analytical or statistical methods used to produce reported results.

observations.evidence: The document abstract identifies the underlying data as the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period can represent 2004 as the period of the underlying survey when explicitly tied to the data source.

observations.evidence: The source document title refers to tea estates in Rwanda and the document metadata lists ref_country as “Rwanda.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Rwanda as the represented geographic context evidenced by the parent document.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title concerns fertilizer use and the document abstract describes the “tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain and subject_summary can represent the agricultural or tea-sector context without requiring a new field.

observations.evidence: The visible table text is in English and the document metadata lists language as “english.”
observations.fit_rationale: language directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Reading tealeaves on the potential impact of the privatization of tea estates in Rwanda.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes idno “9089743” and identifiers such as World Bank D&R identifier “9089743.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but no existing field stores a stable parent-document identifier for retrieval or verification.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/944161468107337888/pdf/wps4566.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a parent-document title field but no field for the source document URL needed to retrieve or verify the snapshot source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent source document that contains the snapshot, distinct from any snapshot-level internal identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document name, while internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot’s in-document label and project_identifier is limited to associated projects or operations.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of snapshots across institutional document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web link for accessing the parent source document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document textually but does not provide a retrievable location, and no existing provenance field stores a document access link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the source document, verify extracted snapshot metadata, and trace provenance back to the original publication.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot caption title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot caption reads “Table 8. A Model of Participation in the Tea Sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The caption is directly representable as title and the “Table 8” prefix is directly representable as internal_identifier.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a tabular display with rows of variables and columns such as Coefficient, Std. Error, z-Statistic, and Prob.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a table without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The caption identifies the snapshot as “A Model of Participation in the Tea Sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_summary field can describe the model’s purpose and variable_name can capture participation in the tea sector as the primary measured concept.

observations.evidence: The caption refers to the “Tea Sector,” and the document abstract discusses the tea sector and privatization of tea estates.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field can represent the tea sector or related agricultural policy domain.

observations.evidence: The source document title and abstract explicitly refer to Rwanda and the 2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Rwanda as the geographic context when supported by the document context.

observations.evidence: The snapshot states “Source: Authors’ calculations,” and the document abstract states that the paper uses data from the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field can capture the cited calculation source and the survey named as the origin of the represented data.

observations.evidence: The document abstract states that the paper uses data from the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_collection_method field can represent the explicitly stated survey method.

observations.evidence: The document abstract identifies the data as coming from the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field can represent 2004 as the data period because it is explicitly tied to the survey data used.

observations.evidence: The table title is “A Model of Participation in the Tea Sector,” and the table reports coefficient, standard error, z-statistic, and probability columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The analysis_method field can represent the explicitly stated modeling context, while the numerical estimates themselves remain out of scope.

observations.evidence: The first column is labeled “Variable,” and the remaining columns are labeled “Coefficient,” “Std. Error,” “z-Statistic,” and “Prob.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing row_dimension and column_dimension fields can describe the table’s conceptual row and column organization without reconstructing cell values.

observations.evidence: The table text and source-document language metadata are in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly represents the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Reading tealeaves on the potential impact of the privatization of tea estates in Rwanda.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/944161468107337888/pdf/wps4566.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval URL that identifies and verifies the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier “9089743” and World Bank ID “090224b0828af3e2.”
observations.fit_rationale: internal_identifier is defined for identifiers assigned to the snapshot within the document, not identifiers assigned to the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata states “date_published”: “2010-07-01.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the period represented by the data, not the publication date of the parent document containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The URL or web location where the parent source document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but cannot store a retrieval link, and no other v1.1 field captures source-document access location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, citation, and auditability of extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A repository, catalog, DOI, or other formal identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is limited to identifiers used to reference the snapshot within the source document, while project_identifier is limited to projects or operations.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves deduplication, source-document linking, provenance tracking, and reliable retrieval across document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or release date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period captures the data period represented in the snapshot and would conflate data temporality with document publication timing.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, version assessment, chronological organization, and provenance verification without misusing data-period fields.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The title explicitly refers to “Tea and Non-Tea Households.”
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field directly describes the households that the data are about.

observations.evidence: The column headers are “Tea,” “Non-Tea,” and “ALL.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the household-type grouping through column_dimension and category_labels, with comparison_group covering the explicit tea versus non-tea comparison.

observations.evidence: The first column is headed “Characteristics” and lists items such as Age, Education, Household Size, Land, Livestock, Bicycle, Road30, and Water30.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension field captures the conceptual row organization, while variable_name can represent the measured characteristics.

observations.evidence: The title states that the table reports “Average Characteristics.”
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type field covers values expressed as averages.

observations.evidence: The row labels include “Education (years)” and “Land (ares).”
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure field can record explicitly stated units such as years and ares.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data source and calculation attribution
observations.evidence: The table footer states “Source: Authors’ calculations,” and the document abstract states that the paper uses data from the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field can represent both the cited calculation source and the named survey source of the represented data.

observations.evidence: The document abstract states that the paper uses data from the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field covers an explicitly identified survey instrument.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal context of represented survey data
observations.evidence: The document abstract identifies the underlying source as the “2004 Quantitative Baseline Survey of the tea sector.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field can capture the explicitly stated 2004 survey timing for the represented data.

observations.evidence: The source document title refers to Rwanda and the document metadata lists ref_country as “Rwanda” and spatial_coverage as “Africa.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Rwanda and the broader Africa context when supported by the parent document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Reading tealeaves on the potential impact of the privatization of tea estates in Rwanda.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the document metadata lists language as “english.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly records the language used in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Persistent identifier for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier “9089743” and World Bank ID “090224b0828af3e2.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a parent document title field, but internal_identifier is for the snapshot and project_identifier is for projects, leaving no adequate field for parent-document identifiers.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/944161468107337888/pdf/wps4566.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can name the parent document but has no field for a URL used to retrieve or verify it.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
