CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Annex 14: Country at a Glance” and “GUINEA: HEALTH SECTOR SUPPORT PROJECT.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the heading and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned annex number without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title states “GUINEA: HEALTH SECTOR SUPPORT PROJECT,” and document metadata lists World Bank Project ID “P065126.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly represents the associated project name and formal project identifier.

observations.evidence: The snapshot and source-document title refer to a “Health Sector Support Project,” and document topics include “Health,” “Health Services Delivery,” and “Maternal Mortality and Morbidity.”
observations.fit_rationale: The health-sector theme and summary purpose can be represented by subject_domain and subject_summary.

observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular sections with multiple charts titled “Development diamond,” “Economic ratios,” “Growth of investment and GDP (%),” and “Growth of exports and imports (%).”
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type captures the mixed table/chart form and panel_title captures the explicitly titled subfigures.

observations.evidence: Rows and chart axes list indicators such as population, GNI per capita, life expectancy, infant mortality, GDP, debt ratios, trade, investment, and imports/exports.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema allows the represented indicators or measured concepts to be recorded as variable_name, with financial_measure available for funding or economic quantities where applicable.

observations.evidence: Tables organize rows by indicators and sectors and columns by “Guinea,” “Sub-Saharan Africa,” “Low-income,” and years such as 1982, 1992, 2001, and 2002.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly represents conceptual row and column dimensions and their explicit category labels.

observations.evidence: The snapshot compares Guinea with “Sub-Saharan Africa” and “Low-income,” and chart legends compare “Guinea” with “Low-income group.”
observations.fit_rationale: comparison_group captures the intended benchmark relationship, while category_labels and geographic_entities can record the explicit comparator labels where appropriate.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is headed “GUINEA” and includes comparator labels “Sub-Saharan Africa,” while document metadata lists ref_country “Guinea.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema covers the primary country, named regional comparator, and geographic reporting level.

observations.evidence: The snapshot includes years and periods such as 2002, 1996–02, 1982, 1992, 2001, 2002, 1982–92, 1992–02, and 2002–06.
observations.fit_rationale: time_period captures the explicit dates and ranges, and temporal_granularity captures annual or multi-year reporting where evident.

observations.evidence: Labels include “millions,” “US$,” “US$ billions,” “%,” “years,” “per 1,000 live births,” “% of GDP,” and “average annual growth.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly captures units, currency denominations, and statistical forms such as percentages, ratios, rates, and growth measures.

observations.evidence: Indicator labels refer to “population,” “labor force,” “children under 5,” “school-age population,” and “population age 15+.”
observations.fit_rationale: population_group adequately represents the human populations or demographic groups that the indicators concern.

observations.metadata_concept: source document title and snapshot language
observations.evidence: Document metadata title is “Guinea - Health Sector Support Project,” and the snapshot text is in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly provides fields for the parent document title and the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Document metadata lists idno “5801174” and identifiers including World Bank D&R “5801174,” World Bank GUID “551731468037482453,” and World Bank Project ID “P065126.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and project_identifier captures the project, but neither records repository-assigned identifiers for the source document itself.

observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/551731468037482453/pdf/28046.pdf” and relations include PDF and text URLs.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrieval or verification link to the source document.

observations.evidence: Document metadata states type “Project Appraisal Document,” and tags include document_type “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field does not capture the genre or institutional document type that contextualizes the extracted annex.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A repository-assigned or persistent identifier for the parent document from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document’s title, internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within the document, and project_identifier identifies the project rather than the source document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports precise source-document identification, deduplication, citation, and verification of extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or access link for the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The existing schema records the parent document title but not a link that enables retrieval or verification of the document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the original document and validate the snapshot’s provenance.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre or document type of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not represent document genre such as Project Appraisal Document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, interpretation, and organization of snapshots by the type of institutional document from which they were extracted.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic country context represented by the snapshot
observations.evidence: The snapshot header reads "Albania" and the source-document metadata lists ref_country as Albania.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields directly represent the country scope and named country entity shown for the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Broad macroeconomic and public finance subject matter
observations.evidence: The snapshot sections include "PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE," "TRADE," "BALANCE of PAYMENTS," and "EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS."
observations.fit_rationale: The subject fields can capture the broad economic domain and summarize the snapshot as Albania macroeconomic, trade, payments, and debt indicators.

observations.metadata_concept: Multiple represented economic variables and indicators
observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly names indicators such as consumer prices, implicit GDP deflator, current revenue, total exports, current account balance, and total debt outstanding.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable and row-dimension fields can represent the named indicators used as the measured concepts in the tables and charts.

observations.metadata_concept: Annual time periods represented in tables and charts
observations.evidence: The tables use year columns including 1977, 1987, 1997, and 1998, while the charts show annual x-axis labels such as 92 through 98.
observations.fit_rationale: The temporal fields and column dimension can capture the represented years and annual reporting resolution.

observations.metadata_concept: Units, currency, and measurement forms used to interpret values
observations.evidence: The snapshot labels measures as "(% change)," "(% of GDP)," "US$ millions," "1993=100," and chart titles such as "Inflation (%)" and "Current account balance to GDP ratio (%)."
observations.fit_rationale: The measurement fields cover percent units, US dollar denomination, index/rate forms, and financial quantities represented in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Categorical organization by indicators, years, and financing or creditor categories
observations.evidence: The snapshot organizes data by indicator rows, year columns, chart series such as GDP deflator and CPI, and pie-chart categories labeled IBRD, IDA, IMF, other multilateral, bilateral, private, and short-term.
observations.fit_rationale: The category and structural fields can represent the conceptual grouping dimensions and explicit labels used to organize the data.

observations.metadata_concept: Composite snapshot made of several visual artifact types
observations.evidence: The image combines large tabular sections with a line chart, bar charts, and a pie chart on the same page.
observations.fit_rationale: Visualization type and panel title can list component encodings and labels, but they do not explicitly capture that the snapshot is a composite page with no single primary visualization.

observations.metadata_concept: Explicit titles for individual chart panels and sections
observations.evidence: Panel and section headings include "Inflation (%)," "Export and import levels (US$ millions)," "Current account balance to GDP ratio (%)," and "Composition of total debt, 1998 (US$ millions)."
observations.fit_rationale: The panel-title field directly represents explicit headings for individual panels within the multi-panel snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document and associated project identification
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Albania - Emergency Road Repair Project" and identifiers include World Bank Project ID "P068853."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has dedicated fields for the parent document title and the project name or identifier associated with the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Institutional source or producer responsible for the snapshot or parent document
observations.evidence: The snapshot footer reads "Development Economics" and the source-document metadata lists producer name "World Bank" with role "Source."
observations.fit_rationale: Data source is limited to the origin of represented data, so using it for an institutional producer or publishing unit would conflate attribution with data provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator or repository identifier for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/543691468740389779/pdf/multi-page.pdf" and document identifiers such as World Bank D&R "439631" and GUID "543691468740389779."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields identify the source document title, snapshot-internal identifiers, or project identifiers but do not store a parent-document URL or repository locator.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document genre or institutional document type
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata states type "Project Appraisal Document" and tags include document_type "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for the parent document's genre or institutional document type.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Indicates whether the snapshot is a single visual artifact or a composite of multiple component artifact types, and may summarize the broad mix of components when explicitly evident.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type captures the primary or component visualization encodings and panel_title captures panel headings, but neither represents the composite nature of a snapshot that combines tables and multiple chart types without a single primary form.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports indexing, quality control, and downstream processing decisions that differ for single charts, tables, and composite analytical pages.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, institutional unit, or publisher explicitly attributed as producing, providing, or publishing the snapshot or its parent source document, when distinct from the represented data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the dataset, survey, publication, or cited origin of represented data, so it does not cleanly represent institutional attribution such as a producing department or publishing organization.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, institutional attribution, filtering, and verification without conflating data origins with document or snapshot producers.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent URL, repository link, or repository-level identifier that enables retrieval or verification of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrieval locator, while internal_identifier and project_identifier refer to the snapshot or associated project rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, and cite the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional type of the parent document containing the snapshot, as explicitly assigned in source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not encode whether it is a project appraisal document, report, working paper, annex, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, filtering, interpretation, and provenance assessment by distinguishing snapshots drawn from different classes of institutional documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.definition: The cartographic feature layer or legend class explicitly represented in a map snapshot, such as roads, rivers, boundaries, facilities, settlements, or other mapped feature types.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels describe data grouping, and location_type describes physical place types, but neither captures the map-specific concept of symbolized cartographic layers listed in a legend.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports search, filtering, and reuse of map snapshots by the types of infrastructure, boundaries, natural features, or facilities they depict.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, unit, organization, or other agent explicitly credited with producing or creating the data snapshot itself.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source refers to the origin of represented data and would conflate data provenance with the creator of the visual artifact.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables attribution, verification, and provenance tracking for maps and other snapshots where the visual artifact has an explicitly credited producer.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly associated with the creation, production, publication, or revision of the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and would distort dates that describe the snapshot artifact rather than the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users verify versioning, currency, and provenance of snapshots without confusing artifact dates with data coverage periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit cartographic scale information provided in a map snapshot, including a scale bar, representative fraction, or equivalent distance reference.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure can record distance units but does not represent the scale relationship needed to interpret distances on a map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves spatial interpretation and reuse of map snapshots by preserving explicit scale information.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent URL, document identifier, or other locator for the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title is not a retrieval locator, while internal_identifier and project_identifier refer to the snapshot or project rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, deduplication, and citation of the parent document from which the snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The cartographic feature layer or legend class explicitly represented in a map snapshot, such as roads, rivers, boundaries, facilities, settlements, or other mapped feature types.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels describe data grouping, and location_type describes physical place types, but neither captures the map-specific concept of symbolized cartographic layers listed in a legend.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports search, filtering, and reuse of map snapshots by the types of infrastructure, boundaries, natural features, or facilities they depict.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, unit, organization, or other agent explicitly credited with producing or creating the data snapshot itself.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source refers to the origin of represented data and would conflate data provenance with the creator of the visual artifact.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables attribution, verification, and provenance tracking for maps and other snapshots where the visual artifact has an explicitly credited producer.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly associated with the creation, production, publication, or revision of the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and would distort dates that describe the snapshot artifact rather than the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users verify versioning, currency, and provenance of snapshots without confusing artifact dates with data coverage periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit cartographic scale information provided in a map snapshot, including a scale bar, representative fraction, or equivalent distance reference.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure can record distance units but does not represent the scale relationship needed to interpret distances on a map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves spatial interpretation and reuse of map snapshots by preserving explicit scale information.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent URL, document identifier, or other locator for the parent source document containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, deduplication, and citation of the parent document from which the snapshot was extracted.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays the heading "Burundi" and major section headings such as "PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE," "TRADE," "BALANCE of PAYMENTS," and "EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title and panel_title fields can capture the displayed country/page heading and individual section or chart headings without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot contains sections on domestic prices, government finance, trade, balance of payments, and external debt/resource flows.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields adequately describe the broad macroeconomic and government-finance content of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Multiple represented indicators and financial measures
observations.evidence: Rows and chart titles name indicators including consumer prices, implicit GDP deflator, current revenue, total exports, imports, current account balance, total debt, and debt service.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name and financial_measure fields can represent the snapshot’s economic indicators and funding- or debt-related measures.

observations.metadata_concept: Categorical organization by indicator, year, trade item, and debt composition category
observations.evidence: The tables use indicator rows and year columns, while charts label series or categories such as GDP deflator, CPI, Exports, Imports, IBRD, IDA, IMF, Bilateral, Private, and Short-term.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category, row, column, and comparison fields can capture the explicit grouping dimensions and labels used to organize the data.

observations.metadata_concept: Annual temporal coverage represented by the data
observations.evidence: The tables show years 1976, 1986, 1996, and 1997, and the charts show annual labels such as 91 through 97 and a debt-composition title for 1997.
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period and temporal_granularity fields directly cover the represented years and annual reporting resolution.

observations.evidence: The page heading reads "Burundi," and the source document title is "Burundi - Second Social Action Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields adequately represent Burundi as the country covered by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Units of measure and statistical expression
observations.evidence: The snapshot labels values as "(% change)," "(% of GDP)," "US$ millions," "1995=100," and "Current account balance to GDP ratio (%)."
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure, currency, and measure_type fields can capture percentages, US-dollar amounts, index bases, ratios, and related measurement forms.

observations.metadata_concept: Composite visualization structure with multiple chart and table types
observations.evidence: The snapshot combines large tables with a line chart for inflation, a bar chart for exports and imports, a bar chart for current account balance, and a pie chart for total debt composition.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type and panel_title fields can describe the mixed table, line, bar, and pie chart components of the composite snapshot.

observations.evidence: All visible headings, labels, and notes in the snapshot are in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives the title as "Burundi - Second Social Action Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists World Bank Project ID "P064510" and additional project name "BI-Second Social Action Project -- P064510."
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields cover the explicit project context associated with the source document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Document type of the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies the document type as "Project Appraisal Document" and includes a document_type tag with the same value.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the parent document’s genre or type, which is distinct retrieval and provenance metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/590301468744270104/pdf/multi-page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can name the parent document but does not provide a field for a source-document locator needed for retrieval or verification.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot or page date distinct from represented data period
observations.evidence: The bottom-right of the snapshot displays the date "10/1/98."
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the period represented by the data, so using it for a printed page or snapshot date would conflate provenance timing with data coverage.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or administrative type of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided by the source document metadata or document context.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not encode whether it is a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, briefing, or another document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, provenance assessment, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent locator for the parent source document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: No existing v1.1 field stores a retrievable locator for the parent document; source_document_title is not sufficient for verification or access.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and downstream systems to retrieve, verify, and cite the document context for a data snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly printed on or directly associated with the snapshot as a page, figure, or generated artifact date, distinct from the period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period represents the dates covered by the data, not the date a snapshot or page was produced, updated, or labeled.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps distinguish data coverage from artifact provenance timing and supports chronological identification of snapshot versions or document pages.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

observations.metadata_concept: Composite snapshot headings and panel titles
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains section headings such as "PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE," "TRADE," "BALANCE of PAYMENTS," and chart headings such as "Inflation (%)," "Export and Import levels (US$ millions)," and "Current account balance to GDP ratio (%)."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title, panel_title, and subject_summary fields can represent the page-level and panel-level descriptive headings without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot presents domestic prices, government finance, trade, balance of payments, external debt, resource flows, and World Bank program measures.
observations.fit_rationale: The broad thematic domain and analytical purpose are directly representable by subject_domain and subject_summary.

observations.evidence: Explicit variables include "Consumer prices," "Implicit GDP deflator," "Current revenue," "Total exports," "Imports of goods and services," "Current account balance," and "Total debt outstanding and disbursed."
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field is designed to capture one or more primary indicators or measured concepts represented in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The tables list economic indicators in rows and years such as 1985, 1995, 1996, and 1997 in columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, column_dimension, and category_dimension fields cover the indicator-by-year organization of the tabular portions.

observations.evidence: The table columns show 1985, 1995, 1996, and 1997, while the charts show annual labels from 91 through 97.
observations.fit_rationale: The represented years and their annual reporting resolution map directly to time_period and temporal_granularity.

observations.evidence: The footer reads "World Bank Resident Mission: West Bank and Gaza," and the source document title is "West Bank and Gaza - Second Community Development Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The named place can be represented as the geographic scope and geographic entity when supported by the snapshot footer and source document title.

observations.metadata_concept: Measurement units, currencies, and statistical forms
observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly uses "(% change)," "(% of GDP, includes current grants)," "US$ millions," "1995=100," and "ratio (%)."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema covers units, monetary denomination, measure type, and interpretive caveats such as included grants.

observations.evidence: The inflation chart legend compares "GDP deflator" and "CPI," and the trade chart legend compares "Exports" and "Imports."
observations.fit_rationale: The comparison_group field captures intended comparative relationships, with category_labels available for the named compared series.

observations.evidence: The snapshot combines large tabular sections with a line chart for inflation and bar charts for export/import levels and current account balance.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the snapshot as a table-and-chart composite or as multiple visualization types.

observations.evidence: The snapshot footer states "World Bank Resident Mission: West Bank and Gaza," and the document metadata lists World Bank as a producer with role "Source."
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate an attributed producer or office with the underlying dataset or publication from which the represented data originate.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "West Bank and Gaza - Second Community Development Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Associated project name and project identifier
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes World Bank Project ID "P058684" and additional project name "GZ-GZ-COMMUNITY DEV. II -- P058684."
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly cover the associated project context evidenced in the document metadata.

observations.evidence: The document notes state "Lending instrument: Specific Investment Loan," and additional metadata includes "additional.wds_lndinstr_exact": "Specific Investment Loan."
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_instrument field directly represents the explicit lending or financing mechanism associated with the snapshot's project context.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language "English" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/573471468763473544/pdf/multi-page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrievable source-document link.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes identifiers such as World Bank D&R "439541," World Bank GUID "573471468763473544," and World Bank Chronical ID "090224b0828d1f7f."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing identifier fields cover the snapshot's internal label or associated project, not repository identifiers for the parent document.

observations.evidence: The lower-right corner of the snapshot displays the date "10/13/98."
observations.fit_rationale: The date is explicit but unlabeled, so it cannot reliably be classified as represented data period, production date, or another provenance date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicit organization, office, or attribution statement credited with producing, publishing, or being responsible for the snapshot when distinct from the underlying data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, while source_document_title identifies the parent document rather than the credited office or attribution statement appearing with the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, verification, and interpretation of snapshots whose visible attribution identifies a responsible institutional unit but not an underlying dataset.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link where the parent source document containing the snapshot can be accessed.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title supports identification but not retrieval, and no existing field stores an access link for the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval, verification, citation, and reinspection of the source document from which the snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A repository, publisher, or catalog identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier refers to a snapshot identifier within a document and project_identifier refers to an associated project, neither of which captures document repository identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables disambiguation, joining, deduplication, and verification of snapshots against institutional document repositories.

observations.metadata_concept: Composite snapshot with multiple component visualization types
observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular sections with embedded line, bar, and pie charts titled inflation, export/import levels, current account balance, and composition of total debt.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type can identify a primary or broad composite form and panel_title can name components, but neither preserves the visualization type of each component in a mixed composite snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot page is headed “Jordan,” and the source-document metadata lists ref_country as Jordan with code JO.
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities adequately capture Jordan as the area and named geographic entity represented.

observations.metadata_concept: Macroeconomic and external finance subject matter
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains section headings “PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE,” “TRADE,” “BALANCE of PAYMENTS,” and “EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain and subject_summary can represent the broad macroeconomic domain and summarize the snapshot’s focus on prices, public finance, trade, payments, and debt.

observations.evidence: The snapshot labels indicators such as consumer prices, implicit GDP deflator, current revenue, total exports, imports, current account balance, and total debt outstanding and disbursed.
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name is defined to capture the indicators or measured concepts represented by the snapshot, including multiple values where appropriate.

observations.evidence: The tables show columns for 1976, 1986, 1996, and 1997, and the charts show annual x-axis labels such as 81 through 97.
observations.fit_rationale: time_period captures the represented years and temporal_granularity captures that the values are reported annually.

observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly uses labels such as “% change,” “% of GDP,” “US$ millions,” “Inflation (%),” and “1995=100.”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure, currency, and measure_type capture percentages, U.S. dollars, index values, counts or amounts, and ratios without needing new fields.

observations.evidence: Rows list economic indicators and categories while columns list years including 1976, 1986, 1996, and 1997.
observations.fit_rationale: row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels adequately describe the table organization by indicators, categories, and years.

observations.evidence: Chart legends compare “GDP deflator” with “CPI,” “Exports” with “Imports,” and the debt composition chart labels categories A through G with meanings such as IBRD, IDA, IMF, and Bilateral.
observations.fit_rationale: comparison_group captures explicit benchmarked or paired series, while category_dimension and category_labels capture named debt-composition categories.

observations.metadata_concept: Panel or component titles within a composite snapshot
observations.evidence: Embedded chart titles include “Inflation (%),” “Export and import levels (US$ millions),” “Current account balance to GDP ratio (%),” and “Composition of total debt, 1997 (US$ millions).”
observations.fit_rationale: panel_title is explicitly designed for titles of individual panels within a multi-panel snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English, and the source-document metadata lists language as English with code en.
observations.fit_rationale: language directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Cited data-producing source or institutional source line
observations.evidence: The snapshot footer reads “Development Economics.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source can capture an explicitly cited publication, dataset, or other source from which the represented data originate when the source line is present.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document title and associated project context
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Jordan - Health Sector Reform Project,” and identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P039749.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title, project_name, and project_identifier adequately represent the parent document title and the associated project identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/466121468773744158/pdf/multi-page.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title and represented data source but has no field for a retrieval locator for the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes identifiers such as World Bank D&R “441538,” World Bank GUID “466121468773744158,” and World Bank Entity ID “000094946_99032505565942.”
observations.fit_rationale: internal_identifier refers to a snapshot identifier and project_identifier refers to an associated project, so neither captures stable identifiers for the parent source document itself.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists document_description type as “Project Appraisal Document” and tags include document_type “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title and project context but has no field for the genre or type of the parent document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published as “1999-03-05.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the data represented in the snapshot, not the publication date of the parent document used for provenance and citation.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The visualization or presentation type of each distinct component or panel within a composite data snapshot, such as table, line chart, bar chart, or pie chart.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type captures only the primary visualization or broad form, while panel_title names components without recording each component’s encoding type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and analysis of mixed composite snapshots by preserving which visual encodings are present within the artifact.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other resolvable locator for the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrieval locator, and data_source concerns the origin of represented data rather than the parent-document file location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to retrieve, verify, and cite the source document from which the snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the data snapshot, distinct from a snapshot identifier or project identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for identifiers assigned to the snapshot within the document, and project_identifier identifies a project rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves deduplication, provenance tracking, citation, and linkage back to institutional document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title and project_name identify the document or associated project but do not encode the document’s genre or institutional type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or issue date of the parent source document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period represents the period covered by the data and should not be conflated with the publication date of the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, citation, versioning, and chronological organization of snapshots by source-document issuance date.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]

observations.metadata_concept: Composite snapshot with multiple component visualization types
observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular sections with embedded line, bar, and pie charts titled inflation, export/import levels, current account balance, and composition of total debt.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type can identify a primary or broad composite form and panel_title can name components, but neither preserves the visualization type of each component in a mixed composite snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot page is headed “Jordan,” and the source-document metadata lists ref_country as Jordan with code JO.
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities adequately capture Jordan as the area and named geographic entity represented.

observations.metadata_concept: Macroeconomic and external finance subject matter
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains section headings “PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE,” “TRADE,” “BALANCE of PAYMENTS,” and “EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain and subject_summary can represent the broad macroeconomic domain and summarize the snapshot’s focus on prices, public finance, trade, payments, and debt.

observations.evidence: The snapshot labels indicators such as consumer prices, implicit GDP deflator, current revenue, total exports, imports, current account balance, and total debt outstanding and disbursed.
observations.fit_rationale: variable_name is defined to capture the indicators or measured concepts represented by the snapshot, including multiple values where appropriate.

observations.evidence: The tables show columns for 1976, 1986, 1996, and 1997, and the charts show annual x-axis labels such as 81 through 97.
observations.fit_rationale: time_period captures the represented years and temporal_granularity captures that the values are reported annually.

observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly uses labels such as “% change,” “% of GDP,” “US$ millions,” “Inflation (%),” and “1995=100.”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure, currency, and measure_type capture percentages, U.S. dollars, index values, counts or amounts, and ratios without needing new fields.

observations.evidence: Rows list economic indicators and categories while columns list years including 1976, 1986, 1996, and 1997.
observations.fit_rationale: row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels adequately describe the table organization by indicators, categories, and years.

observations.evidence: Chart legends compare “GDP deflator” with “CPI,” “Exports” with “Imports,” and the debt composition chart labels categories A through G with meanings such as IBRD, IDA, IMF, and Bilateral.
observations.fit_rationale: comparison_group captures explicit benchmarked or paired series, while category_dimension and category_labels capture named debt-composition categories.

observations.metadata_concept: Panel or component titles within a composite snapshot
observations.evidence: Embedded chart titles include “Inflation (%),” “Export and import levels (US$ millions),” “Current account balance to GDP ratio (%),” and “Composition of total debt, 1997 (US$ millions).”
observations.fit_rationale: panel_title is explicitly designed for titles of individual panels within a multi-panel snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English, and the source-document metadata lists language as English with code en.
observations.fit_rationale: language directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Cited data-producing source or institutional source line
observations.evidence: The snapshot footer reads “Development Economics.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source can capture an explicitly cited publication, dataset, or other source from which the represented data originate when the source line is present.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document title and associated project context
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Jordan - Health Sector Reform Project,” and identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P039749.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title, project_name, and project_identifier adequately represent the parent document title and the associated project identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/466121468773744158/pdf/multi-page.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title and represented data source but has no field for a retrieval locator for the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes identifiers such as World Bank D&R “441538,” World Bank GUID “466121468773744158,” and World Bank Entity ID “000094946_99032505565942.”
observations.fit_rationale: internal_identifier refers to a snapshot identifier and project_identifier refers to an associated project, so neither captures stable identifiers for the parent source document itself.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists document_description type as “Project Appraisal Document” and tags include document_type “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title and project context but has no field for the genre or type of the parent document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published as “1999-03-05.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the data represented in the snapshot, not the publication date of the parent document used for provenance and citation.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the source of the represented data and would misstate document provenance, while source_document_title does not identify the producing institution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking and verification of snapshots without conflating document producer with underlying data source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An external, archival, or repository identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is for the snapshot’s in-document label and project_identifier is for an associated project, leaving parent-document identifiers unrepresented.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable linking, deduplication, retrieval, and verification of snapshots against source-document repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web locator for accessing or verifying the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document textually but does not provide an access or verification locator.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, auditability, and provenance verification for extracted snapshots.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and panel or section headings
observations.evidence: The snapshot displays section headings such as “PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE,” “TRADE,” “BALANCE of PAYMENTS,” and chart titles such as “Inflation (%)” and “Export and import levels (mill. US$).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title and panel_title fields can capture the visible section and chart headings, while subject_summary can summarize the composite analytical purpose.

observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular economic indicators with line, bar, and pie charts on the same page.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the snapshot as a composite figure containing tables and multiple chart types.

observations.metadata_concept: Macroeconomic, trade, government finance, balance of payments, and external debt subject matter
observations.evidence: Visible headings include “Government finance,” “TRADE,” “BALANCE of PAYMENTS,” and “EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS.”
observations.fit_rationale: The broad thematic domain and concise analytical summary fields cover the snapshot’s macroeconomic and finance subject matter.

observations.metadata_concept: Represented economic indicators and financial measures
observations.evidence: The snapshot names indicators including “Consumer prices,” “Current revenue,” “Total exports,” “Current account balance,” and “Total debt outstanding and disbursed.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing variable_name, financial_measure, and measure_type fields can describe the represented indicators and their statistical or financial forms.

observations.evidence: Rows list categories such as “Food,” “Fuel and energy,” “IBRD,” “IDA,” and chart legends label series such as “Exports,” “Imports,” “GDP def.,” and “CPI.”
observations.fit_rationale: The category, row, column, and comparison fields cover the named groupings and series used to organize and compare values.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal coverage and annual reporting resolution
observations.evidence: Tables use year columns “1975,” “1985,” “1995,” and “1996,” while charts show annual x-axis labels from “90” through “96.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field captures represented years and temporal_granularity captures the annual reporting resolution.

observations.metadata_concept: Measurement units, currency denomination, and index basis
observations.evidence: The snapshot labels measures as “(% change),” “(% of GDP),” “(millions US$),” “(1987=100),” and “(local/US$).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields can represent percentage, GDP share, US-dollar monetary units, exchange-rate units, and index forms.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic and project context supplied by the parent document
observations.evidence: The source document title is “Rwanda - Community Reintegration and Development Project,” ref_country lists “Rwanda,” and identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P051931.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic, project, and source-document title fields can represent the parent-document context that identifies the snapshot’s associated country and project.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly covers the language evidenced in both the snapshot and source-document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot footer production or release date distinct from represented data period
observations.evidence: The snapshot footer shows “8/28/97,” separate from the represented data years shown in the tables and charts.
observations.fit_rationale: Using time_period for the footer date would conflate an artifact or release date with the period represented by the data.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata states the document type is “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the document genre that aids identification and retrieval.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/848391468777982563/pdf/multi-page.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but lacks a field for a retrievable document link.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly shown in or directly associated with the snapshot indicating when the visual artifact, page, or extract was produced, issued, or last released, distinct from the period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data, so storing the footer date there would distort the distinction between data coverage and artifact provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance checks, version interpretation, and temporal ordering of snapshots without confusing publication dates with represented data periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided by source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not preserve its genre or institutional type, and project fields describe operations rather than document classification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, retrieval, and interpretation of snapshots by distinguishing artifacts from reports, appraisal documents, briefs, annexes, and other source-document classes.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web link for retrieving or verifying the parent source document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title supports identification but not direct retrieval or verification, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the containing document link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to trace a snapshot back to the source document for verification, citation, and retrieval.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
