observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title or primary map heading
observations.evidence: The map contains the large heading “RWANDA.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source document title is “Rwanda - Community Reintegration and Development Project” and the metadata lists World Bank Project ID “P051931.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture the parent document title and associated project name and identifier without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a cartographic map with geographic labels, borders, a legend, and scale bars.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field adequately represents the artifact as a map.

observations.evidence: The map centers on Rwanda and labels Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, Dem. Rep. of Congo, Kigali, Lake Kivu, Lake Muhazi, and other named places.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the main area represented and the named geographic entities shown.

observations.evidence: The legend distinguishes national capital, prefecture capitals, commune boundaries, main roads, and international boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing spatial fields can represent administrative levels, geographic roles, and location types such as capitals and boundaries.

observations.metadata_concept: Cartographic feature layers shown in the map legend
observations.evidence: The legend lists separate symbolized layers for national capital, prefecture capitals, commune boundaries, main roads, and international boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can partially describe locations or categories but do not preserve the reusable map-layer concept or the legend’s feature-layer inventory.

observations.evidence: The map includes distance scale bars labeled “KILOMETERS” and “MILES.”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure is defined for reported quantitative values, while the evidenced units are cartographic scale units for interpreting map distance.

observations.evidence: Latitude and longitude ticks such as 28°30′, 29°00′, 30°30′, 1°00′, 2°00′, and 2°30′ are printed around the map border.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields name places and scope but do not represent explicit coordinate bounds or graticule metadata.

observations.evidence: The note states that boundaries, colors, denominations, and other information do not imply World Bank judgment or endorsement of boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: interpretive_note directly covers explanatory caveats and disclaimers needed to interpret the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot creator or cartographic production unit
observations.evidence: The map note states, “This map was prepared by the Map Design Unit of The World Bank.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source concerns the source of represented data, so using it for the map-preparing unit would conflate data origin with snapshot creation.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot creation or map edition date
observations.evidence: The map margin shows “FEBRUARY 1998.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period represents the period covered by the data, while the evidenced date appears to identify the map snapshot rather than a represented data period.

observations.evidence: The right margin of the map shows “IBRD 25927R.”
observations.fit_rationale: internal_identifier covers a document- or artifact-assigned identifier used to reference the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map labels and legend are in English, and the document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document identifier for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists idno “441998” and identifiers including “World Bank GUID” value “848391468777982563.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and internal_identifier applies to the snapshot, but neither captures identifiers assigned to the parent source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A cartographic feature layer explicitly shown or named in a map snapshot, such as roads, administrative boundaries, capitals, hydrographic features, or protected areas.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels describe data groupings, while location_type and geographic_granularity only partially capture feature semantics and do not retain the map legend’s layer inventory.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and reuse of maps by the kinds of features they contain, such as roads, boundaries, capitals, or infrastructure layers.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The distance unit or units used in a cartographic scale bar or map distance reference.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure is defined for interpreting reported quantitative values, not for map scale bars used to interpret spatial distance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users assess whether a map supports distance interpretation and which units are available for spatial reading.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Explicit coordinate bounds, graticule range, or latitude-longitude extent shown on a map snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: geographic_scope and geographic_entities capture named places but not coordinate ranges or graticule metadata.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables geospatial indexing, bounding-box search, and spatial interoperability when coordinates are explicitly printed on a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, unit, or organization explicitly credited with creating, preparing, or producing the snapshot itself, distinct from the underlying data source or parent document publisher.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source identifies where represented data originate and would conflate data provenance with the creator of the visual artifact.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves attribution, provenance tracking, and verification of visual artifacts such as maps, figures, and charts.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date or period explicitly associated with the creation, preparation, edition, or publication of the snapshot itself, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the temporal coverage of represented data and would misrepresent a map edition or creation date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports versioning, currency assessment, and provenance interpretation for snapshots whose creation date differs from the data period.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional document ID, GUID, catalog number, or repository identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title captures only the parent document title and internal_identifier refers to identifiers for the snapshot rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable retrieval, deduplication, citation, and verification of the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title or primary map heading
observations.evidence: The map contains the large heading “RWANDA.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source document title is “Rwanda - Community Reintegration and Development Project” and the metadata lists World Bank Project ID “P051931.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture the parent document title and associated project name and identifier without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a cartographic map with geographic labels, borders, a legend, and scale bars.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field adequately represents the artifact as a map.

observations.evidence: The map centers on Rwanda and labels Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, Dem. Rep. of Congo, Kigali, Lake Kivu, Lake Muhazi, and other named places.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the main area represented and the named geographic entities shown.

observations.evidence: The legend distinguishes national capital, prefecture capitals, commune boundaries, main roads, and international boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing spatial fields can represent administrative levels, geographic roles, and location types such as capitals and boundaries.

observations.metadata_concept: Cartographic feature layers shown in the map legend
observations.evidence: The legend lists separate symbolized layers for national capital, prefecture capitals, commune boundaries, main roads, and international boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can partially describe locations or categories but do not preserve the reusable map-layer concept or the legend’s feature-layer inventory.

observations.evidence: The map includes distance scale bars labeled “KILOMETERS” and “MILES.”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure is defined for reported quantitative values, while the evidenced units are cartographic scale units for interpreting map distance.

observations.evidence: Latitude and longitude ticks such as 28°30′, 29°00′, 30°30′, 1°00′, 2°00′, and 2°30′ are printed around the map border.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields name places and scope but do not represent explicit coordinate bounds or graticule metadata.

observations.evidence: The note states that boundaries, colors, denominations, and other information do not imply World Bank judgment or endorsement of boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: interpretive_note directly covers explanatory caveats and disclaimers needed to interpret the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot creator or cartographic production unit
observations.evidence: The map note states, “This map was prepared by the Map Design Unit of The World Bank.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source concerns the source of represented data, so using it for the map-preparing unit would conflate data origin with snapshot creation.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot creation or map edition date
observations.evidence: The map margin shows “FEBRUARY 1998.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period represents the period covered by the data, while the evidenced date appears to identify the map snapshot rather than a represented data period.

observations.evidence: The right margin of the map shows “IBRD 25927R.”
observations.fit_rationale: internal_identifier covers a document- or artifact-assigned identifier used to reference the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map labels and legend are in English, and the document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document identifier for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists idno “441998” and identifiers including “World Bank GUID” value “848391468777982563.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title names the parent document and internal_identifier applies to the snapshot, but neither captures identifiers assigned to the parent source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A cartographic feature layer explicitly shown or named in a map snapshot, such as roads, administrative boundaries, capitals, hydrographic features, or protected areas.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels describe data groupings, while location_type and geographic_granularity only partially capture feature semantics and do not retain the map legend’s layer inventory.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and reuse of maps by the kinds of features they contain, such as roads, boundaries, capitals, or infrastructure layers.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The distance unit or units used in a cartographic scale bar or map distance reference.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure is defined for interpreting reported quantitative values, not for map scale bars used to interpret spatial distance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users assess whether a map supports distance interpretation and which units are available for spatial reading.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Explicit coordinate bounds, graticule range, or latitude-longitude extent shown on a map snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: geographic_scope and geographic_entities capture named places but not coordinate ranges or graticule metadata.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables geospatial indexing, bounding-box search, and spatial interoperability when coordinates are explicitly printed on a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, unit, or organization explicitly credited with creating, preparing, or producing the snapshot itself, distinct from the underlying data source or parent document publisher.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source identifies where represented data originate and would conflate data provenance with the creator of the visual artifact.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves attribution, provenance tracking, and verification of visual artifacts such as maps, figures, and charts.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date or period explicitly associated with the creation, preparation, edition, or publication of the snapshot itself, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the temporal coverage of represented data and would misrepresent a map edition or creation date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports versioning, currency assessment, and provenance interpretation for snapshots whose creation date differs from the data period.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional document ID, GUID, catalog number, or repository identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title captures only the parent document title and internal_identifier refers to identifiers for the snapshot rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable retrieval, deduplication, citation, and verification of the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields can describe the snapshot as a country economic, social, and structural overview.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields capture Croatia as the main geography and Europe & Central Asia as a represented regional comparator.

observations.evidence: Rows and chart labels include indicators such as “Population mid-1996,” “GNP per capita,” “GDP,” “Life expectancy,” “Access to safe water,” “Savings,” and “Indebtedness.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field is designed to capture the indicators and measured concepts represented in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot organizes values by row indicators and column labels including “Croatia,” “Europe & Central Asia,” “Upper-middle-income,” years, and male/female subrows.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category and structural dimension fields adequately represent the table rows, columns, and explicit category labels.

observations.evidence: The snapshot shows periods and years including “1990-96,” “1975,” “1985,” “1995,” “1996,” “1997-05,” and “latest year available since 1989.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields capture the represented dates, ranges, and mixed annual or multi-year reporting periods.

observations.evidence: Indicator labels specify units and forms such as “millions,” “US$,” “billions US$,” “%,” “years,” and “per 1,000 live births.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields capture units, currency denomination, and statistical forms such as counts, percentages, rates, and monetary values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot compares Croatia with “Europe & Central Asia,” “Upper-middle-income,” and a note states that diamonds compare country indicators with its “income-group average.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing comparison_group field captures the intended regional and income-group benchmarks without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular country indicators with development diamond graphics and small line charts for growth rates.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type and panel_title fields can describe the composite figure and its explicitly titled panels.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field directly captures caveats and explanatory notes provided within the snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period would conflate an artifact date with the period represented by the data, and source_document_title or other provenance fields do not capture snapshot-level dates.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users distinguish artifact vintage from data coverage and supports versioning, citation, and chronological retrieval of snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated cartographic scale or scale bar used to interpret distances on a map snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure can record the unit of quantitative data values but does not represent the scale relationship or distance guide of a cartographic map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves spatial interpretation and reuse by indicating the distance scale at which mapped features are presented.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, unit, organization, or service explicitly credited with creating or producing the snapshot artifact itself.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source identifies the source of represented data, while interpretive_note can preserve a credit statement only as unstructured text and does not separately identify the snapshot producer.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, attribution, verification, and retrieval for snapshots produced by specialized units or organizations distinct from the underlying data source or parent-document publisher.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The map title, legend, and notes are written in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Source-document metadata gives the title "Croatia - Municipal Environmental Infrastructure Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map note states that boundaries, colors, denominations, and other information do not imply World Bank judgment on legal status or endorsement of boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field covers explanatory caveats and disclaimers provided within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The note says, "This map was produced by the Map Design Unit of The World Bank."
observations.fit_rationale: data_source concerns the origin of represented data, while the evidence identifies the unit that produced the visual map artifact.

observations.evidence: The bottom right of the map shows "MAY 1998."
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the period represented by the data, and using it for the map's production date would conflate temporal provenance with data coverage.

observations.evidence: The map includes a scale bar labeled from 0 to 5 "KILOMETERS."
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure covers units for reported quantitative values, not the cartographic scale used to interpret map distances.

observations.evidence: A lower-left inset map shows Croatia in regional context among nearby European countries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields capture the places named in the inset but not its structural role as a locator or context map.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or organizational unit explicitly credited with creating or producing the snapshot visual artifact, distinct from the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would misrepresent a cartographic production credit as the origin of the underlying represented data, and no existing provenance field captures the creator of the visual snapshot itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, verification, attribution, and retrieval of snapshots produced by specific units or organizations.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly stated date associated with the creation, issuance, publication, or version of the snapshot artifact itself, distinct from the data period represented.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data, so using it for a map issuance date would conflate data coverage with artifact provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables temporal provenance tracking, version identification, and retrieval of snapshots by their artifact date without inferring a data period.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated map scale, scale bar, or distance scale information used to interpret spatial distances in a map snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure applies to quantitative values represented in the data, while geographic_granularity describes spatial reporting level rather than cartographic distance scale.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves interpretation and reuse of map snapshots by recording the spatial distance reference needed to understand mapped infrastructure and locations.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly present inset or overview map that provides broader geographic context for the main map area.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: geographic_scope and geographic_entities can record places shown but do not indicate that they appear in a distinct locator inset with contextual rather than primary analytical role.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports organization and retrieval of map snapshots with embedded geographic context and helps distinguish primary map coverage from contextual overview coverage.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The cartographic scale or scale-bar information explicitly shown for a map snapshot, distinct from the unit used for distances.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure can record kilometers but cannot preserve the scale-bar relationship used to interpret distance on the map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports geospatial interpretation, comparison, and reuse of map snapshots where distance and scale are analytically relevant.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organizational unit, or institution explicitly credited with creating or producing the snapshot artifact.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would conflate artifact production with the origin of represented data, and no existing field captures snapshot-level creator attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, verification, attribution, and retrieval for snapshots with explicit creator or producer credits.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The date explicitly associated with creation, publication, issue, or versioning of the snapshot artifact, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period captures the temporal coverage of represented data and would distort a printed map date or artifact issue date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, version control, chronological organization, and verification of snapshots independent of data-period metadata.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent or repository-assigned identifier for the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a stable retrieval identifier, and internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable retrieval, deduplication, citation, and verification of snapshots through their parent documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Uganda at a glance."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot sections include "POVERTY and SOCIAL," "KEY ECONOMIC RATIOS and LONG-TERM TRENDS," and "STRUCTURE of the ECONOMY."
observations.fit_rationale: The broad macroeconomic, social, and economic-structure subject matter can be represented by subject_domain and summarized by subject_summary.

observations.evidence: The title names Uganda and the data columns include "Uganda."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields adequately capture Uganda as the primary represented country and named geographic entity.

observations.evidence: The snapshot compares Uganda with "Sub-Saharan Africa" and "Low-income," and the notes state the diamonds compare the country with its income-group average.
observations.fit_rationale: Comparison_group captures the benchmark relationship while category_labels and geographic_entities capture the explicit comparison labels.

observations.evidence: The tables show years and ranges such as 1975, 1985, 1995, 1996, 1975-85, 1986-96, and 1997-05.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields capture the years and multi-year ranges represented by the data.

observations.evidence: The snapshot lists indicators such as population, GNP per capita, life expectancy, infant mortality, GDP, exports, imports, agriculture, industry, and services.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field can represent the multiple explicit indicators and measured concepts shown in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Rows list indicators and sectors, while columns list countries or groups and years such as Uganda, Sub-Saharan Africa, Low-income, 1975, 1985, 1995, and 1996.
observations.fit_rationale: The structural and categorical fields capture the row and column dimensions and their explicit labels.

observations.evidence: Labels include units and forms such as "millions," "US$," "billions US$," "% of population," "years," "per 1,000 live births," and "% of GDP."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields capture units, currency denominations, and measure types such as percentages, counts, ratios, and monetary values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular sections with development-diamond charts and line charts for growth rates of output, investment, exports, and imports.
observations.fit_rationale: Visualization_type can describe the composite figure and component chart/table types, while panel_title can capture explicit component titles.

observations.evidence: The bottom notes state "1996 data are preliminary estimates" and explain that the diamonds show four key indicators and may be incomplete if data are missing.
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field directly captures caveats and explanatory notes provided with the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Uganda - El Nino Emergency Road Repair Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes World Bank Project ID "P057007" and project name "UG-UG EL NINO EMERG RD REP -- P057007."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project fields can capture the associated project name and formal project identifier evidenced in the source metadata.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language "English."
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot page date or as-of date distinct from represented data period
observations.evidence: A date "8/28/97" appears in the top-right corner of the snapshot page.
observations.fit_rationale: Time_period captures the period represented by the data, not a printed page, snapshot, or as-of date that may support identification or version context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies the document type as "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: Source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not capture the document class that supports retrieval and provenance context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes identifiers such as idno "693621," World Bank D&R "693621," and World Bank GUID "519721468760234014."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields capture the parent document title and project identifier but not a distinct identifier for the source document itself.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/519721468760234014/pdf/multi0page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title but lacks a field for a retrieval location or access link to the parent document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published as "1998-04-07."
observations.fit_rationale: Time_period describes the data represented in the snapshot and should not be used for a parent-document publication date relevant to provenance.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date printed on or otherwise explicitly associated with the snapshot as a page, release, or as-of date, distinct from the period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The existing time_period field is defined as the period represented by the data and would conflate a page or as-of date with the data's temporal coverage.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps identify versions of recurring snapshot formats and prevents misuse of printed dates as represented data periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated type or class of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema has source_document_title but no field for the parent document's genre or document class.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, and provenance interpretation by distinguishing snapshots from project appraisal documents, reports, annexes, briefs, and other source-document types.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from project or snapshot identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within a document and project_identifier refers to an associated project, but neither captures an identifier for the parent document itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable source verification, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of the document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or access link for retrieving the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Source_document_title supports identification but does not provide a resolvable location for retrieving or verifying the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves traceability and auditability by linking snapshots back to an accessible source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated publication date of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Time_period is limited to the period represented by the data and cannot safely represent the publication date of the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, citation, version assessment, and temporal organization of snapshots without conflating document publication with data coverage.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.evidence: The map heading reads “UGANDA EL NINO EMERGENCY ROAD REPAIR PROJECT.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the displayed heading, while project_name can capture the named project association.

observations.evidence: The source-document identifiers include “World Bank Project ID” with identifier “P057007,” and additional metadata also lists “additional.project_id”: “P057007.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_identifier field directly represents the formal project identifier associated with the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Uganda - El Nino Emergency Road Repair Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the parent document title containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a cartographic map with roads, rivers, boundaries, towns, a legend, and an inset locator map.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the snapshot as a map without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The map title states “El Nino Emergency Road Repair Project,” and the document topics include “Road Rehabilitation” and “Transport.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject and intervention fields can capture the transport, road rehabilitation, and emergency repair focus.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary geographic scope and named geographic entities
observations.evidence: The map is titled “UGANDA” and labels neighboring or contextual entities including Sudan, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, and Democratic Republic of Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema distinguishes the primary geographic scope from explicitly represented named geographic entities.

observations.metadata_concept: Administrative or spatial reporting levels shown on the map
observations.evidence: The legend lists district boundaries, region boundaries, international boundaries, district capitals, and national capital.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic granularity and location type fields can represent the administrative levels and mapped place types.

observations.metadata_concept: Legend categories for mapped infrastructure and physical features
observations.evidence: The legend lists primary bitumen roads, primary gravel roads, unsurfaced roads, railroads, rivers, falls, ferries, towns, capitals, and boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The category dimension and labels fields can capture the mapped feature classification and its explicit legend labels.

observations.evidence: The map margin shows “IBRD 29450.”
observations.fit_rationale: The internal_identifier field covers a document- or artifact-assigned reference identifier for the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map labels and legend are in English, and the document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: A note states that boundaries, colors, denominations, and other information do not imply World Bank judgment on legal status or endorsement of boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field is intended for caveats and explanatory notes that aid interpretation.

observations.evidence: The map includes scale bars labeled “KILOMETERS 0 50 100 150” and “MILES 0 50 100.”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure can record kilometers or miles, but it does not capture that these units are part of a map scale bar used for cartographic distance interpretation.

observations.metadata_concept: Coordinate graticule or geographic reference grid
observations.evidence: The map border shows latitude and longitude degree labels including 30°, 32°, 34°, 36°, 0°, 2°, and 4°.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields capture named places and spatial levels, not an explicitly displayed coordinate grid or graticule.

observations.evidence: A map note states, “This map was prepared by The Map Design Unit of The World Bank.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source refers to the origin of represented data, not the unit that prepared or authored the visual snapshot artifact.

observations.evidence: The map margin states “MARCH 1998.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the date range represented by the data, whereas this date appears to identify the map artifact’s production or publication vintage.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/519721468760234014/pdf/multi0page.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrieval locator for verification or access.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists idno “693621” and identifiers such as “World Bank GUID” with identifier “519721468760234014.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title lacks a formal parent-document identifier, and internal_identifier is defined for referencing the snapshot within the source document rather than identifying the source document itself.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Scale information explicitly displayed for a map snapshot, such as a scale bar, representative fraction, or distance calibration.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure can store distance units but not the cartographic scale relationship or the presence of a scale bar used to interpret map distances.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports spatial interpretation, comparison of map extents, and analytical reuse of map snapshots where distance and scale are meaningful.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A coordinate reference grid or graticule explicitly displayed in a map snapshot, including labeled meridians, parallels, or other coordinate references when shown.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: geographic_scope and geographic_entities describe named places, but they do not capture coordinate reference information displayed on the map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves geospatial indexing, approximate georeferencing, and retrieval of maps by coordinate reference context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, unit, organization, or other agent explicitly credited with preparing, authoring, or creating the snapshot artifact.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would conflate the creator of the visual artifact with the source of the underlying represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance tracking, verification, citation, and differentiation between data origin and visual artifact authorship.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly associated with creation, preparation, publication, or versioning of the snapshot artifact itself, distinct from the represented data period and parent document date.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data, so using it for a map production date would distort temporal semantics.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users assess map vintage, provenance, and temporal relevance when the artifact date differs from the data period or document date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other network locator for the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document textually but does not enable direct retrieval or verification of the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, citation verification, reproducibility checks, and linking snapshots back to their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from snapshot-internal identifiers and project identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier refers to a snapshot reference within the document, and project_identifier refers to an associated project rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports durable identification, deduplication, provenance verification, and cross-system linking of snapshots to source documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Jordan at a Glance."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Composite visual structure with multiple panels
observations.evidence: The snapshot combines tabular sections such as "POVERTY and SOCIAL" and "STRUCTURE of the ECONOMY" with chart panels such as "Development diamond," "Economic ratios," and growth-rate line charts.
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of visualization_type and panel_title can represent a multi-panel snapshot with tables and charts without semantic loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Broad analytical subject domain and summary
observations.evidence: The snapshot presents poverty, social, economic-ratio, long-term-trend, and structure-of-economy indicators for Jordan.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can describe the macroeconomic and social country-profile purpose of the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Explicit indicators include population, GNP per capita, GDP, poverty headcount index, life expectancy, infant mortality, access to safe water, investment, savings, exports, imports, and debt ratios.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field covers the represented indicators, while financial_measure can additionally capture funding- or finance-related measures where applicable.

observations.metadata_concept: Measurement units, currencies, and measure forms
observations.evidence: The snapshot labels values as millions, billions US$, %, years, per 1,000 live births, and % of GDP.
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure, currency, and measure_type fields adequately represent the explicit units and statistical forms.

observations.evidence: The snapshot includes years and periods such as 1975, 1985, 1990-95, 1994, 1995, 1975-84, 1985-95, and 1996-04.
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field captures the represented years and ranges, and temporal_granularity can describe the annual or multi-year reporting resolution.

observations.evidence: The snapshot columns and legends compare Jordan with "M. East & North Africa" and the "Lower-middle-income group."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic and comparison fields can distinguish Jordan as the primary scope and the region and income group as comparator entities or labels.

observations.evidence: Rows list indicators such as GDP and agriculture, while columns list years and comparator groups such as Jordan, M. East & North Africa, and Lower-middle-income.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields capture the organizing dimensions of the tables.

observations.metadata_concept: Population and demographic groups represented or disaggregated
observations.evidence: The snapshot refers to poor population, urban population, children under 5, school-age population, male, female, and population age 15+.
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field captures groups that data are about, while category fields capture demographic disaggregations such as male and female.

observations.evidence: The snapshot states "Note 1995 data are preliminary estimates" and explains that the diamonds show four key indicators compared with the income-group average.
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field directly captures explicit caveats and explanatory footnotes.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document and associated project context
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Jordan - Community Infrastructure Project" and includes World Bank Project ID "P049581."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing provenance and project fields can capture the parent document title and the associated project name and identifier.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text and source-document language metadata are in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type as "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the parent document's genre or institutional document type.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes identifiers such as World Bank D&R "694678," World Bank GUID "294581468773394111," and World Bank Entity ID "000009265_3971104184327."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields refer to the snapshot within a document or to an associated project, not to catalog identifiers for the parent document itself.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/294581468773394111/pdf/multi-page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but lacks a field for a resolvable access or retrieval URL for the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, category, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not capture its document genre, such as Project Appraisal Document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent catalog, repository, or institutional identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for snapshot references within a document and project_identifier is defined for projects, so using either for parent-document catalog IDs would conflate distinct identifier types.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables verification, deduplication, provenance tracking, and retrieval of snapshots through stable parent-document records.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A resolvable URL or access link for the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title can name the parent document but does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports direct access, provenance verification, and reproducible retrieval of the source document for the snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot headings include “PRICES and GOVERNMENT FINANCE,” “TRADE,” “BALANCE of PAYMENTS,” and “EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields can represent the broad macroeconomic and public finance subject matter without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly presents indicators such as “Consumer prices,” “Implicit GDP deflator,” “Total exports,” “Current account balance,” and “Total debt outstanding and disbursed.”
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field covers the multiple indicators or measured concepts represented in the tables and charts.

observations.evidence: The tables show year columns “1975,” “1985,” “1994,” and “1995,” and the charts show annual labels from “89” through “95.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field captures the represented years and temporal_granularity captures the annual reporting resolution.

observations.evidence: The snapshot uses unit labels including “% change,” “% of GDP,” “millions US$,” “mill. US$,” “local/US$,” and “1990=100.”
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure, currency, and measure_type fields together cover percentage, monetary, exchange-rate, and index measurement contexts.

observations.evidence: The tables organize named economic indicators in rows and years such as 1975, 1985, 1994, and 1995 in columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension and column_dimension fields directly represent the table structure, while category_dimension and category_labels cover the conceptual categories and labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Panel-level titles in a multi-panel snapshot
observations.evidence: Chart panels are titled “Inflation (%),” “Export and Import levels (mill. US$),” “Current account balance to GDP ratio (%),” and “Composition of total debt, 1995 (mill. US$).”
observations.fit_rationale: The panel_title field explicitly covers titles or headings of individual panels within a multi-panel snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context of the represented country
observations.evidence: The source document title is “Jordan - Community Infrastructure Project” and the document metadata lists ref_country as “Jordan.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Jordan as the document-evidenced country context for the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot combines large tabular sections with line, bar, and pie charts on the same page.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field captures only the primary visualization and panel_title captures headings, but neither cleanly records multiple coexisting visualization components in a composite snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language as “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives the title “Jordan - Community Infrastructure Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists World Bank Project ID “P049581” and additional project_name “JO-COMMUNITY INFRA.DEV. -- P049581.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields cover the project-level context explicitly provided by the source-document metadata.

observations.evidence: The source-document notes state “Lending instrument: Specific Investment Loan.”
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_instrument field can represent the explicitly stated lending instrument associated with the project context.

observations.evidence: The snapshot footer reads “International Economics Department.”
observations.fit_rationale: The footer identifies an apparent producing or issuing unit, while data_source is limited to the dataset, survey, publication, or cited source from which represented data originate.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document retrieval locator or external identifier
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/294581468773394111/pdf/multi-page.pdf” and identifiers including “World Bank D&R” identifier “694678.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title and project identifier but lacks a field for a retrieval URL or non-project source-document identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists type as “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field identifies the parent document by title but does not represent its document genre or institutional document type.

observations.metadata_concept: Displayed footer date distinct from represented data period
observations.evidence: The snapshot footer shows the date “11/6/96.”
observations.fit_rationale: The date is explicitly displayed but its role is not specified, and treating it as the represented data period would conflate it with the annual data shown in the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The set of distinct visualization or display components present within a composite snapshot, such as table, line chart, bar chart, map, or pie chart.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type is defined as the primary visualization and therefore loses information when a snapshot contains multiple equally salient visual forms, while panel_title records headings rather than visual component types.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports indexing, filtering, and reuse of composite snapshots by all contained visual forms rather than by a single primary type.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, department, unit, or person explicitly credited on the snapshot as producing, issuing, or preparing the snapshot or its presentation.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source describes the origin of the represented data, not the unit credited with producing or issuing the visual artifact itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves attribution, provenance assessment, and retrieval of snapshots produced by specific institutional units.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent identifier, catalog identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document only by name and project_identifier is limited to the associated project rather than the document record or access location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to retrieve, verify, and cite the source document from which the snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional type of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided by source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not capture whether the parent document is, for example, a project appraisal document, report, brief, annex, or other document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation and filtering of snapshots by the institutional context and document genre in which they appear.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.definition: The set of distinct visualization or display components present within a composite snapshot, such as table, line chart, bar chart, map, or pie chart.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type is defined as the primary visualization and therefore loses information when a snapshot contains multiple equally salient visual forms, while panel_title records headings rather than visual component types.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports indexing, filtering, and reuse of composite snapshots by all contained visual forms rather than by a single primary type.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, department, unit, or person explicitly credited on the snapshot as producing, issuing, or preparing the snapshot or its presentation.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source describes the origin of the represented data, not the unit credited with producing or issuing the visual artifact itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves attribution, provenance assessment, and retrieval of snapshots produced by specific institutional units.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent identifier, catalog identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document only by name and project_identifier is limited to the associated project rather than the document record or access location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to retrieve, verify, and cite the source document from which the snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional type of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided by source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not capture whether the parent document is, for example, a project appraisal document, report, brief, annex, or other document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation and filtering of snapshots by the institutional context and document genre in which they appear.
