observations.evidence: The map heading reads "JORDAN COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT GENERAL LOCATION."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The upper-right corner of the map shows "IBRD 28719."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing internal_identifier field captures a document- or artifact-assigned reference such as this map number.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a cartographic depiction with geographic labels, boundaries, roads, legend, and scale bars.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a map.

observations.evidence: The map title names the "Community Infrastructure Project" and the document metadata lists World Bank Project ID "P049581."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name and project_identifier fields capture the project association and formal project code.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Jordan - Community Infrastructure Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the map.

observations.evidence: The map is titled "JORDAN" and labels places including Amman, Irbid, Zarqa, Aqaba, Petra, and Lake Tiberias.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the country-level scope and explicitly named places.

observations.evidence: The legend includes national capital, governorate capitals, selected cities and towns, governorate boundaries, and international boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_granularity and geographic_role fields can represent the administrative levels and roles shown on the map.

observations.evidence: The legend explicitly lists "AREAS OF SQUATTER SETTLEMENT" and "REFUGEE CAMPS."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing location_type field captures the types of physical locations represented by the map.

observations.metadata_concept: Cartographic feature layers and legend classes
observations.evidence: The legend lists feature classes including squatter settlements, refugee camps, capitals, cities and towns, expressways, roads, railroads, rivers, streams, wadis, and boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can capture some categories or location types, but they conflate cartographic feature layers with data categories and omit non-location infrastructure and hydrographic layers as legend layers.

observations.evidence: The map includes scale bars labeled "MILES" and "KILOMETERS."
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure is related to measurement units, but it is defined for reported quantitative values rather than cartographic scale interpretation.

observations.evidence: Latitude and longitude degree labels such as 29°, 30°, 31°, 32°, 33°, 36°, 37°, and 38° appear around the map frame.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures named places and geographic scope but has no field for an explicitly shown coordinate grid or graticule.

observations.evidence: The bottom-right corner of the map states "JUNE 1997."
observations.fit_rationale: time_period would imply the period represented by the data, while the evidence only identifies a date associated with the map artifact itself.

observations.evidence: A note on the map states, "This map was produced by the Map Design Unit of The World Bank."
observations.fit_rationale: data_source captures the source of represented data, not the cartographic unit credited with producing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map note says the boundaries and denominations shown do not imply World Bank Group judgment on legal status or endorsement of boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field captures explanatory caveats and disclaimers needed to interpret the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map title, legend, scale labels, and disclaimer are written in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/294581468773394111/pdf/multi-page.pdf" and identifiers including "694678" and "294581468773394111."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not capture a locator or identifier needed to retrieve or verify it.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Cartographic feature classes or layers explicitly represented in a map legend or map symbology, such as roads, rivers, settlements, administrative boundaries, or facility types.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels treat the entries as generic data categories, while location_type and geographic_granularity cover only some place or administrative classes and do not preserve their role as map legend layers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports map search, interpretation, and reuse by identifying what kinds of geographic and infrastructure features are depicted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Scale information explicitly shown on a map, including a scale bar, scale units, verbal scale, or representative fraction when present.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure is defined for reported quantitative values and does not distinguish cartographic distance scale from measurement units of represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret distances and assess whether a map is suitable for geographic analysis or contextual use.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly displayed coordinate grid, graticule, or coordinate labels used to spatially reference a map.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: geographic_scope and geographic_entities capture named areas and places but not coordinate-based spatial referencing shown on the map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves spatial discovery, georeferencing assessment, and map reuse by recording whether coordinate reference cues are present.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly associated with the creation, production, publication, version, or issuance of the snapshot artifact, distinct from the period represented by the data unless explicitly stated as such.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data and would conflate artifact production date with data temporal coverage.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, version assessment, and historical interpretation of visual artifacts such as maps.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, department, or unit explicitly credited with creating or producing the snapshot artifact, distinct from the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source identifies where the represented data originate and does not capture a credited visual, cartographic, or analytical producer.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, and verification of snapshots when the creator differs from the data source or parent document publisher.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent identifier, institutional identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrieval or verification handle for the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, auditability, deduplication, and retrieval of the source context for extracted snapshots.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name and project_identifier fields capture the project association and formal project code.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Jordan - Community Infrastructure Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the map.

observations.evidence: The map is titled "JORDAN" and labels places including Amman, Irbid, Zarqa, Aqaba, Petra, and Lake Tiberias.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the country-level scope and explicitly named places.

observations.evidence: The legend includes national capital, governorate capitals, selected cities and towns, governorate boundaries, and international boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_granularity and geographic_role fields can represent the administrative levels and roles shown on the map.

observations.evidence: The legend explicitly lists "AREAS OF SQUATTER SETTLEMENT" and "REFUGEE CAMPS."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing location_type field captures the types of physical locations represented by the map.

observations.metadata_concept: Cartographic feature layers and legend classes
observations.evidence: The legend lists feature classes including squatter settlements, refugee camps, capitals, cities and towns, expressways, roads, railroads, rivers, streams, wadis, and boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can capture some categories or location types, but they conflate cartographic feature layers with data categories and omit non-location infrastructure and hydrographic layers as legend layers.

observations.evidence: The map includes scale bars labeled "MILES" and "KILOMETERS."
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure is related to measurement units, but it is defined for reported quantitative values rather than cartographic scale interpretation.

observations.evidence: Latitude and longitude degree labels such as 29°, 30°, 31°, 32°, 33°, 36°, 37°, and 38° appear around the map frame.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures named places and geographic scope but has no field for an explicitly shown coordinate grid or graticule.

observations.evidence: The bottom-right corner of the map states "JUNE 1997."
observations.fit_rationale: time_period would imply the period represented by the data, while the evidence only identifies a date associated with the map artifact itself.

observations.evidence: A note on the map states, "This map was produced by the Map Design Unit of The World Bank."
observations.fit_rationale: data_source captures the source of represented data, not the cartographic unit credited with producing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map note says the boundaries and denominations shown do not imply World Bank Group judgment on legal status or endorsement of boundaries.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field captures explanatory caveats and disclaimers needed to interpret the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map title, legend, scale labels, and disclaimer are written in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/294581468773394111/pdf/multi-page.pdf" and identifiers including "694678" and "294581468773394111."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not capture a locator or identifier needed to retrieve or verify it.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Cartographic feature classes or layers explicitly represented in a map legend or map symbology, such as roads, rivers, settlements, administrative boundaries, or facility types.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels treat the entries as generic data categories, while location_type and geographic_granularity cover only some place or administrative classes and do not preserve their role as map legend layers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports map search, interpretation, and reuse by identifying what kinds of geographic and infrastructure features are depicted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Scale information explicitly shown on a map, including a scale bar, scale units, verbal scale, or representative fraction when present.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: unit_of_measure is defined for reported quantitative values and does not distinguish cartographic distance scale from measurement units of represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret distances and assess whether a map is suitable for geographic analysis or contextual use.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicitly displayed coordinate grid, graticule, or coordinate labels used to spatially reference a map.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: geographic_scope and geographic_entities capture named areas and places but not coordinate-based spatial referencing shown on the map.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves spatial discovery, georeferencing assessment, and map reuse by recording whether coordinate reference cues are present.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A date explicitly associated with the creation, production, publication, version, or issuance of the snapshot artifact, distinct from the period represented by the data unless explicitly stated as such.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data and would conflate artifact production date with data temporal coverage.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, version assessment, and historical interpretation of visual artifacts such as maps.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, department, or unit explicitly credited with creating or producing the snapshot artifact, distinct from the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source identifies where the represented data originate and does not capture a credited visual, cartographic, or analytical producer.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, and verification of snapshots when the creator differs from the data source or parent document publisher.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent identifier, institutional identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrieval or verification handle for the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, auditability, deduplication, and retrieval of the source context for extracted snapshots.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary measured indicators represented in the table
observations.evidence: The snapshot lists indicators such as “Landscapes under enhanced conservation and/or sustainable management,” “Climate resilience subprojects,” and “Grievances registered related to the delivery of project benefits that are addressed.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema’s variable_name and subject_summary fields can represent the indicators and their analytical purpose without material loss.

observations.evidence: Indicator labels explicitly include units such as “Hectare(Ha),” “Number,” and “Percentage.”
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure and measure_type fields cover the stated units and statistical forms.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal reference dates used as table columns
observations.evidence: The table shows column dates “Aug/2025” and “Dec/2030” for each listed indicator.
observations.fit_rationale: The dates can be represented as time_period values, with column_dimension describing the temporal column organization.

observations.metadata_concept: Project component grouping within the table
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains section headings including “Project Management, M&E and Capacity-Building” and “Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_component field directly represents project components or workstreams shown in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Intervention or activity areas represented by indicators
observations.evidence: The snapshot refers to activities such as “enhanced conservation and/or sustainable management” and “drainage and septage management.”
observations.fit_rationale: The intervention_type field can capture the intervention, service, policy, or operational activity represented by these indicators.

observations.metadata_concept: Human population groups represented by social cohesion indicator
observations.evidence: One indicator states “Increase in social cohesion score between refugees and host community members.”
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field covers the explicitly named groups that the data are about.

observations.evidence: The attached artifact is a grid-form table with rows, columns, and section headings.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly covers the artifact as a table.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists the title “Rwanda - Second Phase of the Socio-economic Inclusion of Refugees and Host Communities Project” and a World Bank Project ID “P509677.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly represent the associated project context evidenced in the source metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic project context for the snapshot
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies “Rwanda” in the document title and ref_country entry.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent the explicitly evidenced country context for the project snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Rwanda - Second Phase of the Socio-economic Inclusion of Refugees and Host Communities Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot and source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists language “English,” and the snapshot text is in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies the document type as “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for the parent document’s document type, which is distinct retrieval and provenance context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists document identifiers including “World Bank D&R” identifier “40062872” and “World Bank GUID” identifier “099102225213540444.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has no field for a persistent identifier of the parent document, while source_document_title is not sufficient for verification or unambiguous retrieval.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102225213540444/pdf/BOSIB-3f2311b3-9a20-44d3-b637-b3b2b3d21695.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema lacks a field for a retrievable locator for the parent document, and the title field cannot encode access or verification location.

observations.metadata_concept: Indicator classification acronym attached to an indicator
observations.evidence: The first indicator heading ends with the acronym “CRI.”
observations.fit_rationale: The acronym is explicitly present but its semantic role is not defined in the supplied evidence, so it cannot be reliably mapped or proposed as a new metadata field.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre or institutional type of the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided by source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not capture the document’s genre or type, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the containing document class.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, and interpretation of snapshots by institutional document genre, such as project appraisal documents, reports, or annexes.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent or repository-assigned identifier for the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title is not guaranteed to be unique, internal_identifier applies to snapshot references within a document, and project_identifier identifies a project rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables unambiguous provenance tracking, deduplication, citation, verification, and retrieval of snapshots back to their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other retrievable locator for the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide an actionable retrieval location, and data_source is for the underlying represented data rather than the container document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves auditability and retrieval by allowing users or systems to access the source document from which the snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: The dates can be represented as time_period values, with column_dimension describing the temporal column organization.

observations.metadata_concept: Project component grouping within the table
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains section headings including “Project Management, M&E and Capacity-Building” and “Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_component field directly represents project components or workstreams shown in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Intervention or activity areas represented by indicators
observations.evidence: The snapshot refers to activities such as “enhanced conservation and/or sustainable management” and “drainage and septage management.”
observations.fit_rationale: The intervention_type field can capture the intervention, service, policy, or operational activity represented by these indicators.

observations.metadata_concept: Human population groups represented by social cohesion indicator
observations.evidence: One indicator states “Increase in social cohesion score between refugees and host community members.”
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field covers the explicitly named groups that the data are about.

observations.evidence: The attached artifact is a grid-form table with rows, columns, and section headings.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly covers the artifact as a table.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists the title “Rwanda - Second Phase of the Socio-economic Inclusion of Refugees and Host Communities Project” and a World Bank Project ID “P509677.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly represent the associated project context evidenced in the source metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic project context for the snapshot
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies “Rwanda” in the document title and ref_country entry.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent the explicitly evidenced country context for the project snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Rwanda - Second Phase of the Socio-economic Inclusion of Refugees and Host Communities Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot and source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists language “English,” and the snapshot text is in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies the document type as “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for the parent document’s document type, which is distinct retrieval and provenance context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists document identifiers including “World Bank D&R” identifier “40062872” and “World Bank GUID” identifier “099102225213540444.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has no field for a persistent identifier of the parent document, while source_document_title is not sufficient for verification or unambiguous retrieval.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102225213540444/pdf/BOSIB-3f2311b3-9a20-44d3-b637-b3b2b3d21695.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema lacks a field for a retrievable locator for the parent document, and the title field cannot encode access or verification location.

observations.metadata_concept: Indicator classification acronym attached to an indicator
observations.evidence: The first indicator heading ends with the acronym “CRI.”
observations.fit_rationale: The acronym is explicitly present but its semantic role is not defined in the supplied evidence, so it cannot be reliably mapped or proposed as a new metadata field.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre or institutional type of the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided by source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not capture the document’s genre or type, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the containing document class.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, and interpretation of snapshots by institutional document genre, such as project appraisal documents, reports, or annexes.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent or repository-assigned identifier for the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title is not guaranteed to be unique, internal_identifier applies to snapshot references within a document, and project_identifier identifies a project rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables unambiguous provenance tracking, deduplication, citation, verification, and retrieval of snapshots back to their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other retrievable locator for the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide an actionable retrieval location, and data_source is for the underlying represented data rather than the container document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves auditability and retrieval by allowing users or systems to access the source document from which the snapshot was extracted.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Table 1: Components and breakdown of allocated amounts.”
observations.fit_rationale: The caption is directly represented by title and the “Table 1” portion is directly represented by internal_identifier.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with columns for Component, Allocation, and WHR funding.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the artifact is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Financial allocation and funding amounts by project component
observations.evidence: The title states “breakdown of allocated amounts” and the columns include “Allocation (US$ M)” and “WHR funding (US$ M).”
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of subject_summary, financial_measure, and project_component captures the table’s analytical subject without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Project components and subcomponents used as row categories
observations.evidence: Rows list “C1: Social Safety Net System,” “SC 1.1.: Cash for Nutrition,” “C2: Access to Socio-Economic Infrastructure and Development of Economic Opportunities,” and related component labels.
observations.fit_rationale: The component hierarchy can be represented as the table row/category dimension with explicit labels and as project_component values.

observations.evidence: The two quantitative column headings state “Allocation (US$ M)” and “WHR funding (US$ M).”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure can capture US$ millions and currency can capture the USD denomination.

observations.metadata_concept: Funding source named in a financial column
observations.evidence: One column is labeled “WHR funding (US$ M).”
observations.fit_rationale: financing_source captures the named source “WHR” while financial_measure captures that the column is a funding amount.

observations.metadata_concept: Associated project name and project identifier
observations.evidence: The source metadata title is “Djibouti - Integrated Community Resilience Project” and identifiers include “World Bank Project ID” with “P506969.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has explicit fields for the associated project name, project identifier, and parent source document title.

observations.evidence: The source document title begins “Djibouti - Integrated Community Resilience Project” and ref_country lists “Djibouti.”
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities adequately represent Djibouti as the geographic context for the project table.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic domain of social protection and community resilience
observations.evidence: The snapshot includes “Social Safety Net System,” and document topics include “Social Protection,” “Safety Nets,” and “Community-Driven Development.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain and subject_summary can represent the broad policy domain and analytical purpose evidenced by the table and document context.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the source metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the evidenced use of English.

observations.metadata_concept: Financing instrument associated with the project
observations.evidence: The source metadata notes “Lending instrument: Investment Project Financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_instrument field directly represents the stated lending instrument.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication date as provenance context
observations.evidence: The source metadata lists “date_published”: “2025-02-21.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title does not encode publication timing and time_period would incorrectly conflate document publication date with the period represented by the table data.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source metadata provides the URL “https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099022525185016955/pdf/BOSIB-87c444de-4797-4bf9-b654-4932a7fb0112.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrieval locator for verification or reuse.

observations.metadata_concept: Institutional identifiers for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source metadata lists identifiers including “World Bank D&R” value “34459919,” “World Bank GUID” value “099022525185016955,” and “World Bank Chronical ID” value “BOSIB-87c444de-4797-4bf9-b654-4932a7fb0112.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields cover the snapshot’s in-document label or the project identifier, not formal identifiers assigned to the parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document type or genre
observations.evidence: The source metadata states the document type is “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not capture the document genre that helps interpret the table’s institutional context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date of the parent source document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided as document provenance rather than as the represented data period.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the data period represented by the snapshot, and source_document_title cannot encode publication timing.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, versioning, citation, and temporal filtering of snapshots by the publication context of their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for accessing the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrieval or verification link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document by the publishing or hosting institution, distinct from the snapshot’s internal identifier and any associated project identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within the document and project_identifier refers to an associated project, so neither represents document-level institutional identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves deduplication, citation, provenance tracking, and cross-system linking for snapshots extracted from institutional repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional document type, genre, or class of the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document but omits genre information such as whether it is a project appraisal document, report, annex, or policy paper.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports search, filtering, and interpretation of snapshots according to the institutional context in which they were published.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Table 1: Components and breakdown of allocated amounts.”
observations.fit_rationale: The caption is directly represented by title and the “Table 1” portion is directly represented by internal_identifier.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with columns for Component, Allocation, and WHR funding.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the artifact is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Financial allocation and funding amounts by project component
observations.evidence: The title states “breakdown of allocated amounts” and the columns include “Allocation (US$ M)” and “WHR funding (US$ M).”
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of subject_summary, financial_measure, and project_component captures the table’s analytical subject without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Project components and subcomponents used as row categories
observations.evidence: Rows list “C1: Social Safety Net System,” “SC 1.1.: Cash for Nutrition,” “C2: Access to Socio-Economic Infrastructure and Development of Economic Opportunities,” and related component labels.
observations.fit_rationale: The component hierarchy can be represented as the table row/category dimension with explicit labels and as project_component values.

observations.evidence: The two quantitative column headings state “Allocation (US$ M)” and “WHR funding (US$ M).”
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure can capture US$ millions and currency can capture the USD denomination.

observations.metadata_concept: Funding source named in a financial column
observations.evidence: One column is labeled “WHR funding (US$ M).”
observations.fit_rationale: financing_source captures the named source “WHR” while financial_measure captures that the column is a funding amount.

observations.metadata_concept: Associated project name and project identifier
observations.evidence: The source metadata title is “Djibouti - Integrated Community Resilience Project” and identifiers include “World Bank Project ID” with “P506969.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has explicit fields for the associated project name, project identifier, and parent source document title.

observations.evidence: The source document title begins “Djibouti - Integrated Community Resilience Project” and ref_country lists “Djibouti.”
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities adequately represent Djibouti as the geographic context for the project table.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic domain of social protection and community resilience
observations.evidence: The snapshot includes “Social Safety Net System,” and document topics include “Social Protection,” “Safety Nets,” and “Community-Driven Development.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain and subject_summary can represent the broad policy domain and analytical purpose evidenced by the table and document context.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and the source metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the evidenced use of English.

observations.metadata_concept: Financing instrument associated with the project
observations.evidence: The source metadata notes “Lending instrument: Investment Project Financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_instrument field directly represents the stated lending instrument.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication date as provenance context
observations.evidence: The source metadata lists “date_published”: “2025-02-21.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title does not encode publication timing and time_period would incorrectly conflate document publication date with the period represented by the table data.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source metadata provides the URL “https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099022525185016955/pdf/BOSIB-87c444de-4797-4bf9-b654-4932a7fb0112.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrieval locator for verification or reuse.

observations.metadata_concept: Institutional identifiers for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source metadata lists identifiers including “World Bank D&R” value “34459919,” “World Bank GUID” value “099022525185016955,” and “World Bank Chronical ID” value “BOSIB-87c444de-4797-4bf9-b654-4932a7fb0112.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields cover the snapshot’s in-document label or the project identifier, not formal identifiers assigned to the parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document type or genre
observations.evidence: The source metadata states the document type is “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not capture the document genre that helps interpret the table’s institutional context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date of the parent source document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided as document provenance rather than as the represented data period.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the data period represented by the snapshot, and source_document_title cannot encode publication timing.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, versioning, citation, and temporal filtering of snapshots by the publication context of their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for accessing the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrieval or verification link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document by the publishing or hosting institution, distinct from the snapshot’s internal identifier and any associated project identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier refers to the snapshot within the document and project_identifier refers to an associated project, so neither represents document-level institutional identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves deduplication, citation, provenance tracking, and cross-system linking for snapshots extracted from institutional repositories.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional document type, genre, or class of the parent source document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document but omits genre information such as whether it is a project appraisal document, report, annex, or policy paper.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports search, filtering, and interpretation of snapshots according to the institutional context in which they were published.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web location where the parent document containing the snapshot can be retrieved or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable locator for verification or access.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, deduplication, and linking from snapshot metadata back to the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from project, operation, or snapshot identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: project_identifier applies to the associated project or operation, while internal_identifier applies to the snapshot within a document; neither cleanly represents document-level catalog identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable document-level citation, retrieval, deduplication, and provenance tracking for extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not indicate its genre or institutional document class.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret snapshot provenance, filter snapshots by source-document genre, and compare artifacts from similar document classes.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot and source context

observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document URL for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL "https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099111524150039416/pdf/BOSIB-8191b179-7209-4faa-b5e0-11783bcd492d.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title but has no field for a retrievable parent-document URL.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document identifier independent of project identifier
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R "34423532," World Bank GUID "099111524150039416," and World Bank Chronical ID "BOSIB-8191b179-7209-4faa-b5e0-11783bcd492d."
observations.fit_rationale: Project_identifier captures the project ID, but using it for document identifiers would conflate project identity with parent-document identity.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata states the document type is "Project Appraisal Document" and tags also include document_type "Project Appraisal Document."

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web location where the parent document containing the snapshot can be retrieved or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable locator for verification or access.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, deduplication, and linking from snapshot metadata back to the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from project, operation, or snapshot identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: project_identifier applies to the associated project or operation, while internal_identifier applies to the snapshot within a document; neither cleanly represents document-level catalog identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable document-level citation, retrieval, deduplication, and provenance tracking for extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not indicate its genre or institutional document class.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret snapshot provenance, filter snapshots by source-document genre, and compare artifacts from similar document classes.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is supplied as artifact type `table` and visually consists of rows and columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `visualization_type` field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is `Kenya - Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems Project`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `source_document_title` field directly captures the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists project name `KE-Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems -- P179698` and World Bank Project ID `P179698`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project fields capture both the associated project name and formal project identifier without loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot indicators refer to health services, immunization, skilled delivery attendance, refugee health facilities, and host communities and refugees.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject fields can represent the health and forced-displacement-related thematic context of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Project result indicators as measured variables
observations.evidence: Rows include indicators such as `Number of children immunized`, `Number of deliveries attended by skilled health personnel`, and `Percentage of complaints in the GRM satisfactorily addressed within 4 weeks`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `variable_name` field is intended for the primary indicator or measured concept represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Several row labels explicitly end with `(Number)` and one label ends with `(Percentage)`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields adequately capture number and percentage as units or statistical forms for numeric values.

observations.metadata_concept: Binary response scale for a non-quantitative indicator
observations.evidence: The row label `A vulnerable and marginalized group plan is developed and disseminated (Yes/No)` explicitly uses `Yes/No` as the value form.
observations.fit_rationale: `unit_of_measure` and `measure_type` are related to value interpretation but are defined around quantitative units or statistical forms, which weakly fits a binary categorical response scale.

observations.evidence: The table repeatedly shows column headings `Oct/2023`, `Jun/2027`, and `Jun/2029`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal and column-dimension fields can represent the reported month-year time points and their role as columns.

observations.evidence: Multiple row labels refer to `Garissa and Turkana`, and the source-document metadata identifies Kenya as the reference country.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Kenya as the broader scope and Garissa and Turkana as explicitly represented entities at county level.

observations.evidence: Rows explicitly mention `children`, `host community`, `refugees`, and `People in Garissa and Turkana who have received essential health, nutrition, and population services`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `population_group` field directly describes the human groups that the represented data are about.

observations.evidence: Rows are organized by result indicators while columns are organized by the dates `Oct/2023`, `Jun/2027`, and `Jun/2029`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing structural fields capture indicator rows and date columns as the table’s organizing dimensions.

observations.evidence: A section header in the snapshot reads `Project management and evaluation`, and the document abstract identifies the third component as project management and evaluation.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `project_component` field directly represents the named component shown in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Interventions, services, and operational activities represented
observations.evidence: The snapshot references immunization, skilled delivery attendance, essential HNP services, refugee health facilities supported, GRM complaint handling, and plan development and dissemination.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `intervention_type` field can capture the services or operational activities represented by the indicators.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists `type` as `Project Appraisal Document` and tags include `Project Appraisal Document` as `document_type`.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures the type or genre of the parent source document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including `34266217`, World Bank GUID `099022324094562763`, and Chronical ID `BOSIB-554c314c-bd55-42a2-87c0-9d7e85bc2a91`.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a snapshot-level `internal_identifier` but no field for stable identifiers of the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL `http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099022324094562763/pdf/BOSIB1554c314c0a2187c019d7e85bc2a91.pdf`.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field stores a retrieval link for the parent document, although it materially supports verification and access to the snapshot source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit non-quantitative or categorical scale used to interpret reported values in the snapshot, such as Yes/No, Pass/Fail, or Low/Medium/High when it functions as the value form rather than a grouping category.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: `unit_of_measure` is defined for quantitative values and `measure_type` for statistical forms, so using either for a binary response scale would conflate categorical value domains with numeric measurement metadata.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Allows indexing and interpretation of snapshots that report binary or categorical indicator statuses rather than numeric quantities.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated type, genre, or document class of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: `source_document_title` identifies the parent document by title but does not preserve whether it is a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, briefing, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, filtering, provenance assessment, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent source document by the publishing or hosting institution.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: `internal_identifier` is defined for document-assigned identifiers of the snapshot itself, while `project_identifier` identifies an associated project rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables source verification, deduplication, citation, and reliable linkage between snapshots and their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link for accessing the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval link that allows users to access or verify the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves discoverability, auditability, and provenance verification by linking the snapshot metadata to the accessible source document.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: Rows include indicators such as `Number of children immunized`, `Number of deliveries attended by skilled health personnel`, and `Percentage of complaints in the GRM satisfactorily addressed within 4 weeks`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `variable_name` field is intended for the primary indicator or measured concept represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Several row labels explicitly end with `(Number)` and one label ends with `(Percentage)`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields adequately capture number and percentage as units or statistical forms for numeric values.

observations.metadata_concept: Binary response scale for a non-quantitative indicator
observations.evidence: The row label `A vulnerable and marginalized group plan is developed and disseminated (Yes/No)` explicitly uses `Yes/No` as the value form.
observations.fit_rationale: `unit_of_measure` and `measure_type` are related to value interpretation but are defined around quantitative units or statistical forms, which weakly fits a binary categorical response scale.

observations.evidence: The table repeatedly shows column headings `Oct/2023`, `Jun/2027`, and `Jun/2029`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal and column-dimension fields can represent the reported month-year time points and their role as columns.

observations.evidence: Multiple row labels refer to `Garissa and Turkana`, and the source-document metadata identifies Kenya as the reference country.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Kenya as the broader scope and Garissa and Turkana as explicitly represented entities at county level.

observations.evidence: Rows explicitly mention `children`, `host community`, `refugees`, and `People in Garissa and Turkana who have received essential health, nutrition, and population services`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `population_group` field directly describes the human groups that the represented data are about.

observations.evidence: Rows are organized by result indicators while columns are organized by the dates `Oct/2023`, `Jun/2027`, and `Jun/2029`.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing structural fields capture indicator rows and date columns as the table’s organizing dimensions.

observations.evidence: A section header in the snapshot reads `Project management and evaluation`, and the document abstract identifies the third component as project management and evaluation.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `project_component` field directly represents the named component shown in the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Interventions, services, and operational activities represented
observations.evidence: The snapshot references immunization, skilled delivery attendance, essential HNP services, refugee health facilities supported, GRM complaint handling, and plan development and dissemination.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing `intervention_type` field can capture the services or operational activities represented by the indicators.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists `type` as `Project Appraisal Document` and tags include `Project Appraisal Document` as `document_type`.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures the type or genre of the parent source document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including `34266217`, World Bank GUID `099022324094562763`, and Chronical ID `BOSIB-554c314c-bd55-42a2-87c0-9d7e85bc2a91`.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a snapshot-level `internal_identifier` but no field for stable identifiers of the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL `http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099022324094562763/pdf/BOSIB1554c314c0a2187c019d7e85bc2a91.pdf`.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field stores a retrieval link for the parent document, although it materially supports verification and access to the snapshot source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit non-quantitative or categorical scale used to interpret reported values in the snapshot, such as Yes/No, Pass/Fail, or Low/Medium/High when it functions as the value form rather than a grouping category.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: `unit_of_measure` is defined for quantitative values and `measure_type` for statistical forms, so using either for a binary response scale would conflate categorical value domains with numeric measurement metadata.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Allows indexing and interpretation of snapshots that report binary or categorical indicator statuses rather than numeric quantities.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated type, genre, or document class of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: `source_document_title` identifies the parent document by title but does not preserve whether it is a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, briefing, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, filtering, provenance assessment, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent source document by the publishing or hosting institution.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: `internal_identifier` is defined for document-assigned identifiers of the snapshot itself, while `project_identifier` identifies an associated project rather than the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables source verification, deduplication, citation, and reliable linkage between snapshots and their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link for accessing the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval link that allows users to access or verify the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves discoverability, auditability, and provenance verification by linking the snapshot metadata to the accessible source document.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports precise retrieval, deduplication, citation, and verification of the source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link for accessing the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval location, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the containing document link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the original document for validation, provenance review, and contextual interpretation of the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, category, or institutional type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not indicate whether it is, for example, a project appraisal document, report, brief, or annex, and no other field captures this document-level context.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret the institutional purpose and evidentiary context of snapshots and improves filtering or organization by document genre.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
