CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is a table of project monitoring indicators and associated measurement metadata.
observations.evidence: The snapshot has columns such as "Indicator Name," "Unit of Measure," "Baseline," "End Target," "Frequency," "Data Source / Methodology," and "Responsibility for Data Collection."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can describe both the table format and its primary analytical purpose without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: The represented variables are project results indicators.
observations.evidence: Indicator entries include "Percentage of registered participants completing training and receiving certificates" and "Beneficiaries of job-focused interventions."
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field directly represents the indicators or measured concepts listed in the table.

observations.metadata_concept: The table is organized by monitoring metadata dimensions across columns.
observations.evidence: Column headers include "Indicator Name," "Corporate," "Unit of Measure," "Baseline," "End Target," "Frequency," "Data Source / Methodology," and "Responsibility for Data Collection."
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension and column_dimension fields capture the conceptual organization of a table by indicators and monitoring attributes.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot identifies units and statistical forms for the indicators.
observations.evidence: The Unit of Measure column includes entries such as "Percentage" and "Number."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields adequately capture the unit and count-or-percentage form of the represented measures.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot presents baseline and end target comparison points for indicators.
observations.evidence: The table has separate "Baseline" and "End Target" columns for the listed indicators.
observations.fit_rationale: The comparison_group field can represent the explicit Baseline versus End Target comparative relationship while excluding the numerical values themselves.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot specifies the frequency or schedule for collecting or reporting each indicator.
observations.evidence: The Frequency column includes entries such as "Twice, once upon registration and once upon training certification" and "Once."
observations.fit_rationale: Temporal_granularity describes the resolution of reported data, whereas the evidenced concept is an indicator collection or reporting schedule.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot identifies data sources and collection methods for monitoring indicators.
observations.evidence: The Data Source / Methodology column includes "Completion Survey conducted at least three months after training completion" and "Reports provided by training providers."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing provenance and methodology fields can capture both cited sources and explicitly stated collection instruments or methods.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot assigns responsibility for indicator data collection to roles or organizations.
observations.evidence: The Responsibility for Data Collection column includes entries such as "M&E Specialist" and "M&E Specialist, training providers."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields capture origins or methods of data collection but not the accountable role or entity responsible for collecting the indicator data.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot marks whether indicators are corporate indicators.
observations.evidence: The Corporate column contains check marks for some indicator rows.
observations.fit_rationale: Category fields can describe the presence of a Corporate column but do not preserve the semantic meaning that an indicator is flagged as part of an institutional indicator set.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot includes explanatory indicator definitions.
observations.evidence: Description rows define indicators, such as "Total number of participants receiving certificates divided by the total number of registered participants."
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field can capture explicit explanatory or methodological descriptions that aid interpretation of the indicator.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is associated with a specific project and project identifier.
observations.evidence: The source document title names "Improved Livelihoods for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project" and the document identifiers include "World Bank Project ID" "P178125."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project and source document fields directly represent this contextual provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: The primary population group is internally displaced persons and related project participants or households.
observations.evidence: The source document abstract refers to "vulnerable Internally Displaced Person (IDP) households," and the table lists participant and household indicators.
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field captures the human groups that the represented project indicators are about.

observations.metadata_concept: The project intervention context is training, certification, and job-focused livelihood support.
observations.evidence: The table mentions "training," "certificates," and "job-focused interventions," while the document abstract describes vocational training, apprenticeships, job acquisition, and business skills support.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project and intervention fields can represent the operational activities contextualizing the indicators.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is geographically contextualized to Azerbaijan.
observations.evidence: The source document title says "Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project" and ref_country lists "Azerbaijan."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic fields adequately capture the country context explicitly associated with the snapshot through the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated schedule or frequency with which the represented data are collected, reported, or measured.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: temporal_granularity represents the temporal resolution of data values, not the operational schedule for collecting or reporting them.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation of monitoring tables and comparison of indicators by expected collection cadence.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The role, organization, or entity explicitly assigned responsibility for collecting or reporting the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source and data_collection_method identify origins and methods, but they do not capture accountable responsibility for collection or reporting.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to assess operational accountability, follow-up contacts, and provenance responsibilities for snapshot data.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicit marker indicating that a represented indicator belongs to an institutional, corporate, or otherwise standardized indicator set.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels can encode a column label but not the reusable semantic status of an indicator as institutionally standardized or corporate.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and aggregation of snapshots containing standardized indicators across projects or documents.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is a table of project monitoring indicators and associated measurement metadata.
observations.evidence: The snapshot has columns such as "Indicator Name," "Unit of Measure," "Baseline," "End Target," "Frequency," "Data Source / Methodology," and "Responsibility for Data Collection."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can describe both the table format and its primary analytical purpose without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: The represented variables are project results indicators.
observations.evidence: Indicator entries include "Percentage of registered participants completing training and receiving certificates" and "Beneficiaries of job-focused interventions."
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field directly represents the indicators or measured concepts listed in the table.

observations.metadata_concept: The table is organized by monitoring metadata dimensions across columns.
observations.evidence: Column headers include "Indicator Name," "Corporate," "Unit of Measure," "Baseline," "End Target," "Frequency," "Data Source / Methodology," and "Responsibility for Data Collection."
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension and column_dimension fields capture the conceptual organization of a table by indicators and monitoring attributes.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot identifies units and statistical forms for the indicators.
observations.evidence: The Unit of Measure column includes entries such as "Percentage" and "Number."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields adequately capture the unit and count-or-percentage form of the represented measures.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot presents baseline and end target comparison points for indicators.
observations.evidence: The table has separate "Baseline" and "End Target" columns for the listed indicators.
observations.fit_rationale: The comparison_group field can represent the explicit Baseline versus End Target comparative relationship while excluding the numerical values themselves.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot specifies the frequency or schedule for collecting or reporting each indicator.
observations.evidence: The Frequency column includes entries such as "Twice, once upon registration and once upon training certification" and "Once."
observations.fit_rationale: Temporal_granularity describes the resolution of reported data, whereas the evidenced concept is an indicator collection or reporting schedule.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot identifies data sources and collection methods for monitoring indicators.
observations.evidence: The Data Source / Methodology column includes "Completion Survey conducted at least three months after training completion" and "Reports provided by training providers."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing provenance and methodology fields can capture both cited sources and explicitly stated collection instruments or methods.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot assigns responsibility for indicator data collection to roles or organizations.
observations.evidence: The Responsibility for Data Collection column includes entries such as "M&E Specialist" and "M&E Specialist, training providers."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields capture origins or methods of data collection but not the accountable role or entity responsible for collecting the indicator data.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot marks whether indicators are corporate indicators.
observations.evidence: The Corporate column contains check marks for some indicator rows.
observations.fit_rationale: Category fields can describe the presence of a Corporate column but do not preserve the semantic meaning that an indicator is flagged as part of an institutional indicator set.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot includes explanatory indicator definitions.
observations.evidence: Description rows define indicators, such as "Total number of participants receiving certificates divided by the total number of registered participants."
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field can capture explicit explanatory or methodological descriptions that aid interpretation of the indicator.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is associated with a specific project and project identifier.
observations.evidence: The source document title names "Improved Livelihoods for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project" and the document identifiers include "World Bank Project ID" "P178125."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project and source document fields directly represent this contextual provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: The primary population group is internally displaced persons and related project participants or households.
observations.evidence: The source document abstract refers to "vulnerable Internally Displaced Person (IDP) households," and the table lists participant and household indicators.
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field captures the human groups that the represented project indicators are about.

observations.metadata_concept: The project intervention context is training, certification, and job-focused livelihood support.
observations.evidence: The table mentions "training," "certificates," and "job-focused interventions," while the document abstract describes vocational training, apprenticeships, job acquisition, and business skills support.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project and intervention fields can represent the operational activities contextualizing the indicators.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is geographically contextualized to Azerbaijan.
observations.evidence: The source document title says "Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project" and ref_country lists "Azerbaijan."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic fields adequately capture the country context explicitly associated with the snapshot through the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated schedule or frequency with which the represented data are collected, reported, or measured.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: temporal_granularity represents the temporal resolution of data values, not the operational schedule for collecting or reporting them.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation of monitoring tables and comparison of indicators by expected collection cadence.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The role, organization, or entity explicitly assigned responsibility for collecting or reporting the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source and data_collection_method identify origins and methods, but they do not capture accountable responsibility for collection or reporting.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to assess operational accountability, follow-up contacts, and provenance responsibilities for snapshot data.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicit marker indicating that a represented indicator belongs to an institutional, corporate, or otherwise standardized indicator set.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension and category_labels can encode a column label but not the reusable semantic status of an indicator as institutionally standardized or corporate.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and aggregation of snapshots containing standardized indicators across projects or documents.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is a table organized by results-framework indicator metadata columns.
observations.evidence: The snapshot displays a grid with headers including Indicator Name, Unit of Measure, Baseline, End Target, Frequency, Data Source / Methodology, and Responsibility for Data Collection.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type and column_dimension fields capture that the artifact is a table and that its columns organize the represented metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: The primary measured indicator concerns beneficiaries taking a more active role in their communities, specifically the disabled subgroup.
observations.evidence: The Indicator Name cell states “Percentage of beneficiaries taking a more active role in their communities - disabled.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name and subject_summary fields can represent the indicator and its analytical purpose without loss.

observations.metadata_concept: The unit and measurement form are percentage-based.
observations.evidence: The Unit of Measure column states “Percentage.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing unit_of_measure and measure_type fields directly capture that values are expressed as a percentage.

observations.metadata_concept: The table explicitly compares baseline and end-target states for the indicator.
observations.evidence: The table includes separate columns labeled “Baseline” and “End Target.”
observations.fit_rationale: The comparison_group field explicitly covers benchmark or baseline-versus-endline style comparative relationships.

observations.metadata_concept: The represented population includes project beneficiaries or participants, with an indicated disabled subgroup and document context of internally displaced persons.
observations.evidence: The snapshot refers to “beneficiaries,” “participants,” and “disabled,” while the document title and abstract identify the project as for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan.
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field is designed to describe the human group the data are about, including beneficiaries and demographic subgroups.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is associated with a named project and formal project identifier.
observations.evidence: The source document title names the Improved Livelihoods for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project and the document identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P178125.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly capture the associated project and its formal identifier.

observations.metadata_concept: The represented intervention is civic engagement training and related support.
observations.evidence: The Frequency and Description text refer to civic engagement training, training completion, and receiving training and support.
observations.fit_rationale: The intervention_type field captures the service or operational activity represented by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is contextualized geographically as Azerbaijan.
observations.evidence: The source document title states “Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project” and the document metadata lists ref_country as Azerbaijan.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Azerbaijan as the relevant geographic context.

observations.metadata_concept: The thematic domain includes forced displacement, social protection, education, livelihoods, and skills development.
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists themes and sectors including Forced Displacement, Social Protection, Education, Jobs, and Skills Development.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field captures broad thematic or sectoral domains evidenced by the source document context.

observations.metadata_concept: The data source and collection method are survey-based instruments.
observations.evidence: The Data Source / Methodology cell states that the Baseline Survey, Post-Training Completion Survey, separate pre-training survey, and follow-up survey will be used for data collection.
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field can capture named surveys and data_collection_method can capture survey-based collection.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot states a data collection schedule and timing relative to the intervention.
observations.evidence: The Frequency cell states “Twice, once before civic engagement training and again at least three months after civic engagement training completion.”
observations.fit_rationale: Temporal_granularity covers reporting resolution and data_collection_method covers instruments, but neither adequately represents collection frequency or relative timing.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot identifies the role responsible for data collection.
observations.evidence: The Responsibility for Data Collection cell states “M&E Specialist.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields capture data sources and methods but not the responsible actor or role for collecting the data.

observations.metadata_concept: The parent source document title is available for provenance.
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Azerbaijan - State and Peacebuilding Fund (SPF) : Improved Livelihoods for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: A resolvable source document URL is available for retrieval and verification.
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099730012222232813/pdf/P1781250bdd2b50b0b9720d5c17632331c.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field helps identify the parent document but does not provide a locator for retrieval or verification.

observations.metadata_concept: The language of the snapshot context is English.
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists language as English and the visible snapshot text is in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot includes an explicit indicator description that aids interpretation.
observations.evidence: The bottom note begins “Description: Total number of individuals trained in civic engagement topics who report a higher level of community activity...”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field covers explanatory notes that aid interpretation, and subject_summary can summarize the analytical subject.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The stated frequency, schedule, or relative timing at which data for the represented snapshot are collected or monitored.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: temporal_granularity describes the resolution of reported data and data_collection_method describes the collection instrument, but the snapshot’s “twice, before and after training” schedule is a distinct metadata concept.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation of monitoring indicators by distinguishing when and how often measurements are collected relative to interventions or events.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, unit, person, or role explicitly assigned responsibility for collecting the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source and data_collection_method identify where data come from or how they are collected, but they do not identify the actor responsible for collection.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, accountability, and verification of operational monitoring data snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A resolvable URL or other locator that enables retrieval of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrieval path, and project_identifier identifies the project rather than the containing document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to retrieve and verify the exact source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is a table organized by results-framework indicator metadata columns.
observations.evidence: The snapshot displays a grid with headers including Indicator Name, Unit of Measure, Baseline, End Target, Frequency, Data Source / Methodology, and Responsibility for Data Collection.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type and column_dimension fields capture that the artifact is a table and that its columns organize the represented metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: The primary measured indicator concerns beneficiaries taking a more active role in their communities, specifically the disabled subgroup.
observations.evidence: The Indicator Name cell states “Percentage of beneficiaries taking a more active role in their communities - disabled.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name and subject_summary fields can represent the indicator and its analytical purpose without loss.

observations.metadata_concept: The unit and measurement form are percentage-based.
observations.evidence: The Unit of Measure column states “Percentage.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing unit_of_measure and measure_type fields directly capture that values are expressed as a percentage.

observations.metadata_concept: The table explicitly compares baseline and end-target states for the indicator.
observations.evidence: The table includes separate columns labeled “Baseline” and “End Target.”
observations.fit_rationale: The comparison_group field explicitly covers benchmark or baseline-versus-endline style comparative relationships.

observations.metadata_concept: The represented population includes project beneficiaries or participants, with an indicated disabled subgroup and document context of internally displaced persons.
observations.evidence: The snapshot refers to “beneficiaries,” “participants,” and “disabled,” while the document title and abstract identify the project as for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan.
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field is designed to describe the human group the data are about, including beneficiaries and demographic subgroups.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is associated with a named project and formal project identifier.
observations.evidence: The source document title names the Improved Livelihoods for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project and the document identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P178125.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly capture the associated project and its formal identifier.

observations.metadata_concept: The represented intervention is civic engagement training and related support.
observations.evidence: The Frequency and Description text refer to civic engagement training, training completion, and receiving training and support.
observations.fit_rationale: The intervention_type field captures the service or operational activity represented by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot is contextualized geographically as Azerbaijan.
observations.evidence: The source document title states “Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project” and the document metadata lists ref_country as Azerbaijan.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Azerbaijan as the relevant geographic context.

observations.metadata_concept: The thematic domain includes forced displacement, social protection, education, livelihoods, and skills development.
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists themes and sectors including Forced Displacement, Social Protection, Education, Jobs, and Skills Development.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field captures broad thematic or sectoral domains evidenced by the source document context.

observations.metadata_concept: The data source and collection method are survey-based instruments.
observations.evidence: The Data Source / Methodology cell states that the Baseline Survey, Post-Training Completion Survey, separate pre-training survey, and follow-up survey will be used for data collection.
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field can capture named surveys and data_collection_method can capture survey-based collection.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot states a data collection schedule and timing relative to the intervention.
observations.evidence: The Frequency cell states “Twice, once before civic engagement training and again at least three months after civic engagement training completion.”
observations.fit_rationale: Temporal_granularity covers reporting resolution and data_collection_method covers instruments, but neither adequately represents collection frequency or relative timing.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot identifies the role responsible for data collection.
observations.evidence: The Responsibility for Data Collection cell states “M&E Specialist.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields capture data sources and methods but not the responsible actor or role for collecting the data.

observations.metadata_concept: The parent source document title is available for provenance.
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Azerbaijan - State and Peacebuilding Fund (SPF) : Improved Livelihoods for Internally Displaced Persons in Azerbaijan Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: A resolvable source document URL is available for retrieval and verification.
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099730012222232813/pdf/P1781250bdd2b50b0b9720d5c17632331c.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field helps identify the parent document but does not provide a locator for retrieval or verification.

observations.metadata_concept: The language of the snapshot context is English.
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists language as English and the visible snapshot text is in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: The snapshot includes an explicit indicator description that aids interpretation.
observations.evidence: The bottom note begins “Description: Total number of individuals trained in civic engagement topics who report a higher level of community activity...”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field covers explanatory notes that aid interpretation, and subject_summary can summarize the analytical subject.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The stated frequency, schedule, or relative timing at which data for the represented snapshot are collected or monitored.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: temporal_granularity describes the resolution of reported data and data_collection_method describes the collection instrument, but the snapshot’s “twice, before and after training” schedule is a distinct metadata concept.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation of monitoring indicators by distinguishing when and how often measurements are collected relative to interventions or events.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, unit, person, or role explicitly assigned responsibility for collecting the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source and data_collection_method identify where data come from or how they are collected, but they do not identify the actor responsible for collection.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, accountability, and verification of operational monitoring data snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A resolvable URL or other locator that enables retrieval of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrieval path, and project_identifier identifies the project rather than the containing document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to retrieve and verify the exact source document from which a snapshot was extracted.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays the heading "DETAILS" and section headings including "World Bank Group Financing," "Non-World Bank Group Financing," and "Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions)."
observations.fit_rationale: The main heading can be represented by title and the explicit section headings within the composite table can be represented by panel_title.

observations.evidence: The artifact is a tabular layout with rows, columns, and numeric entries, and the supplied artifact type is "table."
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The table presents financing amounts under "World Bank Group Financing" and "Non-World Bank Group Financing" and a section titled "Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions)."
observations.fit_rationale: financial_measure captures funding-related quantities such as financing and expected disbursements, while variable_name can capture the measured concepts if needed.

observations.evidence: Rows identify "International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)," "Trust Funds," and "Reform and Reconstruction in Iraq MDTF."
observations.fit_rationale: financing_source directly represents organizations or funding sources providing financial support, and category_labels can retain the explicit row labels.

observations.evidence: The source-document notes include "Lending instrument: Investment Project Financing."
observations.fit_rationale: financing_instrument directly represents the financing mechanism associated with the represented project activity.

observations.evidence: The disbursement section title states "Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions)."
observations.fit_rationale: currency captures US dollars and unit_of_measure can represent the million-dollar scale used to interpret the quantitative values.

observations.evidence: The table labels "WB Fiscal Year" and columns "2022," "2023," and "2024."
observations.fit_rationale: time_period captures the represented years, temporal_granularity captures annual reporting, and column_dimension/category_labels capture fiscal year columns.

observations.evidence: Rows include financing sources and disbursement types such as "Annual" and "Cumulative," while columns include fiscal years and amount columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The structural and categorical fields adequately represent the row and column dimensions and their explicit labels.

observations.evidence: The source document is titled "Iraq - COVID-19 Vaccination Project" and includes World Bank Project ID "P177038."
observations.fit_rationale: project_name and project_identifier directly capture the associated operation, while source_document_title captures the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The document title names Iraq and the document metadata lists ref_country "Iraq" with code "IQ."
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities adequately represent Iraq as the geographic context of the project snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document title and abstract describe a COVID-19 Vaccination Project supporting acquisition and deployment of COVID-19 vaccines, and topics include "Health" and "Immunizations."
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain, subject_summary, and intervention_type can represent the health/immunization context and vaccination intervention associated with the financing table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language "English."
observations.fit_rationale: language directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type as "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the parent document's genre or type, which materially contextualizes the snapshot's institutional purpose.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/395791632832896615/pdf/Iraq-COVID-19-Vaccination-Project.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field records a retrievable link to the parent document for verification or access to the snapshot context.

observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name, while internal_identifier is for the snapshot and project_identifier is for the project, so none cleanly represents document-level identifiers.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not indicate that it is a Project Appraisal Document, and no other existing field captures document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation, filtering, and retrieval of snapshots by the institutional document context in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification link to the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the source document, verify snapshot context, and support provenance review.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document by the publishing or hosting institution.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for snapshot references within the document and project_identifier is defined for projects, so using either for parent document IDs would conflate distinct provenance concepts.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves disambiguation, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of snapshots extracted from institutional document repositories.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.

observations.evidence: The table presents financing amounts under "World Bank Group Financing" and "Non-World Bank Group Financing" and a section titled "Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions)."
observations.fit_rationale: financial_measure captures funding-related quantities such as financing and expected disbursements, while variable_name can capture the measured concepts if needed.

observations.evidence: Rows identify "International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)," "Trust Funds," and "Reform and Reconstruction in Iraq MDTF."
observations.fit_rationale: financing_source directly represents organizations or funding sources providing financial support, and category_labels can retain the explicit row labels.

observations.evidence: The source-document notes include "Lending instrument: Investment Project Financing."
observations.fit_rationale: financing_instrument directly represents the financing mechanism associated with the represented project activity.

observations.evidence: The disbursement section title states "Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions)."
observations.fit_rationale: currency captures US dollars and unit_of_measure can represent the million-dollar scale used to interpret the quantitative values.

observations.evidence: The table labels "WB Fiscal Year" and columns "2022," "2023," and "2024."
observations.fit_rationale: time_period captures the represented years, temporal_granularity captures annual reporting, and column_dimension/category_labels capture fiscal year columns.

observations.evidence: Rows include financing sources and disbursement types such as "Annual" and "Cumulative," while columns include fiscal years and amount columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The structural and categorical fields adequately represent the row and column dimensions and their explicit labels.

observations.evidence: The source document is titled "Iraq - COVID-19 Vaccination Project" and includes World Bank Project ID "P177038."
observations.fit_rationale: project_name and project_identifier directly capture the associated operation, while source_document_title captures the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The document title names Iraq and the document metadata lists ref_country "Iraq" with code "IQ."
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities adequately represent Iraq as the geographic context of the project snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document title and abstract describe a COVID-19 Vaccination Project supporting acquisition and deployment of COVID-19 vaccines, and topics include "Health" and "Immunizations."
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain, subject_summary, and intervention_type can represent the health/immunization context and vaccination intervention associated with the financing table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language "English."
observations.fit_rationale: language directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type as "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the parent document's genre or type, which materially contextualizes the snapshot's institutional purpose.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/395791632832896615/pdf/Iraq-COVID-19-Vaccination-Project.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field records a retrievable link to the parent document for verification or access to the snapshot context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R "33446598," World Bank GUID "395791632832896615," and other World Bank document identifiers.
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name, while internal_identifier is for the snapshot and project_identifier is for the project, so none cleanly represents document-level identifiers.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not indicate that it is a Project Appraisal Document, and no other existing field captures document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation, filtering, and retrieval of snapshots by the institutional document context in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification link to the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the source document, verify snapshot context, and support provenance review.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document by the publishing or hosting institution.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined for snapshot references within the document and project_identifier is defined for projects, so using either for parent document IDs would conflate distinct provenance concepts.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves disambiguation, deduplication, citation, and retrieval of snapshots extracted from institutional document repositories.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 1. MPA Program Framework."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The heading begins with the explicit identifier "Table 1."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing internal_identifier field captures document-assigned figure or table labels such as "Table 1."

observations.evidence: The artifact is a grid with column headers and one data row, and the supplied artifact type is "table."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The table columns include "Phase #," "Project ID," "Sequential or Simultaneous," "Phase’s Proposed DO*," financing amount columns, approval date, and risk rating.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing row_dimension and column_dimension fields capture the conceptual organization of table rows and columns.

observations.evidence: The table lists Project ID "P177038," while the source document is titled "Iraq - COVID-19 Vaccination Project" and metadata includes World Bank Project ID "P177038."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name, project_identifier, and source_document_title fields capture the associated operation and its formal identifier.

observations.metadata_concept: geographic scope of associated project snapshot
observations.evidence: The source document title names "Iraq" and document metadata lists ref_country name "Iraq" with code "IQ."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the country context explicitly associated with the snapshot’s project.

observations.evidence: The source title is "Iraq - COVID-19 Vaccination Project," and the table objective text refers to preventing, detecting, and responding to COVID-19 and strengthening public health preparedness.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture the health/COVID-19 domain, the snapshot’s project-framework subject, and the vaccination/public-health intervention context.

observations.metadata_concept: financial measures, sources, instrument, and denomination
observations.evidence: Headers include "IPF, DPF or PforR," "Estimated IBRD Amount ($ million)," "Estimated IDA Amount ($ million)," and "Estimated Other Amount ($ million)."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing financing and measurement fields capture the instrument, sources, estimated amount measure, currency, and million-dollar denomination.

observations.evidence: The table has a column "Estimated Approval Date" with the displayed date "September 24, 2021."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields can represent an explicitly reported date and its day-level granularity without treating it as the document publication date.

observations.evidence: The table includes the column "Estimated Environmental & Social Risk Rating" with the category "Substantial."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field can capture the risk-rating concept and category_labels can capture the explicit rating value.

observations.evidence: The table text is in English and document metadata lists language name "English" with code "en."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Document metadata lists "date_published": "2021-09-28."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a source document title field but no field for source-document publication date, and time_period would incorrectly conflate publication provenance with the data represented in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Document metadata states the document "type" is "Project Appraisal Document" and tags include document_type "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not represent the document genre that contextualizes the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/395791632832896615/pdf/Iraq-COVID-19-Vaccination-Project.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but lacks a field for a retrieval locator needed to verify or retrieve the source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or release date of the parent document containing the data snapshot, when explicitly provided by source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document name, while time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and would distort the provenance meaning of a publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance tracking, version discrimination, citation, and verification of snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not capture whether the parent source is, for example, a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, or other document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves organization, filtering, and interpretation of snapshots by the institutional context in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web locator for retrieving or verifying the parent document containing the data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a machine-actionable locator for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables source verification, reproducibility, citation, and direct retrieval of the document from which a snapshot was extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.evidence: The snapshot is displayed as a grid with column headers and rows, and the supplied artifact type is table.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Role or skill category used as the row-organizing dimension
observations.evidence: The first column header is “Skills Needed,” with entries such as “Gender/Social Development Specialist” and “Administrative support.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent the row concept as row_dimension or category_dimension and the listed skills as category_labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Staffing input measures represented by the quantitative columns
observations.evidence: The table includes the column headers “Number of Staff Weeks Per Year” and “Number of Trips.”
observations.fit_rationale: The measure concepts, column organization, units, and count form are adequately captured by existing measurement and structural fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Operational office base or assignment location for staff roles
observations.evidence: The comments and trip columns include location-basis terms such as “HQ-based,” “CO-based,” and “Field trips as required.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing category fields can record the labels, but they do not preserve the operational meaning that a staff role is based at headquarters, a country office, or in the field.

observations.metadata_concept: Abbreviation definitions needed to interpret snapshot labels
observations.evidence: The note states “CO=Country Office. HQ = Headquarters.”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field directly covers explanatory notes and definitions provided within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source document title is “Sudan - Basic Education Emergency Support Project,” and document identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P172812.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name, project_identifier, and source_document_title fields capture the associated project context.

observations.evidence: The document title and abstract identify the Basic Education Emergency Support Project and describe sustaining enrollment in public basic education in Sudan.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can capture the education-sector context without material loss.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists ref_country “Sudan” and the title begins “Sudan - Basic Education Emergency Support Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields adequately represent Sudan as the relevant geographic context when supported by the parent document.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English, and the source-document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives document_description.type as “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for the parent document’s genre or document type.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/208261588781212409/pdf/Sudan-Basic-Education-Emergency-Support-Project.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrieval locator or persistent access path.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R “32015019,” World Bank GUID “208261588781212409,” and World Bank Project ID “P172812.”
observations.fit_rationale: Project_identifier captures the project ID and internal_identifier is for the snapshot, but neither cleanly represents unique identifiers for the parent document itself.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The office, organizational location, or field basis from which represented staff, roles, or activities are based or expected to operate.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Category and geographic fields can store labels such as HQ or country office, but they conflate operational basing with ordinary categorical grouping or geographic representation.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would improve interpretation and retrieval of operational staffing and implementation snapshots that distinguish headquarters, country office, field, or similar bases.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not indicate whether it is a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, policy note, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support filtering, provenance assessment, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for accessing the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title supports identification but cannot be used directly to retrieve or verify the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would enable direct retrieval, auditability, and source verification for extracted data snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A unique identifier assigned to the parent source document by an external repository, publisher, or institutional document system.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier applies to the snapshot within a document and project_identifier applies to a project or operation, leaving parent-document identifiers without an adequate field.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support precise source-document disambiguation, deduplication, linking, and provenance verification across repositories.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot is displayed as a grid with column headers and rows, and the supplied artifact type is table.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Role or skill category used as the row-organizing dimension
observations.evidence: The first column header is “Skills Needed,” with entries such as “Gender/Social Development Specialist” and “Administrative support.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent the row concept as row_dimension or category_dimension and the listed skills as category_labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Staffing input measures represented by the quantitative columns
observations.evidence: The table includes the column headers “Number of Staff Weeks Per Year” and “Number of Trips.”
observations.fit_rationale: The measure concepts, column organization, units, and count form are adequately captured by existing measurement and structural fields.

observations.metadata_concept: Operational office base or assignment location for staff roles
observations.evidence: The comments and trip columns include location-basis terms such as “HQ-based,” “CO-based,” and “Field trips as required.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing category fields can record the labels, but they do not preserve the operational meaning that a staff role is based at headquarters, a country office, or in the field.

observations.metadata_concept: Abbreviation definitions needed to interpret snapshot labels
observations.evidence: The note states “CO=Country Office. HQ = Headquarters.”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field directly covers explanatory notes and definitions provided within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source document title is “Sudan - Basic Education Emergency Support Project,” and document identifiers include World Bank Project ID “P172812.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name, project_identifier, and source_document_title fields capture the associated project context.

observations.evidence: The document title and abstract identify the Basic Education Emergency Support Project and describe sustaining enrollment in public basic education in Sudan.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can capture the education-sector context without material loss.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists ref_country “Sudan” and the title begins “Sudan - Basic Education Emergency Support Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields adequately represent Sudan as the relevant geographic context when supported by the parent document.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English, and the source-document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives document_description.type as “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for the parent document’s genre or document type.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/208261588781212409/pdf/Sudan-Basic-Education-Emergency-Support-Project.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrieval locator or persistent access path.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R “32015019,” World Bank GUID “208261588781212409,” and World Bank Project ID “P172812.”
observations.fit_rationale: Project_identifier captures the project ID and internal_identifier is for the snapshot, but neither cleanly represents unique identifiers for the parent document itself.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The office, organizational location, or field basis from which represented staff, roles, or activities are based or expected to operate.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Category and geographic fields can store labels such as HQ or country office, but they conflate operational basing with ordinary categorical grouping or geographic representation.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would improve interpretation and retrieval of operational staffing and implementation snapshots that distinguish headquarters, country office, field, or similar bases.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not indicate whether it is a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, policy note, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support filtering, provenance assessment, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for accessing the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title supports identification but cannot be used directly to retrieve or verify the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would enable direct retrieval, auditability, and source verification for extracted data snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A unique identifier assigned to the parent source document by an external repository, publisher, or institutional document system.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier applies to the snapshot within a document and project_identifier applies to a project or operation, leaving parent-document identifiers without an adequate field.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support precise source-document disambiguation, deduplication, linking, and provenance verification across repositories.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid-like artifact with rows, columns, and section headers such as “IDA Resources (in US$, Millions)” and “Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays headings including “World Bank Group Financing,” “IDA Resources (in US$, Millions),” and “Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions).”
observations.fit_rationale: The title and panel_title fields can represent the visible primary and subsection headings without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The visible headings and labels include “World Bank Group Financing,” “Financing Gap,” “IDA Resources,” and “Expected Disbursements.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can describe the project-financing focus of the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table labels include “Credit Amount,” “Grant Amount,” “Guarantee Amount,” “Total Amount,” “Financing Gap,” and “Expected Disbursements.”
observations.fit_rationale: The financial_measure field is designed for funding-related measures, and variable_name can capture the measured concepts where needed.

observations.evidence: The snapshot names “IBRD/IDA,” “International Development Association (IDA),” and “Crisis Response Window (CRW).”
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_source field covers organizations or funding sources providing financial support, including IDA and the CRW funding channel.

observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly lists “IDA Grant,” and the source-document notes state “Lending instrument: Investment Project Financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_instrument field can represent the grant mechanism and the explicitly stated project lending instrument.

observations.evidence: The section headings state “IDA Resources (in US$, Millions)” and “Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions).”
observations.fit_rationale: The currency and unit_of_measure fields directly capture US dollars and the million-unit scale.

observations.evidence: The snapshot includes a row labeled “Chad,” and the source-document title is “Chad - COVID-19 Response Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Chad as the location covered by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Fiscal-year temporal coverage and annual reporting basis
observations.evidence: The expected disbursements section labels “WB Fiscal Year” with years 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023 and a row labeled “Annual.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period and temporal_granularity fields can represent the fiscal-year range and annual resolution.

observations.evidence: The expected disbursements table distinguishes rows labeled “Annual” and “Cumulative.”
observations.fit_rationale: The distinction can be represented as a row or category dimension with labels, and measure_type can capture the cumulative expression of values.

observations.evidence: Rows include labels such as “Chad,” “Crisis Response Window (CRW),” “Total,” “Annual,” and “Cumulative,” while columns include amount types and fiscal years.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields cover the table’s organizational semantics.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists project name “TD-Chad COVID-19 Strategic Preparedness and Response Project -- P173894” and World Bank Project ID “P173894.”
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly represent the associated project and its formal identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Chad - COVID-19 Response Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The visible snapshot text is in English, and the source-document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata identifies the document type as “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the parent document’s genre or type, which contextualizes and helps retrieve the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document URL for retrieval and verification
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/717781588366403375/pdf/Chad-COVID-19-Response-Project.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a persistent retrieval location or verification URL.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R “32002938,” World Bank GUID “717781588366403375,” and World Bank Entity ID “090224b0878b64bb_1_0.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields refer to the snapshot or project rather than the parent document, so using them would conflate document identity with other entities.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not capture that it is a Project Appraisal Document, and no other existing field represents parent-document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, retrieval, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent online locator for the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title provides a human-readable name but not a retrievable location, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the parent document locator.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, and cite the source document for the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from project identifiers or snapshot-internal identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier identifies the snapshot within a document and project_identifier identifies the associated operation, but neither represents the parent document’s own catalog or repository identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports precise provenance tracking, deduplication, retrieval, and verification of snapshots across document repositories.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The visible headings and labels include “World Bank Group Financing,” “Financing Gap,” “IDA Resources,” and “Expected Disbursements.”

observations.evidence: The table labels include “Credit Amount,” “Grant Amount,” “Guarantee Amount,” “Total Amount,” “Financing Gap,” and “Expected Disbursements.”
observations.fit_rationale: The financial_measure field is designed for funding-related measures, and variable_name can capture the measured concepts where needed.

observations.evidence: The snapshot names “IBRD/IDA,” “International Development Association (IDA),” and “Crisis Response Window (CRW).”

observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly lists “IDA Grant,” and the source-document notes state “Lending instrument: Investment Project Financing.”

observations.evidence: The section headings state “IDA Resources (in US$, Millions)” and “Expected Disbursements (in US$, Millions).”

observations.evidence: The snapshot includes a row labeled “Chad,” and the source-document title is “Chad - COVID-19 Response Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Chad as the location covered by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The expected disbursements table distinguishes rows labeled “Annual” and “Cumulative.”

observations.evidence: Rows include labels such as “Chad,” “Crisis Response Window (CRW),” “Total,” “Annual,” and “Cumulative,” while columns include amount types and fiscal years.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields cover the table’s organizational semantics.
