CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 1. MPA Program Framework."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the caption text and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned label "Table 1."

observations.evidence: The artifact is a tabular display with column headers such as "Phase #," "Project ID," and "Estimated Approval Date."
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Yemen - Emergency COVID-19 Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Associated project name and project identifiers
observations.evidence: The table lists "Yemen COVID-19 Response" under Project ID, and document metadata lists World Bank Project ID "P173789,P173862" with project names including "RY-Yemen COVID-19 Response Project -- P173862."
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields adequately capture the associated project names and formal project IDs when explicitly evidenced.

observations.evidence: The table includes columns "Estimated IBRD Amount ($ million)," "Estimated IDA Amount ($ million)," "Estimated Other Amount ($ million)," and "IPF, DPF or PforR."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing financing and measurement fields represent the financial measures, funding-source categories, dollar denomination, million-unit scale, and financing instrument without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot names "Yemen COVID-19 Response" and the document metadata lists ref_country "Yemen."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can capture Yemen as the represented country explicitly associated with the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document abstract states the project objective is to "prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19" and document topics include "Health," "Pandemics," and "Public Health."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject and intervention fields can describe the health, pandemic response, and public health emergency purpose contextualizing the project table.

observations.evidence: The table headers include "Phase #" and "Sequential or Simultaneous," with the row showing a simultaneous phase relationship.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension and category fields can represent the phase and sequencing dimensions used to organize the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Project milestone date represented in the table
observations.evidence: The table includes the column "Estimated Approval Date" and the row value "April 2, 2020."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field can capture the approval-date indicator and time_period can represent the explicitly shown date if needed as snapshot metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Environmental and social risk assessment attribute
observations.evidence: The table includes the column "Estimated Environmental & Social Risk Rating" and the row value "Substantial."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable and category fields can represent the risk-rating attribute and its explicit categorical label without requiring a domain-specific field.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists idno "31933143" and identifiers such as World Bank GUID "106571586194037855" and Chronical ID "090224b0877c9d0d."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title and snapshot-local identifiers but has no field for stable identifiers assigned to the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/106571586194037855/pdf/Yemen-Emergency-COVID-19-Project.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrieval link to verify or access the document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata states the document type is "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can name the parent document but cannot represent the document genre that contextualizes the snapshot's institutional purpose.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published "2020-03-27."
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the period represented by the data and would conflate that with the administrative publication date of the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional document ID, GUID, repository ID, or catalog identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document name, internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot within the document, and project_identifier refers to a project rather than the source document itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, provenance verification, citation, and reliable retrieval of snapshots back to their exact source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web link for accessing the parent document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval location, and no existing field captures links to the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to verify extracted snapshots, retrieve source context, and connect indexed metadata to the original document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre or document category of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Existing fields capture the source document title but not whether the snapshot comes from a project appraisal document, report, annex, brief, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, interpretation, and retrieval by allowing users to distinguish snapshots by the kind of institutional document they came from.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data and would distort the distinct provenance meaning of a document publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance assessment, versioning, citation, and temporal filtering of snapshots by when their source documents were published.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned table identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads "Table 1. MPA Program Framework."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the caption text and internal_identifier captures the document-assigned label "Table 1."

observations.evidence: The artifact is a tabular display with column headers such as "Phase #," "Project ID," and "Estimated Approval Date."
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Yemen - Emergency COVID-19 Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Associated project name and project identifiers
observations.evidence: The table lists "Yemen COVID-19 Response" under Project ID, and document metadata lists World Bank Project ID "P173789,P173862" with project names including "RY-Yemen COVID-19 Response Project -- P173862."
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields adequately capture the associated project names and formal project IDs when explicitly evidenced.

observations.evidence: The table includes columns "Estimated IBRD Amount ($ million)," "Estimated IDA Amount ($ million)," "Estimated Other Amount ($ million)," and "IPF, DPF or PforR."
observations.fit_rationale: Existing financing and measurement fields represent the financial measures, funding-source categories, dollar denomination, million-unit scale, and financing instrument without material loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot names "Yemen COVID-19 Response" and the document metadata lists ref_country "Yemen."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can capture Yemen as the represented country explicitly associated with the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document abstract states the project objective is to "prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19" and document topics include "Health," "Pandemics," and "Public Health."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject and intervention fields can describe the health, pandemic response, and public health emergency purpose contextualizing the project table.

observations.evidence: The table headers include "Phase #" and "Sequential or Simultaneous," with the row showing a simultaneous phase relationship.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension and category fields can represent the phase and sequencing dimensions used to organize the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Project milestone date represented in the table
observations.evidence: The table includes the column "Estimated Approval Date" and the row value "April 2, 2020."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field can capture the approval-date indicator and time_period can represent the explicitly shown date if needed as snapshot metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Environmental and social risk assessment attribute
observations.evidence: The table includes the column "Estimated Environmental & Social Risk Rating" and the row value "Substantial."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable and category fields can represent the risk-rating attribute and its explicit categorical label without requiring a domain-specific field.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists idno "31933143" and identifiers such as World Bank GUID "106571586194037855" and Chronical ID "090224b0877c9d0d."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title and snapshot-local identifiers but has no field for stable identifiers assigned to the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/106571586194037855/pdf/Yemen-Emergency-COVID-19-Project.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrieval link to verify or access the document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata states the document type is "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can name the parent document but cannot represent the document genre that contextualizes the snapshot's institutional purpose.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published "2020-03-27."
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the period represented by the data and would conflate that with the administrative publication date of the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent document containing the snapshot, such as an institutional document ID, GUID, repository ID, or catalog identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title records only the parent document name, internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot within the document, and project_identifier refers to a project rather than the source document itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports deduplication, provenance verification, citation, and reliable retrieval of snapshots back to their exact source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web link for accessing the parent document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval location, and no existing field captures links to the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to verify extracted snapshots, retrieve source context, and connect indexed metadata to the original document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre or document category of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Existing fields capture the source document title but not whether the snapshot comes from a project appraisal document, report, annex, brief, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, interpretation, and retrieval by allowing users to distinguish snapshots by the kind of institutional document they came from.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data and would distort the distinct provenance meaning of a document publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance assessment, versioning, citation, and temporal filtering of snapshots by when their source documents were published.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing column_dimension and category_labels fields capture the conceptual organization and explicit labels of table columns.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing row_dimension field captures that table rows are organized by indicator.

observations.evidence: The table reports separate columns for "Baseline" and "End Target" for the same indicator.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing comparison_group field can capture the explicit comparison between baseline and end target, while column fields capture the table structure.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name and project_identifier fields directly capture the project context evidenced by the source document.

observations.evidence: The indicator refers to "access to basic services infrastructure financed by the project."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing intervention_type field captures the service or operational activity represented by the indicator.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent the explicitly evidenced country context for the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Djibouti - Integrated Cash Transfer and Human Capital Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language "English."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes themes and topics such as "Social Protection," "Social Safety Nets," "Cash Transfers," and "Social Assistance," while the snapshot concerns beneficiaries accessing basic services infrastructure.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields capture the broad thematic and analytical subject context.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing financing_instrument field directly captures the financing mechanism associated with the represented project.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides a URL to the PDF and identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "31019367" and GUID "893891558231269265."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a parent-document title field and a snapshot internal identifier field, but no field for a retrievable parent-document URL or repository identifier.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists type "Project Appraisal Document" and a tag with tag_group "document_type" and tag "Project Appraisal Document."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but lacks a field for the genre or type of the source document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes notes "Project status: Closed" and a tag with tag_group "project_status" and tag "Closed."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures project name and identifier but has no field for the operational lifecycle status of the associated project.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent URL, repository identifier, DOI, or other locator used to retrieve or verify the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name only, and internal_identifier is defined as a document-assigned identifier for the snapshot rather than a locator for the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, citation, de-duplication, and verification of snapshots against their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not capture whether the parent document is, for example, a project appraisal document, report, annex, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves organization, filtering, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated lifecycle or operational status of the project, program, or operation associated with the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: project_name and project_identifier identify the associated project but do not represent whether the project is active, closed, proposed, or in another lifecycle state.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret project-related indicators and filter snapshots by operational status for monitoring and portfolio analysis.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An explicit qualifier indicating whether the represented values are actual, expected, planned, projected, estimated, target, provisional, or otherwise status-qualified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: title, variable_name, and financial_measure can include the words “Expected Disbursements,” but they conflate the measure with its status and do not provide a reusable structured way to distinguish expected from actual values.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, comparison, and reuse by preventing planned or expected figures from being treated as realized measurements.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable URL, repository identifier, DOI, or other formal locator for the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not support unambiguous retrieval or verification, while internal_identifier is defined for document-assigned snapshot identifiers rather than parent-document locators.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the source document for a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre or formal type of the parent document containing the snapshot, such as Project Appraisal Document, annual report, policy brief, or statistical bulletin.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title and project_name do not capture the parent document’s genre, which can materially affect interpretation of tables such as planned disbursement schedules.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports discovery, filtering, provenance assessment, and interpretation by distinguishing snapshots from different source-document genres.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading or caption identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table text is in Arabic, and the source-document metadata lists language as Arabic with code "ar".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with rows, columns, headers, and numeric entries, visually forming a table.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The table includes Arabic labels for human development, health system performance, non-communicable diseases, and child health, while the document title concerns emergency primary healthcare restoration.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain, subject_summary, and variable_name fields can represent the health and human-development theme and the allocation concept without material loss.

observations.evidence: The table headers include "المحور الرئيسي" and "المحور" with row labels such as "التنمية البشرية" and "أداء النظام الصحي".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing row_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields capture the row-based category dimensions and their explicit labels.

observations.evidence: The left column is labeled "%" and contains percentage values including 60, 20, 20, and 100.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing unit_of_measure and measure_type fields capture percent values expressed as a percentage measure.

observations.evidence: The subtitle states in Arabic that there is a maximum of five axes and the total must equal 100%.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field directly captures explicit explanatory constraints needed to interpret the table.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata gives the project title "Lebanon - Emergency Primary Healthcare Restoration Project" and World Bank Project ID "P152646".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name, project_identifier, and source_document_title fields capture the associated project and parent document identity.

observations.evidence: The source-document title begins with "Lebanon" and the document metadata lists ref_country name "Lebanon" with code "LB".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent the explicitly documented Lebanon context for the snapshot’s parent project.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides a URL to the PDF and multiple document identifiers including World Bank D&R identifier "25073592" and GUID "797281467998531842".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a parent-document URL or repository identifier used to retrieve or verify the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type as "Project Appraisal Document".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title and thematic domain but not the institutional genre of the document containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent URL, accession number, repository identifier, or other locator used to retrieve or verify the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrievable or verifiable locator, internal_identifier is defined for the snapshot within the document, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, deduplication, and auditability of extracted snapshots by linking them to the exact source document record.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre or document class of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name and subject_domain describes thematic content, but neither records that the snapshot comes from a specific document class such as a Project Appraisal Document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables filtering, organization, and interpretation of snapshots by the type of institutional document from which they were extracted.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation and reuse of project schedule and procurement-plan snapshots without misclassifying milestone dates as data coverage periods.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a gridded data artifact with column headers such as “Component,” “Sector,” and financial columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of project cost and financing allocation
observations.evidence: The table organizes project components against “Indicative Costs (US$M),” “% of Total,” “Bank-financing (US$M),” and “% of Bank-financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of subject_summary and financial_measure can describe the table as a project cost and financing allocation snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Financial quantities, measure types, units, and currency
observations.evidence: Column headers explicitly include “Indicative Costs (US$M),” “% of Total,” “Bank-financing (US$M),” and “% of Bank-financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has dedicated fields for financial measures, percentages, monetary units, and currency denomination.

observations.metadata_concept: Project component hierarchy represented in table rows
observations.evidence: The “Component” column lists sections such as “Capacity building,” “Improving educational assets/materials,” and “Project Management.”
observations.fit_rationale: The component hierarchy can be represented as the row dimension and, substantively, as project components and category labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Activity or expenditure classification within the table
observations.evidence: The “Sector” column lists labels such as “Training,” “Technical assistance,” “Civil works,” and “goods.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can capture the sector column as a category dimension with explicit labels and, where appropriate, as intervention types.

observations.metadata_concept: Financing source and financing instrument context
observations.evidence: The snapshot has “Bank-financing” columns, and the document metadata note states “Lending instrument: Learning and Innovation Loan.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly supports the funder or financing source and the associated financing mechanism.

observations.evidence: The document title is “Tajikistan - Education Reform Project (LIL),” and the document identifiers include “World Bank Project ID” with “P057953.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name and project_identifier fields capture the project association evidenced by the parent document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context of the represented project
observations.evidence: The source document title names “Tajikistan,” and the document metadata ref_country lists “Tajikistan.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent Tajikistan as the project geography contextualizing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source document is an education reform project, and the table includes activities such as teacher training, pilot schools, and textbooks.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field adequately captures the education sector context of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document title and language
observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Tajikistan - Education Reform Project (LIL),” and languages list “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly includes fields for the parent document title and the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes idno “439558” and identifiers such as “World Bank GUID” and “World Bank Entity ID.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields refer to the snapshot or associated project, not to a formal identifier for the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/555901468777299385/pdf/multi-page.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title but has no field for a retrieval URL for the parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document type or genre
observations.evidence: The document metadata type is “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source document title field does not capture the parent document’s genre or institutional document type.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document or repository record that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined as a document-assigned identifier for the snapshot itself, and project_identifier identifies an associated project rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, de-duplication, repository lookup, and stable linkage between snapshots and their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link where the parent source document containing the snapshot can be accessed or retrieved.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval, auditability, provenance checking, and user access to the document from which the snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre, class, or document type of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not encode whether the parent source is a project appraisal document, report, annex, brief, or other document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, interpretation of institutional context, and retrieval of snapshots by source-document genre.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of project cost and financing allocation
observations.evidence: The table organizes project components against “Indicative Costs (US$M),” “% of Total,” “Bank-financing (US$M),” and “% of Bank-financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of subject_summary and financial_measure can describe the table as a project cost and financing allocation snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Financial quantities, measure types, units, and currency
observations.evidence: Column headers explicitly include “Indicative Costs (US$M),” “% of Total,” “Bank-financing (US$M),” and “% of Bank-financing.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has dedicated fields for financial measures, percentages, monetary units, and currency denomination.

observations.metadata_concept: Project component hierarchy represented in table rows
observations.evidence: The “Component” column lists sections such as “Capacity building,” “Improving educational assets/materials,” and “Project Management.”
observations.fit_rationale: The component hierarchy can be represented as the row dimension and, substantively, as project components and category labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Activity or expenditure classification within the table
observations.evidence: The “Sector” column lists labels such as “Training,” “Technical assistance,” “Civil works,” and “goods.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can capture the sector column as a category dimension with explicit labels and, where appropriate, as intervention types.

observations.metadata_concept: Financing source and financing instrument context
observations.evidence: The snapshot has “Bank-financing” columns, and the document metadata note states “Lending instrument: Learning and Innovation Loan.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly supports the funder or financing source and the associated financing mechanism.

observations.evidence: The document title is “Tajikistan - Education Reform Project (LIL),” and the document identifiers include “World Bank Project ID” with “P057953.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name and project_identifier fields capture the project association evidenced by the parent document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context of the represented project
observations.evidence: The source document title names “Tajikistan,” and the document metadata ref_country lists “Tajikistan.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent Tajikistan as the project geography contextualizing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source document is an education reform project, and the table includes activities such as teacher training, pilot schools, and textbooks.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field adequately captures the education sector context of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document title and language
observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Tajikistan - Education Reform Project (LIL),” and languages list “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly includes fields for the parent document title and the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes idno “439558” and identifiers such as “World Bank GUID” and “World Bank Entity ID.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing identifier fields refer to the snapshot or associated project, not to a formal identifier for the parent source document.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/555901468777299385/pdf/multi-page.pdf.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title but has no field for a retrieval URL for the parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source document type or genre
observations.evidence: The document metadata type is “Project Appraisal Document.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source document title field does not capture the parent document’s genre or institutional document type.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document or repository record that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is defined as a document-assigned identifier for the snapshot itself, and project_identifier identifies an associated project rather than the parent document record.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, de-duplication, repository lookup, and stable linkage between snapshots and their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link where the parent source document containing the snapshot can be accessed or retrieved.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval, auditability, provenance checking, and user access to the document from which the snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre, class, or document type of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not encode whether the parent source is a project appraisal document, report, annex, brief, or other document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves filtering, interpretation of institutional context, and retrieval of snapshots by source-document genre.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned annex identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Annex 7: Project Processing Schedule.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the schedule heading and internal_identifier captures the annex number without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot subtitle states “WEST BANK AND GAZA: Second Community Development Project,” and the source-document title is “West Bank and Gaza - Second Community Development Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_name field directly represents the project or operation associated with the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document identifiers include “World Bank Project ID” with identifier “P058684,” and additional metadata lists “additional.project_id”: “P058684.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing project_identifier field directly captures the formal identifier assigned to the associated project.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of the snapshot
observations.evidence: The snapshot presents a “Project Processing Schedule” with milestones such as first Bank mission, appraisal mission departure, negotiations, and planned date of effectiveness.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary and variable_name fields can represent that the snapshot summarizes project processing milestones and schedule timing.

observations.evidence: The table columns are labeled “Planned” and “Actual.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing comparison_group field captures the explicit planned-versus-actual comparison, while column_dimension captures the table column organization.

observations.evidence: The first table column is labeled “Project Schedule” and lists milestone rows including “First Bank mission (identification),” “Appraisal mission departure,” and “Negotiations.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing row_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the milestone dimension and its explicit labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal dates and duration represented in the table
observations.evidence: The table includes dates such as “09/15/98,” “02/02/99,” and “04/30/99,” and a row labeled “Time taken to prepare the project (months).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal and measurement fields can capture the represented 1998–1999 date range, date-level reporting, and months as a unit.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with labeled rows and columns under “Project Schedule,” “Planned,” and “Actual.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents the artifact as a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope of the associated project
observations.evidence: The snapshot subtitle begins “WEST BANK AND GAZA,” and document metadata lists ref_country name “West Bank and Gaza.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields adequately capture West Bank and Gaza as the represented project geography.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “West Bank and Gaza - Second Community Development Project.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English, and document metadata lists language name “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Below the table the snapshot states “Prepared by: Kanthan Shankar” and “Preparation assistance: Fifi Antar.”
observations.fit_rationale: The credited preparer and preparation assistant are provenance or authorship credits for the snapshot rather than the source of represented data or an interpretive note.

observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/573471468763473544/pdf/multi-page.pdf” and identifiers including “World Bank D&R” identifier “439541.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field identifies the parent document by name but does not capture a retrieval URL or repository identifier needed to locate or verify the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Person or organization explicitly credited with preparing, authoring, assisting, or otherwise contributing to the creation of the snapshot, preserving the stated contribution role when available.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source refers to the origin of the represented data, and interpretive_note captures explanatory caveats or methodological remarks, so neither adequately represents human preparation or assistance credits printed with the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, accountability, and retrieval or verification workflows for snapshots that include explicit authorship or preparation credits.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent link, repository identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title captures only the parent document name and does not provide a stable locator or repository identifier for retrieval and verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves traceability from a snapshot back to its source document and supports source verification in indexed collections.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL “http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/573471468763473544/pdf/multi-page.pdf” and identifiers including “World Bank D&R” identifier “439541.”

candidate_new_fields.definition: Person or organization explicitly credited with preparing, authoring, assisting, or otherwise contributing to the creation of the snapshot, preserving the stated contribution role when available.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source refers to the origin of the represented data, and interpretive_note captures explanatory caveats or methodological remarks, so neither adequately represents human preparation or assistance credits printed with the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance, accountability, and retrieval or verification workflows for snapshots that include explicit authorship or preparation credits.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent link, repository identifier, or other locator that enables retrieval or verification of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title captures only the parent document name and does not provide a stable locator or repository identifier for retrieval and verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves traceability from a snapshot back to its source document and supports source verification in indexed collections.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or web locator for the parent source document from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a machine-actionable locator for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source retrieval, auditability, and verification of extracted snapshots against the original document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal institutional identifier assigned to the parent source document, distinct from a snapshot internal identifier or project identifier.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier applies to the snapshot within a document and project_identifier applies to an associated project, while neither captures identifiers assigned to the parent document itself.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves deduplication, citation, provenance tracking, and cross-system retrieval of snapshots by their parent documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The institutional genre or document type of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not encode its type, such as a project appraisal document, report, annex, or policy paper.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users interpret the administrative context and evidentiary role of a snapshot and filter snapshots by source-document genre.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the period represented by the data and would misrepresent a document publication date if used for source-document provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, version assessment, provenance review, and chronological organization of snapshots by source-document publication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly represent the associated project and its formal identifier.

observations.evidence: The document notes state "Lending instrument: Specific Investment Loan."
observations.fit_rationale: The financing_instrument field covers the explicitly stated lending mechanism associated with the represented project.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document title and snapshot language
observations.evidence: The document metadata title is "Cambodia - Social Fund II Project" and the language metadata lists "English."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema directly includes fields for the parent document title and the language used in the snapshot or document context.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document identifier or retrieval locator
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes idno "442357," a World Bank GUID "932001468769834027," and URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/932001468769834027/pdf/multi-page.pdf."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document only by title and has no field for a persistent document identifier or retrieval locator.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A persistent identifier, accession number, or retrieval locator assigned to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title can identify the document by name but cannot disambiguate, retrieve, or verify the exact source document when titles are reused or variants exist.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance verification, source retrieval, deduplication, and reliable linking from a snapshot back to its parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The document genre, type, or institutional publication category of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title does not encode whether the snapshot comes from a project appraisal document, report, annex, or other document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves interpretation, filtering, and retrieval by distinguishing the institutional context and purpose of the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, creation, or release date of the parent source document, when explicitly provided as document metadata rather than as the data period represented by the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the date range represented by the data, and using it for document publication date would distort the snapshot's temporal semantics.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, version context, citation, and chronological organization of snapshots without confusing document dates with represented data periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization or person responsible for producing, publishing, or supplying the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source refers to the origin of the represented data, while source_document_title identifies only the document and not the entity responsible for the document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports attribution, provenance assessment, source filtering, and verification of the institutional origin of snapshots.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
