observations.evidence: The attached artifact is a tabular display with row labels and two numeric columns headed "Current Situation (1997)" and "Future Situation (2002)."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Measured concepts represented in the table
observations.evidence: The row labels include "Domestic tariff per m3," "Billed annual water consumption," "Annual charges per household," average Category I and II income, and water charges as percentages of income.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field covers the explicit indicators or measured concepts, while subject_summary can summarize their analytical purpose.

observations.metadata_concept: Table row organization by indicator or measure
observations.evidence: Each table row names a different water, tariff, charge, income, or affordability measure.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension field directly represents the conceptual variable organized by table rows, and category_dimension can also describe the indicator grouping.

observations.metadata_concept: Column organization by current and future situation
observations.evidence: The two column headers are "Current Situation (1997)" and "Future Situation (2002)."
observations.fit_rationale: The column_dimension and category_dimension fields can capture that columns organize values by situation status.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal years represented by the table
observations.evidence: The column headers explicitly include the years "1997" and "2002."
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field directly captures the years represented by the data without needing to infer document dates.

observations.metadata_concept: Explicit comparison between current and future situations
observations.evidence: The table presents side-by-side columns for "Current Situation (1997)" and "Future Situation (2002)."
observations.fit_rationale: The comparison_group field covers the intended comparison between current and future scenarios.

observations.metadata_concept: Units and currency used to interpret values
observations.evidence: Row labels specify units such as "in HRK," "in m3," and "percentage of."
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure, currency, and measure_type fields capture cubic meters, Croatian kuna, and percentage expressions.

observations.evidence: The table includes "Annual charges per household" and rows for "Category I average income" and "Category II average income."
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group and category fields can represent households and the explicitly labeled income categories.

observations.metadata_concept: Water supply, wastewater, and municipal environmental infrastructure subject matter
observations.evidence: The snapshot discusses water tariff, water consumption, and water charges, and the source document title is "Croatia - Municipal Environmental Infrastructure Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields cover the thematic water and municipal infrastructure context, with intervention_type available for represented services.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic context of the represented project
observations.evidence: The source document title begins "Croatia - Municipal Environmental Infrastructure Project" and the document metadata lists ref_country as "Croatia."
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can capture Croatia as the explicitly documented project geography.

observations.metadata_concept: Associated project name and project identifier
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists "World Bank Project ID" as "P043444" and additional.project_name as "HR-Municipal Environmental Infrastructure Project -- P043444."
observations.fit_rationale: The project_name and project_identifier fields directly represent the associated project and its formal identifier.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is "Croatia - Municipal Environmental Infrastructure Project."
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The visible table text is in English, including labels such as "Current Situation" and "Annual charges per household."
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists document_description.type as "Project Appraisal Document" and includes a document_type tag with the same value.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the document genre that contextualizes how the snapshot should be interpreted.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists identifiers including World Bank D&R "693517," World Bank GUID "367181468770702078," and World Bank Project ID "P043444."
observations.fit_rationale: Project_identifier captures only the project ID and source_document_title is not a stable document identifier, so using them would conflate project and document provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval locator for the parent document
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL "http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/367181468770702078/pdf/multi0page.pdf" and related format links.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but lacks a field for a retrieval URL or locator needed to verify the snapshot source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, class, or institutional document type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not represent whether it is a Project Appraisal Document, report, annex, brief, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation, filtering, and retrieval of snapshots by the institutional context in which they appeared.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A stable identifier assigned to the parent document by the publishing institution or repository.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: project_identifier applies to the associated project rather than the source document, and source_document_title is not unique or stable enough for document-level provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables reliable source-document disambiguation, provenance tracking, deduplication, and verification of extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or other resolvable locator for accessing the parent document or its source-repository record.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a retrieval path for confirming or reaccessing the source of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, auditability, retrieval, and reproducibility of snapshot extraction.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for the parent document or source file containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title names the parent document but does not provide a resolvable locator for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, and cite the parent document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional entity credited with authoring, producing, publishing, or otherwise creating the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the source of the represented data, not the creator or author of the parent document, so it would misstate provenance when document attribution is evidenced but data origin is not.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, attribution, filtering by issuing organization, and verification of snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.fit_rationale: The category_dimension and category_labels fields capture both the organizing dimension and its explicit category labels.

observations.evidence: The title states that the data concern impacts “since 1 January 2018.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field can represent the explicitly stated open-ended period beginning on 1 January 2018.

observations.evidence: The chart shows numeric counts for incidents, casualties, and fatalities along a quantitative y-axis.
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type field captures that values are counts, while unit_of_measure can record the counted entities where explicitly named.

observations.evidence: The title states that the armed violence is “impacting civilian houses.”
observations.fit_rationale: The location_type field can represent civilian houses as the type of physical location affected.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing population_group field captures the human household groups that the data are about.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field adequately represents the chart as a bar chart.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Indicates whether and how the snapshot visually represents uncertainty, variability, or precision, when explicitly shown or labeled.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Existing fields describe variables, methods, notes, and visualization type, but none capture explicit uncertainty markers as a reusable interpretive feature.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports discovery and interpretation of snapshots that include uncertainty or variability information without extracting statistical values.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link for accessing or verifying the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide an access path for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve the source document and validate snapshot provenance.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization or person credited with creating, authoring, publishing, or providing the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly stated.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the source of the represented data and would distort parent-document attribution, while source_document_title records only the document name.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, and retrieval by distinguishing who produced the containing document from the source of the data values.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Periodic Analysis of Syrian Workers Outside Camps - Findings - October 2018".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot labels show "Usual working sector" organized by "Type of work permit".
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_summary field can concisely describe the chart as the distribution of usual working sectors by type of work permit.

observations.evidence: The snapshot references work permits and usual working sectors, and the source title refers to Syrian workers outside camps.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field adequately captures the broad labor or employment domain represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: Bars are labeled with percentage values for sector categories within work permit groups.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field can represent the primary measured concept as the percentage or share of workers by usual working sector.

observations.evidence: The bar labels use percent signs such as "85%" and "95%".
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure and measure_type fields directly capture that values are expressed as percentages.

observations.evidence: The chart includes the dimension labels "Usual working sector" and "Type of work permit".
observations.fit_rationale: The category_dimension field is defined to capture conceptual dimensions used to organize, group, or compare represented values.

observations.evidence: Visible labels include "Construction union GFJTU," "Private/public employer," "Construction," "Retail and wholesale," "Agriculture," and "Other".
observations.fit_rationale: The category_labels field directly represents explicit category names associated with the chart dimensions.

observations.evidence: The snapshot shows vertical bars encoding percentage values across categories.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly captures the snapshot as a bar chart.

observations.metadata_concept: Human population group represented by context
observations.evidence: The source-document title states "Syrian Workers Outside Camps".
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field is intended to describe the human group that the represented data are about.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists ref_country entries "Jordan" and "Syrian Arab Republic" and additional primary_country "Jordan".
observations.fit_rationale: Existing geographic fields can represent the named geographic entities and any explicitly stated geographic role without adding a new field.

observations.metadata_concept: Language of snapshot and source context
observations.evidence: The chart labels are in English and the document metadata lists language "English".
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Ambiguous temporal context in document title
observations.evidence: The source-document title ends with "Findings - October 2018".
observations.fit_rationale: The evidence may indicate a findings or report reference date rather than the data period represented by the chart, so applying time_period is not reliable.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF URL for the parent document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable source-document URL used to verify or access the snapshot context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL for accessing the parent source document or its landing page from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrievable location, and data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than access to the containing document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, provenance tracing, and linking from an indexed snapshot back to its source context.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.fit_rationale: subject_summary and variable_name can represent the snapshot's purpose and measured concept without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The y-axis lists categories such as Shelter, Non-food items, Legal assistance, Child protection, and Cash.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can capture the organizing service dimension, its explicit labels, and the represented intervention or service types.

observations.evidence: The legend compares "Displaced Yemenis and host community members" with "Refugees and Asylum seekers in the north."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture the human groups represented and the explicit comparative relationship between them.

observations.evidence: The x-axis is labeled from 0% to 100%.
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure and measure_type adequately represent that values are expressed as percentages.

observations.evidence: The snapshot uses paired horizontal bars for each service category.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type directly captures the snapshot as a horizontal bar chart.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists ref_country as Yemen, and the snapshot legend refers to refugees and asylum seekers "in the north."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent Yemen as the geographic scope or entity and the location qualifier through existing geographic context fields.

observations.evidence: The source-document title is "Understanding how UNHCR engages with communities in Yemen: Community engagement survey report (September 2020)."
observations.fit_rationale: data_collection_method can capture the explicitly stated survey basis of the report containing the snapshot.

observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain can represent the broad humanitarian coordination and protection domain evidenced by the document and snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Understanding how UNHCR engages with communities in Yemen: Community engagement survey report (September 2020)."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title directly represents the parent document title containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The chart text is in English and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: language directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing v1.1 field captures a retrievable URL for the parent document or attachment needed to verify the snapshot source.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication or posting date
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata records date_published as 2025-09-24 and additional posted/originally_published as 24 Sep 2025.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures the parent document publication date, and time_period would incorrectly conflate publication timing with the data period represented by the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: URL or URLs where the parent source document or its official attachment can be accessed for retrieval and verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support direct retrieval, while data_source refers to the origin of represented data rather than the location of the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the document from which a snapshot was extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, or release date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the represented data period and would distort semantics if used for document publication timing; no source-document date field exists in v1.1.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, version disambiguation, provenance tracking, and temporal filtering of snapshots by source-document release date.

observations.evidence: The chart presents responses about services and assistance respondents know are provided by UNHCR.
observations.fit_rationale: subject_summary and variable_name can represent the snapshot's purpose and measured concept without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The y-axis lists categories such as Shelter, Non-food items, Legal assistance, Child protection, and Cash.

observations.metadata_concept: Respondent population groups and explicit comparison
observations.evidence: The legend compares "Displaced Yemenis and host community members" with "Refugees and Asylum seekers in the north."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture the human groups represented and the explicit comparative relationship between them.

observations.evidence: The x-axis is labeled from 0% to 100%.
observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure and measure_type adequately represent that values are expressed as percentages.

observations.evidence: The snapshot uses paired horizontal bars for each service category.
observations.fit_rationale: visualization_type directly captures the snapshot as a horizontal bar chart.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists ref_country as Yemen, and the snapshot legend refers to refugees and asylum seekers "in the north."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent Yemen as the geographic scope or entity and the location qualifier through existing geographic context fields.

observations.evidence: The source-document title is "Understanding how UNHCR engages with communities in Yemen: Community engagement survey report (September 2020)."
observations.fit_rationale: data_collection_method can capture the explicitly stated survey basis of the report containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document themes are "Coordination" and "Protection and Human Rights," and the chart concerns UNHCR services and assistance.
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain can represent the broad humanitarian coordination and protection domain evidenced by the document and snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Understanding how UNHCR engages with communities in Yemen: Community engagement survey report (September 2020)."
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title directly represents the parent document title containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The chart text is in English and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: language directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing v1.1 field captures a retrievable URL for the parent document or attachment needed to verify the snapshot source.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication or posting date
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata records date_published as 2025-09-24 and additional posted/originally_published as 24 Sep 2025.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures the parent document publication date, and time_period would incorrectly conflate publication timing with the data period represented by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned chart identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Chart 2: Households in need of help to withdraw or spend the cash.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the heading and internal_identifier captures the “Chart 2” reference without semantic loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject and measured concept
observations.evidence: The snapshot describes “Households in need of help to withdraw or spend the cash.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent both the snapshot purpose and the measured concept of needing help with cash withdrawal or spending.

observations.evidence: The title explicitly refers to “Households.”
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field directly covers the human group that the represented data are about.

observations.evidence: The legend lists “Yes,” “No,” and “Do not know,” and the bar labels include reasons such as “Did not know how to use the card,” “Limited Mobility,” and “Other.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category fields can describe the response categories and reason labels used to organize the values.

observations.evidence: All displayed values are percentages, such as “82,30%,” “71%,” and “26%.”
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure and measure_type fields adequately represent that values are expressed as percentages.

observations.metadata_concept: Composite visualization using donut and bar charts
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains a donut chart on the left and a bar chart on the right connected by an arrow.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can describe the explicit visual encodings, including multiple visualization types where appropriate.

observations.evidence: The source-document title is “Ecuador: Cash Assistance - Post Distribution Monitoring, March 2025,” and the document metadata lists ref_country as “Ecuador.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Ecuador as the contextual geography for the snapshot when supported by the parent document metadata.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language as “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Ecuador: Cash Assistance - Post Distribution Monitoring, March 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic or sectoral domain from document context
observations.evidence: The document title refers to “Cash Assistance,” and the metadata themes include “Protection and Human Rights” and “Shelter and Non-Food Items.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and intervention_type fields can capture the explicit cash-assistance and humanitarian-sector context.

observations.metadata_concept: Report month as possible data or report period
observations.evidence: The source-document title includes “March 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The evidence does not reliably establish whether March 2025 is the snapshot’s represented data period rather than only the parent report period.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published as “2025-08-29” and date_available as “2025-08-29.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has no field for parent-document publication date, and time_period would incorrectly conflate publication timing with represented data timing.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/ecuador/ecuador-cash-assistance-post-distribution-monitoring-march-2025” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures a retrieval link for the parent document, while data_source is defined for the origin of represented data rather than access location.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document producer or source organization
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists producer name “UNHCR” with role “Source,” and the author full_name is “UNHCR.”
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document attribution with the underlying data origin, while source_document_title omits the producer organization.

observations.evidence: The document metadata type is “Situation Report,” and additional.unhcr_format is “Situation Report.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema can name the parent document but has no field for its document genre or type.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or availability date of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided in source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but not when it was published, and time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, version assessment, citation, and avoiding conflation between document release timing and snapshot data timing.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent access link for the parent document or its source-page record containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: No existing v1.1 field stores an access or retrieval link for the parent document, and data_source does not represent document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables verification, retrieval, provenance tracing, and auditability of extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization or person credited as producing, authoring, publishing, or serving as the source of the parent document, when explicitly identified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is about the origin of represented data, not document attribution, and source_document_title omits responsible organizations.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, source verification, and attribution for snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit genre, format, or type of the parent document containing the snapshot, such as situation report, annual report, or policy brief.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document but does not capture its genre or format, which affects retrieval and interpretation.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, organization, and contextual interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document in which they appear.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language as “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Ecuador: Cash Assistance - Post Distribution Monitoring, March 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic or sectoral domain from document context
observations.evidence: The document title refers to “Cash Assistance,” and the metadata themes include “Protection and Human Rights” and “Shelter and Non-Food Items.”

observations.metadata_concept: Report month as possible data or report period

observations.fit_rationale: The evidence does not reliably establish whether March 2025 is the snapshot’s represented data period rather than only the parent report period.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published as “2025-08-29” and date_available as “2025-08-29.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has no field for parent-document publication date, and time_period would incorrectly conflate publication timing with represented data timing.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/ecuador/ecuador-cash-assistance-post-distribution-monitoring-march-2025” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures a retrieval link for the parent document, while data_source is defined for the origin of represented data rather than access location.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document producer or source organization
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists producer name “UNHCR” with role “Source,” and the author full_name is “UNHCR.”
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document attribution with the underlying data origin, while source_document_title omits the producer organization.

observations.evidence: The document metadata type is “Situation Report,” and additional.unhcr_format is “Situation Report.”

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or availability date of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided in source-document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but not when it was published, and time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, version assessment, citation, and avoiding conflation between document release timing and snapshot data timing.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent access link for the parent document or its source-page record containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables verification, retrieval, provenance tracing, and auditability of extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization or person credited as producing, authoring, publishing, or serving as the source of the parent document, when explicitly identified.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit genre, format, or type of the parent document containing the snapshot, such as situation report, annual report, or policy brief.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, organization, and contextual interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document in which they appear.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope field directly captures Somalia as the primary area represented.

observations.metadata_concept: Named geographic entities shown on or contextualizing the map
observations.evidence: The map labels Somalia and neighboring countries including Kenya, Ethiopia, Djibouti, Eritrea, and Yemen.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_entities field is designed to capture named places explicitly represented in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The map displays internal administrative boundary lines and multiple bubbles positioned at subnational locations within Somalia.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_granularity field can record that the map reports or locates data at a subnational spatial level, while geographic_role can describe the locations as reporting locations if explicitly stated.

observations.metadata_concept: Reporting period indicated by the source report title
observations.evidence: The source-document title is 'Inter-Agency Complaint/Feedback Mechanism Aggregator Model Analysis Report - Q2 2024'.
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field can represent Q2 2024 when the report title explicitly identifies that reporting period.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document title identifying the source of the snapshot
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is 'Inter-Agency Complaint/Feedback Mechanism Aggregator Model Analysis Report - Q2 2024'.
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the parent document title.

observations.metadata_concept: Language of the snapshot and source context
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists language as English, and the map labels are in English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures English as the language used in the snapshot context.

observations.metadata_concept: Broad thematic domain of the snapshot context
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists the UNHCR theme as 'Protection and Human Rights'.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field can represent the broad protection and human rights theme contextualizing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creator or responsible organization
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists the author as Save the Children and producers include UNHCR with role 'Source'.
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field refers to the dataset, survey, publication, or cited source of represented data and would conflate source-document authorship or hosting responsibility with underlying data provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the source document or attached PDF
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb report URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the source document by title but has no field for a resolvable access or retrieval location.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication or release date
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published as 2024-02-01 and additional.unhcr_originally_published as 1 Feb 2024.
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the period represented by the data and would misrepresent a parent document publication date as the snapshot's data period.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional entity credited with creating, authoring, publishing, or otherwise being responsible for the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Existing fields include source_document_title and data_source, but data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data rather than the creator or responsible entity for the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance review, source credibility assessment, filtering by producing organization, and disambiguation of snapshots from similarly titled documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A resolvable URL or persistent link for accessing the parent document or its source landing page containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title supports identification but not retrieval, and no existing schema field stores a document access link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables verification, retrieval, citation, deduplication, and reprocessing of snapshots from their original source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, release, or originally published date of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided as document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the period represented by the data and cannot safely encode the parent document publication date without conflating different temporal concepts.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance verification, versioning, temporal filtering of source documents, and distinction between data/reporting periods and document release dates.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title and document-assigned figure number
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Figure 14. Costs by nationality (n= 6,294,786 JOD).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the caption and internal_identifier captures “Figure 14” without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays vertical bars for nationality categories with numeric labels above the bars.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a bar chart.

observations.evidence: The title says “Costs by nationality” and the y-axis is labeled “Cost in Jordanian Dinar,” with “JOD” also shown in the title parenthetical.
observations.fit_rationale: The represented cost concept, financial nature, unit, and currency are covered by existing measurement and financial fields.

observations.evidence: The x-axis is labeled “Nationality” and the displayed labels include Syrian, Iraqi, Yemeni, Sudanese, Jordanian, Egyptian, and Other.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields capture the nationality grouping and its explicit labels.

observations.evidence: The source-document title is “Jordan Medical Referrals at a Glance: Year End Report, January - December, 2016.”
observations.fit_rationale: The explicit report period in the source-document title can be represented as the snapshot time_period when used as contextual evidence.

observations.evidence: The source-document title refers to “Jordan Medical Referrals,” and the document themes include “Health” and “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields adequately capture the health-sector medical-referral context for the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document title begins “Jordan Medical Referrals at a Glance,” and the metadata lists Jordan as the primary country.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Jordan as the explicit geographic context.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Jordan Medical Referrals at a Glance: Year End Report, January - December, 2016.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The chart text is in English and the document metadata lists English as the language.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language evidenced in the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/jordan/jordan-medical-referrals-glance-year-end-report-january-december-2016” and a PDF relation URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the source document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification link to the parent document.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors including Save the Children, Jordan Health Aid Society, and UN High Commissioner for Refugees, and additional UNHCR sources with the same organizations.
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate parent-document creators or ReliefWeb source organizations with the dataset or source from which the represented data originate.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published and date_available as “2025-11-27” and additional UNHCR posted/originally published values as “27 Nov 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The date is a parent-document publication or posting date, not the represented data period captured by time_period.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its canonical landing page or file can be retrieved or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable or verifiable location for it.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance verification, document retrieval, deduplication, and auditability for extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional source credited with creating, authoring, issuing, or supplying the parent source document.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, while the evidenced organizations are credited for the parent document or ReliefWeb source record rather than explicitly for the underlying data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, filtering by producing organization, and verification without misclassifying document creators as data sources.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit publication, posting, or availability date of the parent source document, distinct from the period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period represents the data period, and source_document_title does not encode publication or posting chronology for the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, citation, version checking, and provenance auditing while avoiding conflation of publication date with represented data period.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope and geographic_entities can represent Lebanon as the explicitly evidenced geographic context for the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal context of the represented survey
observations.evidence: The source-document title ends with "November 2015."
observations.fit_rationale: time_period captures the explicitly stated November 2015 survey context without relying on publication or harvest dates.

observations.metadata_concept: Percentage unit and proportional measure scale

observations.fit_rationale: unit_of_measure captures percent and measure_type captures percentage or proportion.

observations.evidence: The source-document title identifies a "Health access and utilization survey among non-camp refugees in Lebanon."
observations.fit_rationale: data_collection_method captures the survey method while source_document_title preserves the parent document title that provides the context.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title includes the parenthetical "(n=238)."
observations.fit_rationale: title and interpretive_note can preserve the text but do not provide a structured way to identify the sample size underlying the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the source document containing the snapshot

observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document but no existing field captures a locator needed to retrieve or verify it.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated number of observations, respondents, households, records, or other analytical units underlying the represented data snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Existing fields can store the full title or an unstructured interpretive note, but they cannot distinguish sample size as reusable methodological metadata for search, filtering, or assessment.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports interpretation of statistical reliability, comparison across snapshots, and retrieval of charts or tables by the size of the represented analytical sample.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent locator for the parent document or source file from which the data snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema has source_document_title but lacks a field for the document locator, so retrieval and verification information would be lost or conflated with title or data_source.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the parent document associated with a snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicit rule or criterion used to select, limit, or rank the categories displayed in a snapshot, such as top-N, bottom-N, threshold-based inclusion, or ranked subset selection.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: title can retain the wording and category_dimension can identify the grouping variable, but neither provides a structured way to represent that the visible categories are a ranked top-10 subset.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports search, filtering, and analytical reuse by distinguishing complete category displays from ranked or otherwise limited category subsets.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional entity explicitly credited with authoring, producing, or issuing the parent document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is reserved for the origin of the represented data, and source_document_title identifies only the parent document name, so using either would omit or conflate document-level attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, verification, and retrieval workflows for snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL explicitly provided for accessing, locating, or verifying the parent document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a machine-actionable location for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to trace a snapshot back to the source document for validation, citation, and re-extraction.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.evidence: The snapshot caption reads "Summary of verified incidents and total numbers of affected population in Ukraine."
observations.fit_rationale: The caption directly identifies and summarizes the snapshot, which is represented by the existing title and subject_summary fields.

observations.evidence: The snapshot labels the measures as "Verified civilian casualties," "Verified civilians killed," "Verified civilians injured," "IDPs," "Returnees," and "Non-displaced."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the indicators and measured concepts represented in the figure.

observations.evidence: The snapshot explicitly refers to civilians, IDPs, returnees, non-displaced people, and affected population.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing population_group field captures who the data are about, while category_labels can capture explicit displacement-status labels if treated as categories.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope of the represented data
observations.evidence: The caption states that the summary is "in Ukraine," and the source-document metadata lists ref_country as Ukraine.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields adequately represent Ukraine as the area covered by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot presents total numbers of casualties and affected population, including values displayed as whole numbers and millions.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent that the values are counts or numbers of people without storing the extracted numerical values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a horizontal set of large-number indicator cards separated by vertical dashed lines.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field can describe the figure as an indicator-card, KPI-style infographic, or similar visual form.

observations.evidence: The source-document title refers to protection risks and violations against civilians, and the document themes include "Protection and Human Rights," "Mine Action," and "Gender."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field adequately captures the protection and humanitarian thematic context evidenced by the document metadata.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Ukraine: Protection Analysis Update - Unabated violations against civilians increase the impact of protection risks on the population (June 2023) [EN/UK]."
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot or parent context
observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English, and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language evidenced in both the snapshot and the document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Represented data period or report issue month
observations.evidence: The source-document title includes "(June 2023)," but the snapshot itself does not state a data date or range.
observations.fit_rationale: It is unclear whether June 2023 is the period represented by the snapshot data or only part of the parent report identification, so time_period cannot be reliably applied.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable source-document locator used to verify or access the snapshot context.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document issuing or authoring organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors as UNICEF, Protection Cluster, and UN High Commissioner for Refugees, and producers include UNHCR with role "Source."
observations.fit_rationale: data_source would conflate document authors or issuers with the source of the represented data, while source_document_title does not capture organizational attribution.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent source-document publication or posting date
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published as 2025-06-18 and additional ReliefWeb posting and original publication dates as 18 Jun 2025.
observations.fit_rationale: time_period would misrepresent a document publication date as the represented data period, and source_document_title does not capture publication timing.

observations.evidence: The document metadata type and additional.unhcr_format identify the source document as a "Situation Report."
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for the genre or format of the source document that contextualizes the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web location where the parent source document or its file can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot context.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable locator, and data_source concerns the origin of represented data rather than access to the containing document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, auditability, deduplication, and verification of snapshots against their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, author, producer, or issuing body responsible for creating or publishing the parent source document, distinct from the source of the represented data unless explicitly the same.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would incorrectly conflate document attribution with the dataset or survey underlying the represented values, and source_document_title does not capture creator attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, filtering by issuing organization, and assessment of institutional context without overstating data-origin evidence.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated publication, posting, or release date of the parent source document containing the snapshot, distinct from the time period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined for the period represented by the data and would be misleading for document release timing, while source_document_title does not encode publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports versioning, citation, retrieval, and temporal organization of snapshots by source-document release date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated genre, format, or document class of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not capture whether it is a situation report, assessment, policy paper, annual report, or another document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables filtering, interpretation, and organization of snapshots by the kind of institutional document in which they appear.
