observations.evidence: The snapshot is displayed as a tabular infographic with service rows and multiple numeric columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table-like visual artifact.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of older people receiving support
observations.evidence: The snapshot includes the summary text “Total older people supported in 2024” and rows describing individuals receiving various forms of assistance.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary field can concisely describe the snapshot's purpose as summarizing support provided to older people.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary measured concept of supported individuals
observations.evidence: Rows repeatedly use phrases such as “Individuals receiving cash assistance,” “Individuals receiving medical support,” and “Individuals provided with individual legal assistance.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the measured concept as individuals receiving or being provided support.

observations.evidence: The snapshot states “Total older people supported in 2024,” and the source-document title identifies an “Older Refugees Briefing Note.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing population_group field captures the primary human group as older people or older refugees when explicitly supported.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal period represented by the snapshot data
observations.evidence: The snapshot text explicitly says “Total older people supported in 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field directly represents the data period 2024.

observations.metadata_concept: Unit and statistical form of the reported quantities
observations.evidence: The snapshot describes quantities as “Individuals receiving” or “Persons with Specific Needs provided with” assistance.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing unit_of_measure and measure_type fields capture that the values are counts of people or individuals.

observations.metadata_concept: Assistance or service types represented in rows
observations.evidence: Row labels include cash assistance, medical support, MHPSS services and activities, targeted protection assistance, hygiene kits, and individual legal assistance.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing intervention_type, row_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the service categories used to organize the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Subject domain of humanitarian health and protection support
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists themes “Health” and “Protection and Human Rights,” and the snapshot rows include medical, MHPSS, protection, and legal assistance.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field captures broad thematic domains evidenced by the document and snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document title names “Refugee Coordination Forum Moldova,” and document metadata lists Moldova as the primary country.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Moldova as the documented geographic context for the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the source-document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Disability & Age Task Force - Refugee Coordination Forum Moldova - Older Refugees Briefing Note (January 2025) [EN/RO].”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the parent document title.

observations.metadata_concept: Icon-only demographic or accessibility column categories
observations.evidence: The column headers are represented by icons resembling an older woman with a cane, an older man with a cane, and a wheelchair user without accompanying text labels.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields are related, but the absence of textual labels makes the exact semantic categories insufficiently certain to assess coverage reliably.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the landing-page URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/moldova/disability-age-task-force-refugee-coordination-forum-moldova-older-refugees-briefing-note-january-2025-enro” and a PDF URL in relations.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification URL for the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document creators or credited organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors OCHA, REACH, and UNHCR and a producer entry for UNHCR.
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field would conflate credited document creators with the origin of the represented data, and source_document_title does not capture creator attribution.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document publication or availability date
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_available and date_published as “2025-11-05.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field represents the data period shown in the snapshot, not the administrative publication date of the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The URL or persistent landing page where the parent document containing the snapshot can be accessed or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrievable locator, and no provenance field captures a parent-document URL.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, citation, verification, and de-duplication of snapshots extracted from source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional entity credited with authoring, producing, or publishing the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data and would misrepresent document authors or producers when they are not explicitly the data source.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports attribution, provenance review, source credibility assessment, and organization-based retrieval without conflating document creation with data origin.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, or availability date of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided as document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is reserved for the period represented by the snapshot data and cannot safely store the parent document's publication date without semantic confusion.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports versioning, citation, temporal filtering of source documents, and verification of when the snapshot was disseminated.

observations.metadata_concept: snapshot title and document-assigned table identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Table 2: Estimation results.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures “Estimation results” and internal_identifier captures the document label “Table 2” without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is laid out as a two-column table with row labels and an “OLS regression” column.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: analytical method used to produce the reported results
observations.evidence: The column header explicitly states “OLS regression.”
observations.fit_rationale: The analysis_method field is defined to capture explicitly stated statistical methods such as regression.

observations.metadata_concept: statistical model variable role for controls or covariates
observations.evidence: The table includes a section labeled “Other control variables” with items such as housing type, source for cooking and sanitation, asset and animal ownership, and location.
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method captures the regression method and variable_name captures primary measured concepts, but neither represents explicitly labeled model roles such as control variables.

observations.metadata_concept: primary analytical subject of the snapshot within the parent brief
observations.evidence: The source document title is “Uganda Policy Brief: Targeting assistance programmes to persons with specific needs - December 2020,” and the table title is “Estimation results.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_summary can concisely describe that the snapshot presents estimation results related to targeting assistance programmes for persons with specific needs.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the theme “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain is intended to capture broad thematic or policy domains such as protection and human rights.

observations.metadata_concept: human population group represented or referenced
observations.evidence: The parent title refers to “persons with specific needs,” and the table includes the row label “HH Has a PSN member.”
observations.fit_rationale: population_group directly captures the human group that the represented analysis concerns.

observations.evidence: The source document title begins “Uganda Policy Brief,” and the document metadata lists Uganda as the primary country.
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope can represent Uganda as the primary geographic context supplied by the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Uganda Policy Brief: Targeting assistance programmes to persons with specific needs - December 2020.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title exactly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: language directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF URL for the parent document.
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but no existing field records a retrievable locator for verification or access.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists UNHCR as producer with role “Source” and author full_name “UNHCR.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source would imply the origin of the represented data, while the evidence only supports UNHCR as the parent-document creator or source organization.

observations.metadata_concept: source document publication or release date
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published “2025-11-27” and additional fields “unhcr_posted” and “unhcr_originally_published” as “27 Nov 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the data period represented by the snapshot, not the publication or release date of the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated analytical role assigned to variables in a statistical model represented by the snapshot, such as control variable, predictor, treatment variable, or dependent variable.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: analysis_method records the model type and variable_name records primary measured concepts, but neither captures the role that variables play within an explicitly presented statistical model.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would improve discovery and interpretation of regression or model-results snapshots by distinguishing controls, predictors, outcomes, and other model roles without reconstructing numeric results.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent online locator for the parent document or source landing page from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document textually but does not provide a machine-actionable access or verification link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support retrieval, provenance verification, citation, and re-access to the source context for the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person or organization explicitly credited with authoring, creating, producing, or providing the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is reserved for the origin of the represented data and would conflate document authorship or provision with data provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would help users verify document provenance and organize snapshots by responsible institution without misusing data_source.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, release, or originally published date explicitly associated with the parent document, distinct from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the represented data period and source_document_title only stores the document title, so neither cleanly represents document release timing.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support source verification, temporal organization of extracted snapshots, and retrieval of the correct document version without implying a data period.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

observations.metadata_concept: snapshot title and document-assigned table identifier
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Table 2: Estimation results.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures “Estimation results” and internal_identifier captures the document label “Table 2” without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is laid out as a two-column table with row labels and an “OLS regression” column.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: analytical method used to produce the reported results
observations.evidence: The column header explicitly states “OLS regression.”
observations.fit_rationale: The analysis_method field is defined to capture explicitly stated statistical methods such as regression.

observations.metadata_concept: statistical model variable role for controls or covariates
observations.evidence: The table includes a section labeled “Other control variables” with items such as housing type, source for cooking and sanitation, asset and animal ownership, and location.
observations.fit_rationale: analysis_method captures the regression method and variable_name captures primary measured concepts, but neither represents explicitly labeled model roles such as control variables.

observations.metadata_concept: primary analytical subject of the snapshot within the parent brief
observations.evidence: The source document title is “Uganda Policy Brief: Targeting assistance programmes to persons with specific needs - December 2020,” and the table title is “Estimation results.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_summary can concisely describe that the snapshot presents estimation results related to targeting assistance programmes for persons with specific needs.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the theme “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain is intended to capture broad thematic or policy domains such as protection and human rights.

observations.metadata_concept: human population group represented or referenced
observations.evidence: The parent title refers to “persons with specific needs,” and the table includes the row label “HH Has a PSN member.”
observations.fit_rationale: population_group directly captures the human group that the represented analysis concerns.

observations.evidence: The source document title begins “Uganda Policy Brief,” and the document metadata lists Uganda as the primary country.
observations.fit_rationale: geographic_scope can represent Uganda as the primary geographic context supplied by the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Uganda Policy Brief: Targeting assistance programmes to persons with specific needs - December 2020.”
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title exactly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language “English.”
observations.fit_rationale: language directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF URL for the parent document.
observations.fit_rationale: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but no existing field records a retrievable locator for verification or access.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists UNHCR as producer with role “Source” and author full_name “UNHCR.”
observations.fit_rationale: data_source would imply the origin of the represented data, while the evidence only supports UNHCR as the parent-document creator or source organization.

observations.metadata_concept: source document publication or release date
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists date_published “2025-11-27” and additional fields “unhcr_posted” and “unhcr_originally_published” as “27 Nov 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: time_period describes the data period represented by the snapshot, not the publication or release date of the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent online locator for the parent document or source landing page from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document textually but does not provide a machine-actionable access or verification link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: This field would support retrieval, provenance verification, citation, and re-access to the source context for the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person or organization explicitly credited with authoring, creating, producing, or providing the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the conceptual grouping and explicit group labels shown in the table.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent the named geographic entities and their contextual roles when used as document context for the snapshot.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.fit_rationale: The schema can represent both the conceptual dimensions and the explicit labels used to organize rows and columns.

observations.evidence: The table heading states "en novembre 2024" and the source document title also refers to "novembre 2024".
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field captures November 2024 and temporal_granularity can represent the monthly reporting resolution.

observations.evidence: The snapshot title names "KWANGO, KWILU, MAÏ-NDOMBE," sections include "KINSHASA," and the document metadata lists ref_country "Democratic Republic of the Congo".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields capture the country context, named places, and explicitly indicated province-level organization.

observations.evidence: The table includes count columns for violation categories and a "%" column alongside "Total".
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent counts and percentages without recording cell values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a tabular display with rows, columns, and section totals.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly supports identifying the artifact as a table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French and the document metadata lists language "French" with code "fr".
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Cluster Protection RDC : Points saillants de la situation de protection en République démocratique du Congo en novembre 2024".
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: No v1.1 field captures a retrievable URL for the parent document or its source file.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication or posting date
observations.evidence: The document metadata records "date_published": "2025-11-04" and additional metadata lists "posted" and "originally_published" as "4 Nov 2025".
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the period represented by the data, so using it for the parent document publication date would conflate provenance timing with data timing.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creator or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors "UNICEF," "Protection Cluster," and "UN High Commissioner for Refugees," and lists UNHCR as a producer with role "Source".
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field describes the origin of the represented data, not necessarily the organizations that authored or supplied the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document, landing page, or source file containing the snapshot can be accessed.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support direct retrieval or verification through an access link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, auditability, deduplication, and verification of snapshots against their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, or release date of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided as document provenance rather than the data period.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period refers to the period represented by the data and would distort the meaning of a document publication or posting date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps identify document versions, support provenance checks, and distinguish data reference periods from publication chronology.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, person, or entity explicitly credited with authoring, producing, or contributing the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source captures the cited origin of the represented data, while source document creators may only describe document authorship or publication responsibility.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, filtering, and verification without conflating document authorship with the underlying data source.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes

observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Main obstacles accessing to information.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a table with rows of obstacles and two population-group columns containing percentages and embedded bars.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a table without material loss.

observations.evidence: The title and row labels describe obstacles to accessing information, including lack of contact information, no phone, no electricity, and limited internet access.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_summary and variable_name fields adequately capture the snapshot’s measured concept and analytical purpose.

observations.metadata_concept: Obstacle categories used as row groupings
observations.evidence: Rows list obstacle labels such as “Have no phone,” “No electricity,” and “Limited/ no access to internet.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema covers both the row dimension as obstacle type and the explicit category labels.

observations.evidence: The column headers are “IDPs” and “Refugees in the north.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture the population-group column dimension, labels, subject groups, and explicit comparison between groups.

observations.evidence: Each reported value is shown with a percent sign, such as 40%, 27%, and 60%.
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure and measure_type fields adequately represent that values are percentages.

observations.evidence: The source-document title refers to communities in Yemen, the document metadata lists ref_country as Yemen, and the snapshot column label includes “Refugees in the north.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can capture Yemen as the scope and the northern location qualifier where explicitly represented.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Understanding how UNHCR engages with communities in Yemen: Community engagement survey report (September 2020).”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists themes “Coordination” and “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field can represent the broad thematic domains evidenced by the document context.

observations.evidence: The parent document title identifies the source as a “Community engagement survey report.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field covers the explicitly indicated survey basis without needing to reconstruct results.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/yemen/understanding-how-unhcr-engages-communities-yemen-community-engagement-survey-report” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification URL.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creator or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors including UNHCR, ACTED, CCY, DRC, and “5 more,” and producers include UNHCR with role “Source.”
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document creators or contributors with the source of the represented data, while source_document_title omits responsible organizations.

observations.evidence: The document metadata states date_published “2025-09-24” and additional.unhcr_originally_published “24 Sep 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field describes the period represented by the data, so using it for document publication date would distort the temporal semantics.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its canonical landing page or file can be retrieved or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a resolvable location for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, auditability, deduplication, and retrieval of the source context for a data snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or organizations credited with authoring, producing, publishing, or otherwise creating the parent source document.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is reserved for the cited origin of the represented data, and source_document_title does not capture responsible document creators or contributors.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, verification, and organization of snapshots by responsible source-document entities without conflating them with data-origin sources.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, or release date of the parent source document, distinct from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the represented data period and cannot safely encode a document publication date without semantic distortion.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, version assessment, retrieval, and temporal organization of snapshots by parent-document release date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its landing page can be retrieved or verified.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a machine-actionable retrieval or verification location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports snapshot provenance checks, document retrieval, deduplication, and citation back to the exact source context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated publication, posting, or availability date of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the period represented by the data and cannot safely represent the parent document publication date, while source_document_title contains no date semantics.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports versioning, provenance verification, temporal filtering of source materials, and distinction between data period and document release date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly stated genre, format, or document type of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document but does not capture whether it is a situation report, annual update, report, annex, or other source-document form.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, filtering, and interpretation of snapshots by the type of institutional document in which they appear.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An organization or person explicitly identified as producing, authoring, publishing, or otherwise contributing to the parent source document, without asserting that they are the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the dataset, survey, publication, or cited source from which the represented data originate, so it does not cleanly capture parent-document provenance contributors.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance tracking, verification, organizational filtering, and avoiding conflation between document authorship and underlying data origin.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support direct retrieval or verification through a web locator, and data_source refers to the origin of the represented data rather than the document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, auditability, citation, and verification of extracted snapshots against their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or release date of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided as document metadata.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and would distort semantics if used for a document publication date, while source_document_title has no temporal component.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports versioning, citation, provenance checks, and distinguishing document release timing from the data period represented in a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An organization or person explicitly credited as an author, producer, publisher, or source of the parent document containing the snapshot, without asserting that they are the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would conflate document attribution with the dataset, survey, publication, or other source from which the represented values originate, and no existing field captures parent-document contributors separately.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports attribution, provenance review, filtering by producing organization, and verification of the institutional context for snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Publication or posting date of the parent source document, distinct from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and would distort semantics if used for a document publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, version distinction, chronological retrieval, and audit of document provenance without confusing publication timing with data coverage.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Organization or person credited with authoring, producing, or contributing to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source refers to the source of the represented data and does not cleanly capture parent-document authorship or production responsibility.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves attribution, provenance tracking, and filtering of snapshots by the institutions responsible for the source document.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot is presented as a grid with rows and columns, and the artifact metadata labels it as type "table".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: French language used in the snapshot
observations.evidence: The table text is in French, including phrases such as "Enlèvement d’un conseiller municipal," and the document metadata lists language "French".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Rapport de monitoring de protection région du Boucle du Mouhoun - Août 2020".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document title refers to "monitoring de protection" and the metadata themes include "Protection and Human Rights" along with other humanitarian themes.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field can represent the broad protection and humanitarian domain evidenced for the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of protection incidents and follow-up actions
observations.evidence: The visible table row includes an incident description "Enlèvement d’un conseiller municipal" and actions such as "Intensifier les activités de monitoring" and "Partager l’alerte".
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of subject_summary, variable_name, and intervention_type can describe the table’s focus on protection incidents and related response actions without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Incident date or represented time period
observations.evidence: The visible row shows the date "24/08/2020" and the parent document title states "Août 2020".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field can capture the explicit date or monthly period represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The visible table row reports a specific day, "24/08/2020".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal_granularity field can represent that the table reports information at a daily level.

observations.evidence: The document title identifies "région du Boucle du Mouhoun," the document metadata lists Burkina Faso, and the visible row includes "Nouna/ Tèbèrè".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture both the broader area and the named locations represented.

observations.evidence: The row associates "Nouna/ Tèbèrè" with the incident "Enlèvement d’un conseiller municipal".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_role field can express that the named places function as incident or reporting locations.

observations.metadata_concept: Quantitative count measure for incidents or affected cases
observations.evidence: The visible row includes the value "01" in a separate table column next to the incident description.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent the count-style measurement concept without storing the extracted value.

observations.metadata_concept: Monetary currency used for cash assistance values
observations.evidence: A visible cell in the snapshot mentions "cash transfert 40 000 FCFA".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing currency, unit_of_measure, and financial_measure fields can describe the FCFA-denominated cash-transfer measure without capturing the numeric value.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the ReliefWeb URL "https://reliefweb.int/report/burkina-faso/rapport-de-monitoring-de-protection-r-gion-du-boucle-du-mouhoun-ao-t-2020" and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification URL for the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type and UNHCR format as "Situation Report".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a field for the parent document title but no field for the source document’s genre or format.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creators or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors or sources including "OCHA," "INTERSOS," and "UN High Commissioner for Refugees".
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document creators with the origin of the represented data, while source_document_title does not capture attribution.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its source landing page can be accessed for retrieval or verification.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not support direct retrieval or verification of the document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to trace a snapshot back to the accessible source document for audit, citation, and re-checking context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, format, or document class of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the document but does not distinguish whether it is a situation report, assessment, annual report, dashboard, or other document type.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, organization, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An organization or person credited with authoring, producing, publishing, or otherwise creating the parent source document.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, not the creator of the parent document, and source_document_title does not provide attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, citation, verification, and retrieval by preserving who is responsible for the document containing the snapshot without mislabeling them as the data source.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot is presented as a grid with rows and columns, and the artifact metadata labels it as type "table".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: French language used in the snapshot
observations.evidence: The table text is in French, including phrases such as "Enlèvement d’un conseiller municipal," and the document metadata lists language "French".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is "Rapport de monitoring de protection région du Boucle du Mouhoun - Août 2020".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document title refers to "monitoring de protection" and the metadata themes include "Protection and Human Rights" along with other humanitarian themes.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field can represent the broad protection and humanitarian domain evidenced for the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary analytical subject of protection incidents and follow-up actions
observations.evidence: The visible table row includes an incident description "Enlèvement d’un conseiller municipal" and actions such as "Intensifier les activités de monitoring" and "Partager l’alerte".
observations.fit_rationale: The combination of subject_summary, variable_name, and intervention_type can describe the table’s focus on protection incidents and related response actions without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Incident date or represented time period
observations.evidence: The visible row shows the date "24/08/2020" and the parent document title states "Août 2020".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field can capture the explicit date or monthly period represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The visible table row reports a specific day, "24/08/2020".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal_granularity field can represent that the table reports information at a daily level.

observations.evidence: The document title identifies "région du Boucle du Mouhoun," the document metadata lists Burkina Faso, and the visible row includes "Nouna/ Tèbèrè".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture both the broader area and the named locations represented.

observations.evidence: The row associates "Nouna/ Tèbèrè" with the incident "Enlèvement d’un conseiller municipal".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_role field can express that the named places function as incident or reporting locations.

observations.metadata_concept: Quantitative count measure for incidents or affected cases
observations.evidence: The visible row includes the value "01" in a separate table column next to the incident description.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent the count-style measurement concept without storing the extracted value.

observations.metadata_concept: Monetary currency used for cash assistance values
observations.evidence: A visible cell in the snapshot mentions "cash transfert 40 000 FCFA".
observations.fit_rationale: The existing currency, unit_of_measure, and financial_measure fields can describe the FCFA-denominated cash-transfer measure without capturing the numeric value.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the ReliefWeb URL "https://reliefweb.int/report/burkina-faso/rapport-de-monitoring-de-protection-r-gion-du-boucle-du-mouhoun-ao-t-2020" and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema captures the parent document title but has no field for a retrieval or verification URL for the source document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type and UNHCR format as "Situation Report".
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a field for the parent document title but no field for the source document’s genre or format.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creators or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors or sources including "OCHA," "INTERSOS," and "UN High Commissioner for Refugees".
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document creators with the origin of the represented data, while source_document_title does not capture attribution.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering, organization, and interpretation of snapshots by the kind of institutional document from which they were extracted.

observations.evidence: The snapshot displays the headings “PROVINCES DE KWANGO, KWILU, MAI-NDOMBE” and “Violations et abus de droits.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field can represent the explicit heading identifying the table without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | novembre 2023.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the parent document title.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic domain of protection and human rights
observations.evidence: The document theme is “Protection and Human Rights,” and the table heading refers to “Violations et abus de droits.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field covers the broad protection and human rights theme represented by the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of rights violations and abuses by province
observations.evidence: The table groups “Violations et abus de droits” across the provinces Kwango, Kwilu, and Maï-Ndombe.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary field can concisely describe the table’s analytical purpose.

observations.evidence: The central table heading is “Violations et abus de droits.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the measured concept represented by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Categorization by province and rights-violation type
observations.evidence: Rows are labeled “Provinces,” and columns include “Droit à la propriété,” “Droit à l’intégrité physique,” “Violation du droit à la liberté,” and “VBG.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category and structural dimension fields capture the province rows and violation-type columns.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic coverage and named geographic entities
observations.evidence: The snapshot title lists “KWANGO, KWILU, MAI-NDOMBE,” and the document metadata identifies “Democratic Republic of the Congo.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent the country context and the explicitly named provinces.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading says “PROVINCES DE KWANGO, KWILU, MAI-NDOMBE,” and the row header is “Provinces.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_granularity field directly captures that the data are reported at province level.

observations.evidence: The source-document title includes “novembre 2023.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field can represent the explicitly stated November 2023 period when used as document context for the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Quantitative expression as counts and percentages
observations.evidence: The table includes numeric columns for violation categories plus “Total” and “%.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields cover counts, totals, and percent values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with row and column headers and tabular numeric entries.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the document metadata language is “French.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used in the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata provides the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/republique-democratique-du-congo-points-saillants-de-protection-novembre-2023” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema records the source document title but has no field for a retrieval link needed to locate or verify the parent document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists “date_published”: “2025-11-25” and “date_available”: “2025-11-25.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field describes the represented data period and would conflate that concept with the parent document’s publication date.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creators or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors “OCHA,” “Education Cluster,” “Save the Children,” and “UNICEF,” while the producer entry lists “UNHCR” with role “Source.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_source field is for the origin of represented data, not for creators or source organizations of the parent document when data origin is not explicitly established.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent document or its file can be accessed for retrieval, verification, or citation of the snapshot source context.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but cannot support direct retrieval or verification through a link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to locate the original document containing the snapshot and verify extraction context.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication or availability date of the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from the period represented by the data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the data’s represented temporal coverage and would distort provenance if used for document publication timing.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, versioning, recency assessment, and provenance checks for extracted snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, person, or institutional entity credited with creating, authoring, producing, or providing the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source should not be used for document authors or source organizations unless they are explicitly the origin of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, filtering, and verification of snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Publication, posting, or release date of the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from the data period represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The existing time_period field represents the period covered by the data, not the administrative publication date of the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps identify document versions, assess currency of the source context, and avoid misusing publication dates as represented data periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Organization or person credited as an author, producer, reporting source, or contributor for the parent document containing the snapshot, when distinct from the underlying data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The closest existing field, data_source, is defined for the source of the represented data and does not safely capture parent-document attribution or reporting-source roles.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, source filtering, and verification while preserving the distinction between document contributors and underlying data sources.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document publication or posting date
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists "date_published": "2025-11-25" and additional fields state the report was posted and originally published on 25 Nov 2025.
observations.fit_rationale: Time_period describes the represented data period and cannot encode the parent document publication date without conflating distinct temporal concepts.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document contributing or source organizations
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists producers with UNHCR as role "Source" and authors or ReliefWeb sources including OCHA, Education Cluster, Save the Children, and UNICEF.
observations.fit_rationale: Data_source is for the dataset or cited source of the represented data, so using it for parent-document authors or reporting sources would conflate document attribution with underlying data provenance.

candidate_new_fields.definition: URL for the parent document, landing page, or retrievable file from which the snapshot was extracted.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema records the parent document title but has no field for a URL that enables retrieval or verification of the exact source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, deduplication, access, and reproducible retrieval of snapshots from institutional documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Publication, posting, or release date of the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from the data period represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The existing time_period field represents the period covered by the data, not the administrative publication date of the source document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps identify document versions, assess currency of the source context, and avoid misusing publication dates as represented data periods.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Organization or person credited as an author, producer, reporting source, or contributor for the parent document containing the snapshot, when distinct from the underlying data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The closest existing field, data_source, is defined for the source of the represented data and does not safely capture parent-document attribution or reporting-source roles.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, source filtering, and verification while preserving the distinction between document contributors and underlying data sources.
