observations.evidence: The snapshot has the prominent heading “PROVINCE DE L’ITURI ET HAUT-UELE” and a table heading “Violations et abus des droits en septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the primary heading or caption identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The caption states “Tableau présentant les tendances de violations et abus des droits signalées par le monitoring de protection en Ituri et Haut Uele.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary field captures the snapshot’s purpose as a table of reported rights-violation trends.

observations.evidence: The source document themes list “Gender” and “Protection and Human Rights,” and the table includes “Violations et abus des droits” and “Allégations VBG.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field captures broad thematic domains such as protection, human rights, and gender.

observations.evidence: The table heading is “Violations et abus des droits en septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the measured concept of rights violations and abuses.

observations.evidence: Column groups include “Violation du droit à la liberté,” “Violation du droit à la propriété,” “Violation du droit à la vie et l’intégrité physique,” “Allégations Violations de la Résolution 1612,” and “Allégations VBG.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields capture the violation-type dimension and its explicit labels.

observations.evidence: Each violation category and the total are subdivided into “Sept” and “Oct.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture month as an organizing dimension and the explicit month labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal period represented by the data
observations.evidence: The table heading says “en septembre et octobre 2024,” and the source document title also says “septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field captures the represented data period of September and October 2024.

observations.evidence: The table reports separate columns for “Sept” and “Oct.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal_granularity field captures monthly reporting resolution.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading names “Province de l’Ituri et Haut-Uele,” and the source document refers to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope field captures the primary areas represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table lists Aru, Djugu, Irumu, Mahagi, Mambasa, Faradje, “Province de l’ITURI,” and “Province de HAUT-UELE.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_entities field captures the named places explicitly represented.

observations.evidence: The left header is “Territoires,” and section headers identify “Province de l’ITURI” and “Province de HAUT-UELE.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture both the administrative reporting levels and the table row dimension.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic role in the represented data
observations.evidence: The caption says the reported violations are “en Ituri et Haut Uele,” and rows are labeled as territories.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_role field can represent the territories and provinces as reporting locations for the violations.

observations.evidence: Rows are territories and province totals, while columns are grouped by violation type, month, and total.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing structural fields capture the conceptual variables represented by table rows and columns.

observations.evidence: The artifact is a grid of rows and columns with numeric entries and headings.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field captures the snapshot as a table.

observations.evidence: The table presents numeric entries under violation categories and a “Total” column for each month.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent counts of reported violations or allegations.

observations.evidence: The caption states the violations and abuses were “signalées par le monitoring de protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_collection_method field captures protection monitoring as the stated collection method or instrument.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the source-document metadata lists language “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent document or source file
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the parent document.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field records a retrievable locator for the parent document without conflating it with title or represented-data source.

observations.metadata_concept: Creators or issuing organizations of the parent document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists authors “UNICEF,” “Protection Cluster,” and “UN High Commissioner for Refugees,” and producer “UNHCR.”
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would imply origin of the represented data, while source_document_title cannot capture document creators or issuers.

observations.metadata_concept: Publication date of the parent document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists “date_published”: “2025-11-04” and additional fields “posted” and “originally_published” as “4 Nov 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field describes the represented data period rather than the parent document’s publication date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent locator where the parent document or source file containing the snapshot can be accessed.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but not by retrievable location, and data_source is reserved for the origin of the represented data rather than the document locator.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, deduplication, and citation of snapshots through access to the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional entity credited with creating, issuing, or authoring the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would conflate document creators with the origin of the represented data, and source_document_title only captures the document name.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, institutional filtering, and verification of snapshots extracted from source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The date on which the parent document containing the snapshot was published, posted, or otherwise made publicly available, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period captures the period represented by the data and should not be used for document publication timing, while source_document_title has no date semantics.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables versioning, temporal retrieval, citation, and verification of the parent document without confusing publication date with data coverage period.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot has the prominent heading “PROVINCE DE L’ITURI ET HAUT-UELE” and a table heading “Violations et abus des droits en septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field captures the primary heading or caption identifying the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The caption states “Tableau présentant les tendances de violations et abus des droits signalées par le monitoring de protection en Ituri et Haut Uele.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary field captures the snapshot’s purpose as a table of reported rights-violation trends.

observations.evidence: The source document themes list “Gender” and “Protection and Human Rights,” and the table includes “Violations et abus des droits” and “Allégations VBG.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field captures broad thematic domains such as protection, human rights, and gender.

observations.evidence: The table heading is “Violations et abus des droits en septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures the measured concept of rights violations and abuses.

observations.evidence: Column groups include “Violation du droit à la liberté,” “Violation du droit à la propriété,” “Violation du droit à la vie et l’intégrité physique,” “Allégations Violations de la Résolution 1612,” and “Allégations VBG.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields capture the violation-type dimension and its explicit labels.

observations.evidence: Each violation category and the total are subdivided into “Sept” and “Oct.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture month as an organizing dimension and the explicit month labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal period represented by the data
observations.evidence: The table heading says “en septembre et octobre 2024,” and the source document title also says “septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field captures the represented data period of September and October 2024.

observations.evidence: The table reports separate columns for “Sept” and “Oct.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal_granularity field captures monthly reporting resolution.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading names “Province de l’Ituri et Haut-Uele,” and the source document refers to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope field captures the primary areas represented by the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table lists Aru, Djugu, Irumu, Mahagi, Mambasa, Faradje, “Province de l’ITURI,” and “Province de HAUT-UELE.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_entities field captures the named places explicitly represented.

observations.evidence: The left header is “Territoires,” and section headers identify “Province de l’ITURI” and “Province de HAUT-UELE.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture both the administrative reporting levels and the table row dimension.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic role in the represented data
observations.evidence: The caption says the reported violations are “en Ituri et Haut Uele,” and rows are labeled as territories.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_role field can represent the territories and provinces as reporting locations for the violations.

observations.evidence: Rows are territories and province totals, while columns are grouped by violation type, month, and total.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing structural fields capture the conceptual variables represented by table rows and columns.

observations.evidence: The artifact is a grid of rows and columns with numeric entries and headings.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field captures the snapshot as a table.

observations.evidence: The table presents numeric entries under violation categories and a “Total” column for each month.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent counts of reported violations or allegations.

observations.evidence: The caption states the violations and abuses were “signalées par le monitoring de protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_collection_method field captures protection monitoring as the stated collection method or instrument.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the source-document metadata lists language “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | septembre et octobre 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent document or source file
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the parent document.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field records a retrievable locator for the parent document without conflating it with title or represented-data source.

observations.metadata_concept: Creators or issuing organizations of the parent document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists authors “UNICEF,” “Protection Cluster,” and “UN High Commissioner for Refugees,” and producer “UNHCR.”
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would imply origin of the represented data, while source_document_title cannot capture document creators or issuers.

observations.metadata_concept: Publication date of the parent document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists “date_published”: “2025-11-04” and additional fields “posted” and “originally_published” as “4 Nov 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field describes the represented data period rather than the parent document’s publication date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent locator where the parent document or source file containing the snapshot can be accessed.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but not by retrievable location, and data_source is reserved for the origin of the represented data rather than the document locator.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, deduplication, and citation of snapshots through access to the source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The person, organization, or institutional entity credited with creating, issuing, or authoring the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source would conflate document creators with the origin of the represented data, and source_document_title only captures the document name.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance, attribution, institutional filtering, and verification of snapshots extracted from source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The date on which the parent document containing the snapshot was published, posted, or otherwise made publicly available, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period captures the period represented by the data and should not be used for document publication timing, while source_document_title has no date semantics.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables versioning, temporal retrieval, citation, and verification of the parent document without confusing publication date with data coverage period.

observations.fit_rationale: The category_dimension, row_dimension, and column_dimension fields cover conceptual variables used to organize table values.

observations.fit_rationale: The schema includes category_labels for explicit non-geographic labels and geographic_entities for named places represented in the table.

observations.fit_rationale: The temporal_granularity field can represent the semiannual resolution explicitly stated for the snapshot context.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary geographic scope in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading states "PROVINCE DU NORD KIVU" and the document title begins "République démocratique du Congo".
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields cover the primary area and named geographic entities represented by the snapshot.

observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_granularity field captures the administrative level of reporting, while row_dimension captures the table-row organization.

observations.metadata_concept: Quantitative counts of reported incidents or allegations
observations.evidence: The table presents integer values under violation categories and a "Total" column and row.
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type field covers counts, and unit_of_measure can capture reported violations or allegations where explicitly described.

observations.metadata_concept: Protection monitoring as data collection context
observations.evidence: The caption states the violations and abuses were "signalées par le monitoring de protection".
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field covers monitoring as the explicitly stated method or instrument underlying the reported data.

observations.metadata_concept: French language used in the snapshot
observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French and the document metadata lists language as "French" with code "fr".
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly covers the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with row and column headers and tabulated values.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field covers tables as a primary visualization form.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is "République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection - Aperçu Semestriel (01 janvier 2024 - 30 juin 2024)".
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrievable URL for the parent document and original PDF
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF relation URL at globalprotectioncluster.org.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema stores the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable document or file URL.

observations.metadata_concept: Publication or posting date of the parent document
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists "date_published": "2025-11-25" and additional fields "posted" and "originally_published" as "25 Nov 2025".
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field represents the data period, not the administrative publication date of the parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Source-document authors or contributing organizations distinct from data source
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors or sources including OCHA, Education Cluster, Save the Children, UNICEF, and UNHCR as a producer with role "Source".
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would risk conflating document attribution with the origin of the represented data, while source_document_title does not capture contributors.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A retrievable URL for the parent source document or original file containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but cannot support direct retrieval or verification through a URL.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, or audit the source document associated with a snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, or official release date of the parent source document, distinct from the data period represented in the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period would misrepresent the concept because it describes the data coverage period rather than the document's administrative publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports source verification, version assessment, citation, and temporal organization of snapshots by document release date.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A person or organization credited as an author, producer, publisher, or contributing source of the parent document when not evidenced as the source of the represented data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is reserved for the origin of the represented data and source_document_title only records the parent document name, leaving document attribution semantically underrepresented.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves attribution, provenance tracking, filtering, and verification of snapshots by the organizations or authors responsible for the source document.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The first table column is labeled "Territoires" and lists named territories such as Beni, Goma, Lubero, Masisi, Nyiragongo, Oïcha, and Rutshuru.
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic_granularity field captures the administrative level of reporting, while row_dimension captures the table-row organization.

observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type field covers counts, and unit_of_measure can capture reported violations or allegations where explicitly described.

observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field covers monitoring as the explicitly stated method or instrument underlying the reported data.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with row and column headers and tabulated values.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field covers tables as a primary visualization form.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is "République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection - Aperçu Semestriel (01 janvier 2024 - 30 juin 2024)".
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.fit_rationale: The schema stores the parent document title but has no field for a retrievable document or file URL.

observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field represents the data period, not the administrative publication date of the parent document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Organizations or persons credited as authors, producers, publishers, or source organizations for the parent document containing the snapshot, distinct from the data_source of the represented data unless explicitly the same.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports citation, provenance review, retrieval, and attribution of snapshots extracted from institutional documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL, persistent link, or authoritative locator for the parent source document or a downloadable version of it.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrievable or verifiable locator.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables users to retrieve, verify, and cite the source document containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The publication, posting, or public availability date of the parent source document, separate from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period describes the data represented in the snapshot and should not be used for document publication or posting dates.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps distinguish data coverage from document release timing and supports citation, versioning, and provenance checks.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A formal identifier assigned to the parent source document in source-document metadata or by the issuing repository.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: internal_identifier is limited to snapshot references within a document, while source_document_title may be non-unique and does not capture repository or document identifiers.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves source-document disambiguation, deduplication, retrieval, and provenance tracking for extracted snapshots.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]

candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves source-document disambiguation, deduplication, retrieval, and provenance tracking for extracted snapshots.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot shows the headings “PROVINCES DE L’ITURI ET DU HAUT UELE (Faradje)” and “Violations et abus des droits en avril 2024,” and the source document title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title and source_document_title fields capture the snapshot heading and parent-document title without material semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The table title refers to “Violations et abus des droits,” and the document metadata lists the theme “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field directly represents the broad humanitarian protection and human-rights domain.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of reported rights violations and abuses
observations.evidence: The table is titled “Violations et abus des droits en avril 2024” and its caption says it presents trends of violations and abuses reported by protection monitoring in Ituri.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_summary and variable_name fields can represent the table’s analytical subject and measured concept.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal period and monthly reporting context
observations.evidence: The snapshot title states “en avril 2024,” and the source document title also ends with “avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The fields time_period and temporal_granularity capture April 2024 and its monthly reporting resolution.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and geographic reporting units
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading names “PROVINCES DE L’ITURI ET DU HAUT UELE (Faradje),” the rows are labeled “Territoires,” and the document metadata references Democratic Republic of the Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing spatial fields capture the represented country, provinces, territory-level units, and their role as reporting locations.

observations.metadata_concept: Categorical organization by territory and violation type
observations.evidence: The table rows list territories such as Aru, Djugu, Faradje, Irumu, Mahagi, and Mambasa, while columns list violation categories such as “Droit à la liberté,” “Droit à la propriété,” “Droit à l’intégrité physique,” “VBG,” and child-rights violations.
observations.fit_rationale: The category, row, and column dimension fields capture the table’s organization by territory and violation type.

observations.metadata_concept: Measurement form as counts and percentages
observations.evidence: The table includes violation-category columns, a “Total” column, and a “%” column.
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent counts and percentages as the forms and units of reported values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid of rows and columns with headers, totals, and percentages.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly captures the snapshot’s primary form as a table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the source-document metadata lists the language as “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the French language evidenced in the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data collection or reporting method
observations.evidence: The caption states that the table presents violations and abuses “signalées par le monitoring de protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field can represent protection monitoring as the explicitly stated method by which the underlying reports were collected.

observations.metadata_concept: Interpretive reference for child-rights violation category
observations.evidence: The column heading “Violations graves des droits de l’enfant” includes the parenthetical reference “(rés. 1612).”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field can capture the explicit reference that qualifies or explains the child-rights violation category.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrievable URL for the parent document and PDF
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb report URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrieval URL or file link.

observations.metadata_concept: Organizations credited as source-document creators or contributors
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors including OCHA, Education Cluster, Save the Children, and UNICEF, and lists UNHCR as a producer with role “Source.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field refers to the origin of represented data, so using it for document authors or publishing-source organizations would conflate document attribution with data provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: Embedded secondary visualization within a tabular snapshot
observations.evidence: The table header area under “Territoires” contains a small locator map alongside the tabular structure.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field captures the primary table form but does not preserve the presence of an embedded map within the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document, landing page, or associated downloadable file for the snapshot can be accessed.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document textually but does not store a retrievable link, and no other v1.1 field captures document access URLs.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, deduplication, and linking back from a snapshot record to its source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization or person explicitly credited with creating, authoring, publishing, or contributing to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the source of the represented data, while the evidenced organizations are credited at the document level and should not be assumed to be the data origin.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, attribution, filtering by producing organization, and verification of institutional source context for snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A secondary visualization type explicitly present within or embedded in a snapshot whose primary visualization type is different.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type records the primary visual encoding but cannot distinguish a table that also includes an embedded map from a plain table.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users and systems identify composite visual artifacts that may require different interpretation, indexing, or extraction handling than single-form snapshots.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot shows the headings “PROVINCES DE L’ITURI ET DU HAUT UELE (Faradje)” and “Violations et abus des droits en avril 2024,” and the source document title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title and source_document_title fields capture the snapshot heading and parent-document title without material semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The table title refers to “Violations et abus des droits,” and the document metadata lists the theme “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field directly represents the broad humanitarian protection and human-rights domain.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of reported rights violations and abuses
observations.evidence: The table is titled “Violations et abus des droits en avril 2024” and its caption says it presents trends of violations and abuses reported by protection monitoring in Ituri.
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_summary and variable_name fields can represent the table’s analytical subject and measured concept.

observations.metadata_concept: Temporal period and monthly reporting context
observations.evidence: The snapshot title states “en avril 2024,” and the source document title also ends with “avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The fields time_period and temporal_granularity capture April 2024 and its monthly reporting resolution.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and geographic reporting units
observations.evidence: The snapshot heading names “PROVINCES DE L’ITURI ET DU HAUT UELE (Faradje),” the rows are labeled “Territoires,” and the document metadata references Democratic Republic of the Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing spatial fields capture the represented country, provinces, territory-level units, and their role as reporting locations.

observations.metadata_concept: Categorical organization by territory and violation type
observations.evidence: The table rows list territories such as Aru, Djugu, Faradje, Irumu, Mahagi, and Mambasa, while columns list violation categories such as “Droit à la liberté,” “Droit à la propriété,” “Droit à l’intégrité physique,” “VBG,” and child-rights violations.
observations.fit_rationale: The category, row, and column dimension fields capture the table’s organization by territory and violation type.

observations.metadata_concept: Measurement form as counts and percentages
observations.evidence: The table includes violation-category columns, a “Total” column, and a “%” column.
observations.fit_rationale: The measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent counts and percentages as the forms and units of reported values.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid of rows and columns with headers, totals, and percentages.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly captures the snapshot’s primary form as a table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the source-document metadata lists the language as “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the French language evidenced in the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Underlying data collection or reporting method
observations.evidence: The caption states that the table presents violations and abuses “signalées par le monitoring de protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field can represent protection monitoring as the explicitly stated method by which the underlying reports were collected.

observations.metadata_concept: Interpretive reference for child-rights violation category
observations.evidence: The column heading “Violations graves des droits de l’enfant” includes the parenthetical reference “(rés. 1612).”
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field can capture the explicit reference that qualifies or explains the child-rights violation category.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrievable URL for the parent document and PDF
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb report URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrieval URL or file link.

observations.metadata_concept: Organizations credited as source-document creators or contributors
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors including OCHA, Education Cluster, Save the Children, and UNICEF, and lists UNHCR as a producer with role “Source.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field refers to the origin of represented data, so using it for document authors or publishing-source organizations would conflate document attribution with data provenance.

observations.metadata_concept: Embedded secondary visualization within a tabular snapshot
observations.evidence: The table header area under “Territoires” contains a small locator map alongside the tabular structure.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field captures the primary table form but does not preserve the presence of an embedded map within the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document, landing page, or associated downloadable file for the snapshot can be accessed.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document textually but does not store a retrievable link, and no other v1.1 field captures document access URLs.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, verification, deduplication, and linking back from a snapshot record to its source document.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization or person explicitly credited with creating, authoring, publishing, or contributing to the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the source of the represented data, while the evidenced organizations are credited at the document level and should not be assumed to be the data origin.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves provenance tracking, attribution, filtering by producing organization, and verification of institutional source context for snapshots.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A secondary visualization type explicitly present within or embedded in a snapshot whose primary visualization type is different.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type records the primary visual encoding but cannot distinguish a table that also includes an embedded map from a plain table.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Helps users and systems identify composite visual artifacts that may require different interpretation, indexing, or extraction handling than single-form snapshots.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title or caption identifying the table
observations.evidence: The snapshot contains the heading “Violations et abus de droits en avril 2024” and the caption “Tableau présentant les tendances de violations et abus des droits signalées par le monitoring de protection dans le Nord Kivu.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field can hold the table heading or caption, and subject_summary can concisely describe the stated analytical purpose.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Protection and human rights subject domain
observations.evidence: The document theme is “Protection and Human Rights,” and the snapshot concerns “violations et abus de droits.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field represents the broad thematic domain evidenced by both the document theme and the table content.

observations.metadata_concept: Data time period and monthly temporal granularity
observations.evidence: The snapshot title states “en avril 2024,” and the source document title also ends with “avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field can record April 2024, and temporal_granularity can record that the represented reporting period is monthly.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and represented geographic entities
observations.evidence: The snapshot header says “PROVINCE DU NORD KIVU,” rows list territories such as Lubero, Masisi, Nyiragongo, Oïcha, Rutshuru, and Goma, and document metadata references the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing spatial fields can capture North Kivu as the scope, the named territories as entities, and the administrative level as territory or province.

observations.metadata_concept: Table organization by territories and rights-violation categories
observations.evidence: The row header is “Territoires,” and column headers include “Droit à la liberté,” “Droit à la propriété,” “Droit à l’intégrité physique,” “VBG,” “Violations graves des droits de l’enfant,” “Total,” and “%.”
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the table’s organizing dimensions and explicit category labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Measured concept and measure types for violations, totals, and percentages
observations.evidence: The table reports counts across rights-violation categories and includes “Total” and “%” columns for each territory.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields can describe rights violations or abuses as the measured concept and counts and percentages as the statistical forms or units.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a visible grid of rows and columns and the supplied artifact type is “table.”
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The caption says the violations and abuses were “signalées par le monitoring de protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field can represent protection monitoring as the explicitly stated method or mechanism underlying the reported data.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the document metadata lists language name “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Explicit normative or classification reference qualifying a measure
observations.evidence: The column label “Violations graves des droits de l’enfant (rés. 1612)” cites “rés. 1612” as part of the measure label.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can preserve the text as a label or note, but they do not separately capture an explicitly cited legal, normative, or classification reference that qualifies the represented measure.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document or associated PDF
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the ReliefWeb URL and a PDF relation URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a field for the parent document title but no field for a source-document access URL needed for retrieval or verification.

observations.metadata_concept: Source-document contributing organizations distinct from represented data source
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors or sources including OCHA, Education Cluster, Save the Children, UNICEF, and producer UNHCR.
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source for these document contributors would conflate parent-document attribution with the dataset, survey, or monitoring source from which the table’s represented data originate.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A legal, policy, methodological, or classification framework explicitly cited in the snapshot as defining, qualifying, or contextualizing a represented measure or category.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: interpretive_note, variable_name, and category_labels can retain the cited wording but do not distinguish the cited framework itself from the measure or category text.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Separately indexing cited frameworks supports interpretation, retrieval, and comparison of snapshots organized by specific legal or classification standards.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its directly associated file can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide an access location for verifying or retrieving the source.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Capturing the source-document URL improves traceability, auditability, and reproducibility of snapshot metadata extraction.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An organization or person explicitly credited with authoring, producing, publishing, or otherwise contributing to the parent source document, when this role is distinct from the represented data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, so using it for document contributors would conflate data provenance with document attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Document contributor metadata supports provenance assessment, institutional filtering, and verification without misidentifying contributors as underlying data sources.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot contains the heading “Violations et abus de droits en avril 2024” and the caption “Tableau présentant les tendances de violations et abus des droits signalées par le monitoring de protection dans le Nord Kivu.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field can hold the table heading or caption, and subject_summary can concisely describe the stated analytical purpose.

observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “République démocratique du Congo | Points Saillants de Protection | avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Protection and human rights subject domain
observations.evidence: The document theme is “Protection and Human Rights,” and the snapshot concerns “violations et abus de droits.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field represents the broad thematic domain evidenced by both the document theme and the table content.

observations.metadata_concept: Data time period and monthly temporal granularity
observations.evidence: The snapshot title states “en avril 2024,” and the source document title also ends with “avril 2024.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field can record April 2024, and temporal_granularity can record that the represented reporting period is monthly.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and represented geographic entities
observations.evidence: The snapshot header says “PROVINCE DU NORD KIVU,” rows list territories such as Lubero, Masisi, Nyiragongo, Oïcha, Rutshuru, and Goma, and document metadata references the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing spatial fields can capture North Kivu as the scope, the named territories as entities, and the administrative level as territory or province.

observations.metadata_concept: Table organization by territories and rights-violation categories
observations.evidence: The row header is “Territoires,” and column headers include “Droit à la liberté,” “Droit à la propriété,” “Droit à l’intégrité physique,” “VBG,” “Violations graves des droits de l’enfant,” “Total,” and “%.”
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, column_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the table’s organizing dimensions and explicit category labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Measured concept and measure types for violations, totals, and percentages
observations.evidence: The table reports counts across rights-violation categories and includes “Total” and “%” columns for each territory.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields can describe rights violations or abuses as the measured concept and counts and percentages as the statistical forms or units.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a visible grid of rows and columns and the supplied artifact type is “table.”
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The caption says the violations and abuses were “signalées par le monitoring de protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The data_collection_method field can represent protection monitoring as the explicitly stated method or mechanism underlying the reported data.

observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in French, and the document metadata lists language name “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly represents the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Explicit normative or classification reference qualifying a measure
observations.evidence: The column label “Violations graves des droits de l’enfant (rés. 1612)” cites “rés. 1612” as part of the measure label.
observations.fit_rationale: Existing fields can preserve the text as a label or note, but they do not separately capture an explicitly cited legal, normative, or classification reference that qualifies the represented measure.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document or associated PDF
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the ReliefWeb URL and a PDF relation URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a field for the parent document title but no field for a source-document access URL needed for retrieval or verification.

observations.metadata_concept: Source-document contributing organizations distinct from represented data source
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors or sources including OCHA, Education Cluster, Save the Children, UNICEF, and producer UNHCR.
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source for these document contributors would conflate parent-document attribution with the dataset, survey, or monitoring source from which the table’s represented data originate.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A legal, policy, methodological, or classification framework explicitly cited in the snapshot as defining, qualifying, or contextualizing a represented measure or category.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: interpretive_note, variable_name, and category_labels can retain the cited wording but do not distinguish the cited framework itself from the measure or category text.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Separately indexing cited frameworks supports interpretation, retrieval, and comparison of snapshots organized by specific legal or classification standards.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its directly associated file can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide an access location for verifying or retrieving the source.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Capturing the source-document URL improves traceability, auditability, and reproducibility of snapshot metadata extraction.

candidate_new_fields.definition: An organization or person explicitly credited with authoring, producing, publishing, or otherwise contributing to the parent source document, when this role is distinct from the represented data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, so using it for document contributors would conflate data provenance with document attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Document contributor metadata supports provenance assessment, institutional filtering, and verification without misidentifying contributors as underlying data sources.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document title contextualizing the snapshot
observations.evidence: The document metadata title is “Mali : Rapport final - Formation sur les questions transversales (Genre, RPA, Protection, VGB et PEAS) pour le group des chargés de communications et de plaidoyer humanitaire de l'Équipe Humanitaire Pays.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title containing the table.

observations.evidence: The table text is in French, including headers such as “PARTICIPANTS,” “ÉVALUATION,” “QUESTIONS,” “FEMMES,” and “HOMMES,” and the document metadata lists language as French.
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document title begins with “Mali : Rapport final” and document metadata lists ref_country as Mali.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields can represent Mali as the explicitly evidenced geographic context.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic domain of training evaluation in gender and protection topics
observations.evidence: The document title refers to training on “questions transversales (Genre, RPA, Protection, VGB et PEAS),” and document themes include “Gender” and “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain and subject_summary fields can capture the broad thematic area and concise analytical subject of the evaluation table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with row and column headings and the supplied artifact type is “table.”
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Evaluation rating scale as organizing dimension
observations.evidence: The table columns under “ÉVALUATION” include ordered labels such as “1: Faible,” “3: Bon,” “4: Très bon,” and “5: Excellent.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension, category_labels, and column_dimension fields can represent the rating scale and its labels without material loss.

observations.evidence: The table has a “QUESTIONS” column containing prompts such as “Quelle est la note globale de la formation” and “Avez-vous trouvé les connaissances acquises utiles.”
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension and category_dimension fields adequately capture that questions organize the table rows.

observations.evidence: The left side of the table has “PARTICIPANTS” columns labeled “FEMMES,” “HOMMES,” and “TOTAL.”
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field can describe participants and category_dimension/category_labels can capture sex-based grouping.

observations.metadata_concept: Measured concepts of participant counts and evaluation responses
observations.evidence: The table reports participant totals by “FEMMES,” “HOMMES,” and “TOTAL” and response counts or percentages across evaluation ratings.
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name, measure_type, and unit_of_measure fields can represent the measured concepts and the use of counts and percentages.

observations.metadata_concept: Graphical emphasis or annotation highlighting high evaluation ratings
observations.evidence: A blue oval is drawn around the “4: Très bon” and “5: Excellent” evaluation columns and their values.
observations.fit_rationale: The interpretive_note field captures textual notes or caveats, but not non-textual callouts or highlighted regions that alter interpretation of the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the source document
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/mali/mali-rapport-final-formation-sur-les-questions-transversales-genre-rpa-protection-vgb-et-peas-pour-le-group-des-charges-de-communications-et-de-plaidoyer-humanitaire-de-lequipe-humanitaire-pays” and a related PDF URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field identifies the parent document by title but does not capture a retrieval or verification link.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A non-textual mark, callout, highlight, or other visual annotation explicitly present in the snapshot that emphasizes or identifies a subset of the displayed information.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: Existing fields describe titles, variables, categories, notes, and visualization type, but none represent an explicit graphical highlight such as the blue oval around selected columns.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Capturing visual annotations supports interpretation, search, and reuse by recording what the source snapshot visually emphasizes without reconstructing the table data.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent link for retrieving or verifying the parent source document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but omits the retrieval link needed to access or verify the source, and data_source is reserved for the origin of represented data rather than the containing document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: A source document URL supports provenance verification, retrieval, deduplication, and auditability of extracted snapshots.
