observations.evidence: The snapshot heading states, “Le tableau ci-dessous indique la répartition des incidents par typologie et par commune.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the displayed heading identifying the table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with rows, columns, headers, and totals, and the supplied artifact type is “table.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The heading says the table shows the distribution of incidents by typology and commune.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary field can concisely describe the table’s purpose without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The source document title refers to “Monitoring de Protection,” and document themes include “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field captures the broad protection and human-rights domain evidenced by the document context.

observations.evidence: The table header uses “Incidents” and the title refers to “répartition des incidents.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures incidents as the primary measured concept.

observations.evidence: Cells contain integer counts of incidents and the table includes row and column totals such as “Total 120.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent that values are counts measured in incidents.

observations.evidence: The heading says incidents are distributed “par typologie et par commune,” with commune rows and incident-type columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension, row_dimension, and column_dimension fields represent the two organizing dimensions of commune and incident typology.

observations.evidence: Rows include commune names such as “Chétimari,” “Bosso,” and “Diffa,” while columns include incident labels such as “Enlèvements,” “Homicides,” and “Violences psychologiques.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_labels and geographic_entities fields can store the explicit row and column labels.

observations.evidence: Column headers group incident subtypes under parent categories such as “Violation du droit à la liberté,” “Violation du droit à la vie et à l’intégrité,” and “Violences sexuelles.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing category fields can list dimensions and labels but do not preserve the parent-child grouping between violation categories and incident subtypes.

observations.evidence: The document title names “Région de Diffa,” document metadata lists ref_country “Niger,” and table rows are communes including Diffa, Bosso, and Mainé-soroa.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing spatial fields capture Niger and Diffa as the geographic scope and communes as the represented granularity/location type.

observations.metadata_concept: Time period represented by the snapshot context
observations.evidence: The source document title states “Région de Diffa, octobre 2022.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields can represent October 2022 and the monthly context explicitly stated in the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The table text is in French and document metadata lists language “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language evidenced in both the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.evidence: Document metadata gives the title “République du Niger : Rapport mensuel de Monitoring de Protection | Région de Diffa, octobre 2022.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The parent document title describes the report as “Rapport mensuel de Monitoring de Protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_collection_method field can represent Protection Monitoring as the explicitly named monitoring method contextualizing the table.

observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/niger/republique-du-niger-rapport-mensuel-de-monitoring-de-protection-region-de-diffa-octobre-2022” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing v1.1 field captures a source-document URL needed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot’s parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creator or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: Document metadata lists authors including “UNHCR,” “ACF,” “ACTED,” and “DRC,” and additional UNHCR sources include the same organizations.
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document creators or listed source organizations with the dataset or cited source from which the represented data originate.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly displayed parent-child or grouped structure among category labels within a snapshot, such as top-level category groups and their subordinate labels.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension, category_labels, and column_dimension can record dimensions and labels but cannot preserve the visible hierarchy linking incident subtypes to broader violation categories.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Preserving category hierarchy improves interpretation, search, and downstream reuse of tables or charts with grouped headers or nested classifications.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its directly associated file can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide an access location, and no existing field stores document retrieval links.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: A source-document URL enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the original context of the extracted snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, person, or institutional contributor explicitly identified as an author, producer, or creator of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, so using it for document authors or source organizations would conflate data provenance with document creation provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Recording source-document creators supports provenance tracking, credibility assessment, document discovery, and verification without asserting that the creators are the underlying data source.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading states, “Le tableau ci-dessous indique la répartition des incidents par typologie et par commune.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the displayed heading identifying the table.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with rows, columns, headers, and totals, and the supplied artifact type is “table.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The heading says the table shows the distribution of incidents by typology and commune.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_summary field can concisely describe the table’s purpose without semantic loss.

observations.evidence: The source document title refers to “Monitoring de Protection,” and document themes include “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain field captures the broad protection and human-rights domain evidenced by the document context.

observations.evidence: The table header uses “Incidents” and the title refers to “répartition des incidents.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name field captures incidents as the primary measured concept.

observations.evidence: Cells contain integer counts of incidents and the table includes row and column totals such as “Total 120.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measure_type and unit_of_measure fields can represent that values are counts measured in incidents.

observations.evidence: The heading says incidents are distributed “par typologie et par commune,” with commune rows and incident-type columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension, row_dimension, and column_dimension fields represent the two organizing dimensions of commune and incident typology.

observations.evidence: Rows include commune names such as “Chétimari,” “Bosso,” and “Diffa,” while columns include incident labels such as “Enlèvements,” “Homicides,” and “Violences psychologiques.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_labels and geographic_entities fields can store the explicit row and column labels.

observations.evidence: Column headers group incident subtypes under parent categories such as “Violation du droit à la liberté,” “Violation du droit à la vie et à l’intégrité,” and “Violences sexuelles.”
observations.fit_rationale: Existing category fields can list dimensions and labels but do not preserve the parent-child grouping between violation categories and incident subtypes.

observations.evidence: The document title names “Région de Diffa,” document metadata lists ref_country “Niger,” and table rows are communes including Diffa, Bosso, and Mainé-soroa.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing spatial fields capture Niger and Diffa as the geographic scope and communes as the represented granularity/location type.

observations.metadata_concept: Time period represented by the snapshot context
observations.evidence: The source document title states “Région de Diffa, octobre 2022.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields can represent October 2022 and the monthly context explicitly stated in the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The table text is in French and document metadata lists language “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language evidenced in both the snapshot and document metadata.

observations.evidence: Document metadata gives the title “République du Niger : Rapport mensuel de Monitoring de Protection | Région de Diffa, octobre 2022.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the parent document title.

observations.evidence: The parent document title describes the report as “Rapport mensuel de Monitoring de Protection.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing data_collection_method field can represent Protection Monitoring as the explicitly named monitoring method contextualizing the table.

observations.evidence: Document metadata provides the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/niger/republique-du-niger-rapport-mensuel-de-monitoring-de-protection-region-de-diffa-octobre-2022” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing v1.1 field captures a source-document URL needed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot’s parent document.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document creator or contributing organizations
observations.evidence: Document metadata lists authors including “UNHCR,” “ACF,” “ACTED,” and “DRC,” and additional UNHCR sources include the same organizations.
observations.fit_rationale: Using data_source would conflate document creators or listed source organizations with the dataset or cited source from which the represented data originate.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The explicitly displayed parent-child or grouped structure among category labels within a snapshot, such as top-level category groups and their subordinate labels.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_dimension, category_labels, and column_dimension can record dimensions and labels but cannot preserve the visible hierarchy linking incident subtypes to broader violation categories.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Preserving category hierarchy improves interpretation, search, and downstream reuse of tables or charts with grouped headers or nested classifications.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its directly associated file can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide an access location, and no existing field stores document retrieval links.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: A source-document URL enables users and systems to retrieve, verify, cite, and audit the original context of the extracted snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The organization, person, or institutional contributor explicitly identified as an author, producer, or creator of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source is defined as the origin of the represented data, so using it for document authors or source organizations would conflate data provenance with document creation provenance.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Recording source-document creators supports provenance tracking, credibility assessment, document discovery, and verification without asserting that the creators are the underlying data source.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Forcibly displaced and returned persons in southern Africa, Data as of 30 April 2023*.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading that identifies the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Population Data Analysis - Regional Bureau for Southern Africa, April 2023.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table labels and notes are in English, and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a tabular artifact with column headers such as “Country of Asylum,” “Location,” “Population Group,” and “Total.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic domain of forced displacement population data
observations.evidence: The title refers to “Forcibly displaced and returned persons,” and document themes include “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields can capture the broad theme and analytical subject of displaced and returned populations.

observations.evidence: The table has a “Population Group” header with categories including “Refugee,” “Asylum-Seeker,” “Other of Concern,” “IDP by Conflict,” “Returned IDP,” “Refugee Returnee,” “Statelessness,” and “Host Community.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing population_group, category_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the affected population categories used in the table.

observations.evidence: The table reports counts of population groups and a “Total” column for persons by country and location.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name, unit_of_measure, and measure_type fields can represent population counts measured in persons.

observations.evidence: The title states “Data as of 30 April 2023,” with a note that “The number of IDPs in DRC is as of 31 March 2023.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field can capture the represented data date, while interpretive_note can preserve the stated exception for DRC IDPs.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and named geographic entities
observations.evidence: The title says “southern Africa,” and table row groups include countries such as Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mozambique, South Africa, Congo, Zambia, Angola, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Eswatini, Botswana, Lesotho, Madagascar, Comoros, and Mauritius.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the regional scope and named countries represented in the table.

observations.evidence: The first column header is “Country of Asylum.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_role field directly captures the semantic role played by the countries.

observations.evidence: The table reports rows under “Location” with subheaders “Name,” “Longitude (X),” and “Latitude (Y),” and includes location labels such as “IDP Camp,” “Maratane Camp,” “Lovua Settlement,” and “Other.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_granularity, location_type, geographic_entities, and category_dimension fields can represent location-level organization and explicitly named location types.

observations.evidence: The Location header includes “Longitude (X)” and “Latitude (Y)” columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and column_dimension fields can describe longitude and latitude as table dimensions without extracting the numerical coordinate values.

observations.evidence: The table includes a “Self-settled***” column with values such as Yes and No, and the note explains that self-settled refers to individuals without available information such as names and locations whose locations are categorized as unknown.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields can represent the self-settled classification, and interpretive_note can capture its explicit definition.

observations.evidence: The footer notes that DRC IDP counts are as of 31 March 2023, IDPs by disaster are not included, and some location figures could differ from operation reports due to inconsistency in proGres v4.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field is designed for explanatory notes, caveats, assumptions, footnotes, and methodological remarks provided within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/population-data-analysis-regional-bureau-southern-africa-april-2023” and a PDF attachment URL in relations.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not represent a retrievable source-document URL for verification or access.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its source landing page can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title captures only the parent document name, and data_source concerns the origin of represented data rather than the access location of the containing document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, provenance verification, and auditability of snapshots by linking metadata records back to the source document or attachment.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Forcibly displaced and returned persons in southern Africa, Data as of 30 April 2023*.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading that identifies the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Population Data Analysis - Regional Bureau for Southern Africa, April 2023.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The table labels and notes are in English, and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a tabular artifact with column headers such as “Country of Asylum,” “Location,” “Population Group,” and “Total.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field can represent the artifact as a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Thematic domain of forced displacement population data
observations.evidence: The title refers to “Forcibly displaced and returned persons,” and document themes include “Protection and Human Rights.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing subject_domain and subject_summary fields can capture the broad theme and analytical subject of displaced and returned populations.

observations.evidence: The table has a “Population Group” header with categories including “Refugee,” “Asylum-Seeker,” “Other of Concern,” “IDP by Conflict,” “Returned IDP,” “Refugee Returnee,” “Statelessness,” and “Host Community.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing population_group, category_dimension, and category_labels fields can represent the affected population categories used in the table.

observations.evidence: The table reports counts of population groups and a “Total” column for persons by country and location.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing variable_name, unit_of_measure, and measure_type fields can represent population counts measured in persons.

observations.evidence: The title states “Data as of 30 April 2023,” with a note that “The number of IDPs in DRC is as of 31 March 2023.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field can capture the represented data date, while interpretive_note can preserve the stated exception for DRC IDPs.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic scope and named geographic entities
observations.evidence: The title says “southern Africa,” and table row groups include countries such as Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mozambique, South Africa, Congo, Zambia, Angola, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Eswatini, Botswana, Lesotho, Madagascar, Comoros, and Mauritius.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_scope and geographic_entities fields capture the regional scope and named countries represented in the table.

observations.evidence: The first column header is “Country of Asylum.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_role field directly captures the semantic role played by the countries.

observations.evidence: The table reports rows under “Location” with subheaders “Name,” “Longitude (X),” and “Latitude (Y),” and includes location labels such as “IDP Camp,” “Maratane Camp,” “Lovua Settlement,” and “Other.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic_granularity, location_type, geographic_entities, and category_dimension fields can represent location-level organization and explicitly named location types.

observations.evidence: The Location header includes “Longitude (X)” and “Latitude (Y)” columns.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and column_dimension fields can describe longitude and latitude as table dimensions without extracting the numerical coordinate values.

observations.evidence: The table includes a “Self-settled***” column with values such as Yes and No, and the note explains that self-settled refers to individuals without available information such as names and locations whose locations are categorized as unknown.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing category_dimension and category_labels fields can represent the self-settled classification, and interpretive_note can capture its explicit definition.

observations.evidence: The footer notes that DRC IDP counts are as of 31 March 2023, IDPs by disaster are not included, and some location figures could differ from operation reports due to inconsistency in proGres v4.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field is designed for explanatory notes, caveats, assumptions, footnotes, and methodological remarks provided within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata includes the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/population-data-analysis-regional-bureau-southern-africa-april-2023” and a PDF attachment URL in relations.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not represent a retrievable source-document URL for verification or access.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL where the parent source document or its source landing page can be accessed for retrieval or verification of the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title captures only the parent document name, and data_source concerns the origin of represented data rather than the access location of the containing document.

observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field describes the represented data period, so using it for the parent document publication date would conflate different temporal concepts.

observations.fit_rationale: The schema has fields for the snapshot visualization type and document title but no field for the genre or format of the parent document.

observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field refers to the origin of the represented data, while this evidence concerns attribution for the parent document or metadata source.

candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document by name but does not provide a retrieval or verification link.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval, citation checking, provenance verification, and re-access to the source document containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Publication, posting, or release date of the parent document, distinct from the time period represented by the snapshot data.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and would distort semantics if used for a document publication date.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports document versioning, provenance review, chronological organization, and distinction between data period and source release timing.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Genre, format, or document class of the parent source document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: visualization_type describes the snapshot artifact, and source_document_title does not encode the parent document genre or format.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports filtering and retrieval by institutional document class, such as situation reports, assessments, or briefs.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Organization or person credited with authoring, producing, publishing, or supplying the parent document, distinct from the cited data source for the represented values.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source concerns the source of the represented data and would conflate data provenance with parent-document attribution.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance tracking, verification of institutional authorship, and discovery by issuing or supplying organization.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with row labels and month columns, presenting values in a tabular layout.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly captures that the snapshot is a table.

observations.evidence: The column headers explicitly state MAY 2023 and JUNE 2023.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields capture both the represented months and the monthly temporal organization of the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Financial and assistance measures represented in the rows
observations.evidence: Row labels include Sayrafa USD Transactions, UNHCR & WFP Assistance, UNHCR & WFP Share, Overall Cash Assistance, and Overall Share.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can represent the financial measures and row-based indicator labels without material loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Units, currency, and statistical form of reported values
observations.evidence: The table displays dollar-denominated amounts with $ symbols and share values with percent signs.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing measurement fields cover USD currency, monetary units, and percentage or share-style measures.

observations.metadata_concept: Named organizations represented as actors in the measured assistance
observations.evidence: The snapshot row labels explicitly refer to UNHCR & WFP Assistance and UNHCR & WFP Share.
observations.fit_rationale: Category labels preserve the text but do not separately capture represented organizations, while financing_source and data_source would imply funding or data-origin roles not explicitly evidenced.

observations.metadata_concept: Interpretive footnote attached to the table
observations.evidence: The footnote states, '*including safety net assistance through the ESSN and NPTP'.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing interpretive_note field directly captures explanatory notes and caveats provided within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is 'Joint Report on Dual Currency Disbursement, July 2023'.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly represents the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Language used in the snapshot and source context
observations.evidence: The snapshot text is in English and the document metadata lists language as English.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Document-level retrieval URL for the source containing the snapshot
observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL 'https://reliefweb.int/report/lebanon/joint-report-dual-currency-disbursement-july-2023' and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema identifies the parent document by title but has no field for a retrieval or verification URL for that document.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists the document type and UNHCR format as 'Situation Report'.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has no field for the genre or document type of the parent source, and subject_domain would describe topic rather than publication form.

observations.metadata_concept: Source document publication date distinct from represented data period
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published as 2025-11-13 and additional.unhcr_originally_published as 13 Nov 2025.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing time_period field describes the period represented by the snapshot data and should not be used for the parent document's publication date.

observations.metadata_concept: Organizations credited as authors or sources of the parent document
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors OCHA, UN High Commissioner for Refugees, and World Food Programme, and producers include UNHCR with role Source.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields do not capture parent-document authorship or credited institutional source without implying data origin or financing roles.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Named organization or institutional actor explicitly represented as a subject, actor, comparator, or participant in the snapshot, excluding organizations identified only as data sources, funders, authors, or publishers unless that represented role is explicit.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: category_labels can retain the row text but does not normalize organization names, while financing_source and data_source encode specific roles that are not explicitly evidenced by the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports retrieval and analysis of snapshots involving specific organizations as represented actors without conflating them with data provenance or funding roles.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web link for retrieving or verifying the parent document that contains the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: source_document_title identifies the parent document but does not provide a retrievable link, and data_source is reserved for the source of the represented data rather than the document location.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables verification, citation, retrieval, and deduplication of snapshots through their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The genre, format, or publication type of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: No existing field captures the parent document's publication form, and subject_domain describes thematic content rather than document genre.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves organization and retrieval of snapshots by source publication type, such as situation report, annual report, or policy brief.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The date on which the parent document containing the snapshot was published, posted, or otherwise made publicly available, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and cannot safely represent the publication date of the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance verification, citation, version awareness, and separation of data-period metadata from publication timing.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Person or organization explicitly credited as an author, creator, or institutional source of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source captures the origin of represented data and financing_source captures funding support, neither of which is equivalent to parent-document authorship or credited source organization.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports attribution, verification, and retrieval of snapshots by the institutions or authors responsible for the containing document.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves organization and retrieval of snapshots by source publication type, such as situation report, annual report, or policy brief.

candidate_new_fields.definition: The date on which the parent document containing the snapshot was published, posted, or otherwise made publicly available, when explicitly provided.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: time_period is defined as the period represented by the data and cannot safely represent the publication date of the parent document.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance verification, citation, version awareness, and separation of data-period metadata from publication timing.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Person or organization explicitly credited as an author, creator, or institutional source of the parent document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source captures the origin of represented data and financing_source captures funding support, neither of which is equivalent to parent-document authorship or credited source organization.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports attribution, verification, and retrieval of snapshots by the institutions or authors responsible for the containing document.

observations.metadata_concept: Snapshot title identifying the table subject
observations.evidence: The table heading reads “Stratégies de survie durant les 7 derniers jours précédant l’enquête.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the primary heading that identifies the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with row labels for strategies and columns for PDM and mVAM values.
observations.fit_rationale: The visualization_type field directly represents that the artifact is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: French language used in the snapshot
observations.evidence: The table text is in French, and the document metadata lists the language as “French” with code “fr.”
observations.fit_rationale: The language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The rows describe food-consumption coping strategies, and the document metadata theme is “Food and Nutrition.”
observations.fit_rationale: The subject_domain field captures the broad thematic domain represented by the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Primary measured concepts: household use of coping strategies and reduced coping strategy index
observations.evidence: The column heading states “Ménages ayant eu recours aux stratégies (%)” and the final row states “Indice réduit des stratégies de survie (moyenne).”
observations.fit_rationale: The variable_name field captures the indicators or measured concepts represented in the table.

observations.metadata_concept: Food coping strategy as the organizing row dimension
observations.evidence: The left column is headed “Stratégies” and lists specific strategies such as consuming less preferred foods and reducing the number of meals.
observations.fit_rationale: The row_dimension, category_dimension, and category_labels fields capture the conceptual row grouping and its explicit labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Households as the population described by the measurements
observations.evidence: The table heading says “Ménages ayant eu recours aux stratégies (%).”
observations.fit_rationale: The population_group field captures the human population that the data are about.

observations.evidence: The table reports percentages under “Ménages ayant eu recours aux stratégies (%)” and a final row labeled “moyenne.”
observations.fit_rationale: The unit_of_measure field captures percent and the measure_type field captures percentage and average forms.

observations.evidence: The title refers to “les 7 derniers jours précédant l’enquête,” while the column headers state “déc. 2014” and “janv. 2015.”
observations.fit_rationale: The time_period field can represent the relative seven-day reference period and dated survey rounds, while temporal_granularity can represent the monthly reporting labels.

observations.metadata_concept: Comparison between PDM and mVAM survey rounds
observations.evidence: The table presents separate columns for “PDM (déc. 2014)” and “mVAM (janv. 2015).”
observations.fit_rationale: The column and category fields capture the survey-round organization, and comparison_group captures the explicit side-by-side comparison.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic and location context of the Abala refugee camp in Niger
observations.evidence: The source document title states “Niger - Démarrage du projet pilote mVAM dans le camp de réfugiés d'Abala.”
observations.fit_rationale: The geographic and location fields capture Niger, Abala, and the refugee-camp location type when document context explicitly describes the snapshot setting.

observations.metadata_concept: Parent document title for provenance and identification
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Niger - Démarrage du projet pilote mVAM dans le camp de réfugiés d'Abala: Numéro 1, Janvier 2015.”
observations.fit_rationale: The source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The document metadata lists authors including UNICEF, Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development, UN High Commissioner for Refugees, and World Food Programme.
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field is for the origin of represented data, so using it for document authors or ReliefWeb source organizations would conflate data provenance with source-document attribution.

observations.evidence: The document metadata includes the URL “https://reliefweb.int/report/niger/niger-d-marrage-du-projet-pilote-mvam-dans-le-camp-de-r-fugi-s-dabala-num-ro-1-janvier” and a PDF attachment URL.
observations.fit_rationale: No existing field captures a retrieval locator for the parent document, even though it supports verification and access to the snapshot context.

observations.metadata_concept: Named humanitarian crisis or disaster context
observations.evidence: The document metadata lists “Sahel Crisis: 2011-2017” under disasters and “Drought” under disaster types.
observations.fit_rationale: subject_domain can capture a broad theme but not a named crisis or disaster context that situates the snapshot analytically.

candidate_new_fields.definition: Organizations or persons credited as authors, publishers, producers, or source organizations of the parent document containing the snapshot, when explicitly provided and distinct from the data source.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: data_source describes the origin of the represented data, while the cited organizations are document-level authors or source organizations and should not be treated as data origins without explicit evidence.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Supports provenance tracking, verification, citation, and retrieval of snapshots by responsible source-document organizations without conflating them with data sources.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for the parent document or its downloadable file containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: The schema includes source_document_title but has no field for a URL or locator that enables direct access to the document containing the snapshot.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Enables retrieval, audit, verification, and re-linking of snapshots to their source documents.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A named crisis, disaster, emergency, or other contextual event explicitly associated with the snapshot or its parent document.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: subject_domain captures broad thematic areas but does not preserve named event or crisis context such as a specific drought or humanitarian crisis.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves search, grouping, and interpretation of snapshots tied to emergencies, disasters, or other named events across documents and organizations.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

candidate_new_fields.definition: A URL or persistent web locator for the parent document or its downloadable file containing the snapshot.

candidate_new_fields.definition: A named crisis, disaster, emergency, or other contextual event explicitly associated with the snapshot or its parent document.
candidate_new_fields.why_existing_fields_are_insufficient: subject_domain captures broad thematic areas but does not preserve named event or crisis context such as a specific drought or humanitarian crisis.
candidate_new_fields.operational_value: Improves search, grouping, and interpretation of snapshots tied to emergencies, disasters, or other named events across documents and organizations.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

CandidateField.description:
Propose an evidence-backed field for later human adjudication.

Attributes
----------
proposed_name : str
    Reusable candidate field name in snake_case.
definition : str
    Proposed definition of the candidate field.
supporting_observation_ids : list[str]
    Observation identifiers supporting the proposal.
why_existing_fields_are_insufficient : str
    Explanation of the material gap in the existing schema.
operational_value : str
    Value of the field for describing and using data snapshots.
source_level : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Level at which evidence for the field is available.
CandidateField.title: CandidateField

ValidationObservation.description:
Describe one metadata concept and its fit with the frozen schema.

Attributes
----------
observation_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
metadata_concept : str
    Reusable metadata concept evidenced by the inputs.
evidence : str
    Concise explicit evidence supporting the observation.
evidence_source : Literal["snapshot", "document", "both"]
    Input source containing the cited evidence.
closest_schema_fields : list[str]
    Exact v1.1 field names that most closely represent the concept.
fit_status : Literal["covered", "weak_fit", "no_fit", "out_of_scope", "uncertain"]
    Coverage classification for the observation.
fit_rationale : str
    Explanation of the assigned coverage classification.
ValidationObservation.title: ValidationObservation

schema_.description:
Structured validation assessment for one held-out snapshot.

Attributes
----------
observations : list[ValidationObservation]
    Metadata observations evaluated against the frozen schema.
candidate_new_fields : list[CandidateField]
    Evidence-backed field proposals requiring human adjudication.

observations.evidence: The snapshot heading reads “Evolution des prix de quelques produits de grande consommation à Komanda.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing title field directly captures the heading that identifies the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The snapshot is a grid with column headers including “Désignation,” “Unité,” “Prix avant la crise,” “Prix pendant la crise,” and “Ecarts.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing visualization_type field directly represents that the snapshot is a table.

observations.metadata_concept: Analytical subject of consumer product price changes
observations.evidence: The title states price evolution for selected mass-consumption products, and the rows list products such as Maïs, Haricot, Riz, and Charbon de bois.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing fields can capture the subject summary, the measured concept of price, and the product category labels without semantic loss.

observations.metadata_concept: Commodity or package unit used to interpret each reported price
observations.evidence: The table includes an “Unité” column with entries such as Bassin, Seau, 1 kg, Sac, Barre, Boite, and Régime.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing unit_of_measure field broadly covers units used to interpret reported quantitative values, including the per-product units for the prices.

observations.metadata_concept: Crisis-phase comparison between before and during periods
observations.evidence: Column headers explicitly compare “Prix avant la crise (Janvier 2022)” with “Prix pendant la crise (24 avril 2022).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing comparison_group field explicitly includes before-versus-after style comparative relationships and can capture before versus during the crisis.

observations.metadata_concept: Dates represented by the compared price columns
observations.evidence: The price columns specify “Janvier 2022” and “24 avril 2022.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing temporal fields can represent the explicitly stated month and specific date associated with the reported prices.

observations.metadata_concept: Geographic location represented by the table
observations.evidence: The snapshot title names “Komanda,” and the source document title names “Nord Kivu - Ituri, République Démocratique du Congo.”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing geographic fields can represent the named locality and broader geographic context evidenced by the snapshot and parent document.

observations.evidence: The table text is in French, with phrases such as “Evolution des prix,” “Désignation,” and “Prix avant la crise,” and the document metadata lists French.
observations.fit_rationale: The existing language field directly captures the language used within the snapshot.

observations.evidence: The source-document metadata title is “Zone Frontalière Nord Kivu - Ituri, République Démocratique du Congo : Protection Analysis Update (Juin 2022).”
observations.fit_rationale: The existing source_document_title field directly captures the title of the parent document containing the snapshot.

observations.metadata_concept: Retrieval URL for the parent source document
observations.evidence: The document metadata provides a ReliefWeb URL and a PDF attachment URL for the source document.
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has a field for the source document title but no field for a retrievable source document URL needed for verification or access.

observations.metadata_concept: Publication date of the parent source document
observations.evidence: The source-document metadata lists date_published as “2025-04-09” and additional.unhcr_posted as “9 Apr 2025.”
observations.fit_rationale: The schema has temporal fields for represented data periods but no field for the publication date of the parent document as provenance metadata.

observations.metadata_concept: Organizations credited as source-document authors or sources
observations.evidence: The document metadata authors list UNICEF, Health Cluster, and WHO, and additional.unhcr_sources lists the same organizations.
observations.fit_rationale: The data_source field refers to the origin of represented data, so using it for document authors or source organizations would conflate document attribution with data provenance.
